1. **[Bug] 客户端异常**: This issue was discussed and resolved in a [GitHub discussion](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1176) and a [closed issue](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1175) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1176)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1175)</sup>.
2. **[Bug] 集成ollama调用llava多模态模型时无法识别图片**: This issue was resolved by a pull request that enabled vision support for the LLaVA models. The specific changes can be seen in [this pull request](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/pull/1791) <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1482)</sup>.

For the 4turbo model, there are specific configurations required to handle image inputs correctly. You need to enable the "Support Visual Recognition" setting in the model configuration:

```json
"vision": {
  "extra": "This configuration will only enable image upload capabilities within the application. Whether recognition is supported depends entirely on the model itself; please test the model's visual recognition capabilities on your own.",
  "title": "Support Visual Recognition"
}
```

Additionally, the GPT-4 Turbo model supports visual capabilities, allowing visual requests to be made using JSON format and function calls <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/en-US/setting.json)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/en-US/models.json)</sup>.

If you encounter errors during image processing, the code includes error handling mechanisms to catch and log errors, returning a structured error response. This ensures that any issues are properly reported and handled <sup>[[6]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/api/text-to-image/[provider]/route.ts)</sup><sup>[[7]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/ai360/index.test.ts)</sup>.

Please check your configuration settings and ensure that the "Support Visual Recognition" feature is enabled. If the issue persists, reviewing the error logs might provide more insights into the problem.

Regarding the 504 Gateway Timeout error, common causes include server overload, network issues, upstream server issues, and configuration errors. Here are some troubleshooting steps you can follow:

1. **Retry the Request**: Sometimes, the issue is temporary. Retry the request after some time.
2. **Check Server Load**: Ensure that the server is not overloaded and has sufficient resources.
3. **Network Diagnostics**: Check for any network issues that might be causing delays.
4. **Upstream Server Health**: Verify that the upstream server is operational and responding in a timely manner.
5. **Configuration Review**: Review the server and gateway configurations to ensure they are correct <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/fr-FR/error.json)</sup>.

Additionally, setting a high token limit like 32000 can lead to performance issues, increased processing time, and higher costs. For the 'o1' model, the framework includes specific error handling mechanisms such as handling invalid API keys, business errors, and location not supported errors. The discussion titled [连接性检查，无相应](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1237) mentions that updating to the latest version (124.2) resolved the issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1237)</sup>.

Regarding the 504 Gateway Timeout error, common causes include server overload, network issues, upstream server issues, and configuration errors. Here are some troubleshooting steps you can follow:

1. **Retry the Request**: Sometimes, the issue is temporary. Retry the request after some time.
2. **Check Server Load**: Ensure that the server is not overloaded and has sufficient resources.
3. **Network Diagnostics**: Check for any network issues that might be causing delays.
4. **Upstream Server Health**: Verify that the upstream server is operational and responding in a timely manner.
5. **Configuration Review**: Review the server and gateway configurations to ensure they are correct <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/fr-FR/error.json)</sup>.

Additionally, setting a high token limit like 32000 can lead to performance issues, increased processing time, and higher costs. It is recommended to set a more reasonable token limit to avoid these issues <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/minimax/index.ts)</sup>.

For the 'o1' model, the framework includes specific error handling mechanisms such as handling invalid API keys, business errors, and location not supported errors. These mechanisms ensure robust error handling and provide meaningful feedback <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/anthropic/index.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[6]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/anthropic/index.ts)</sup>.

If you have already tried these steps and the issue persists, consider updating to the latest version of the framework as suggested in the similar discussion.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering where markdown table content inside `.md` files is not available in the knowledge base and cannot be known by the AI might be due to a limitation or bug in the current implementation.

There is existing functionality for extracting and indexing table content from markdown files. The system can parse and extract table content, including its representation in HTML, as demonstrated in the provided JSON content <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/unstructured/__tests__/fixtures/table-parse/auto-partition-basic-raw.json)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/unstructured/__tests__/fixtures/table-parse/fast-partition-basic-output.json)</sup>. However, it seems that this functionality might not be working as expected in your case.

To address this issue, you might want to check the following:

1. **Ensure Proper Parsing**: Verify that the markdown file is being parsed correctly and that the table content is being extracted and indexed. You can check the logs or the indexed data to confirm this.

2. **Check for Known Issues**: There is a known issue documented regarding the handling of markdown files in the knowledge base, which might be related to your problem <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup>.

3. **Review the Codebase**: The part of the codebase responsible for parsing and indexing uploaded files involves components like PostgreSQL, PGVector, S3-compatible Object Storage, OpenAI Embedding, and optionally Unstructured.io. Specifically, the `src/store/file/slices/chat/action.ts` file contains the logic for handling file uploads and processing <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/knowledge-base.mdx)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/chat/action.ts)</sup>.

If the issue persists, it might be necessary to further investigate the specific implementation details or consider reporting this as a bug for further assistance from the development team.

I found some similar issues and discussions that might be relevant to the problem you're experiencing with Claude 3 on AWS Bedrock:

1. **Closed Issue**: [[Bug] claude3-opus回答存在显示错误](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2733)
   - This issue was resolved by a pull request that fixed and improved the tool calling mechanism <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2733)</sup>.

2. **Closed Issue**: [[Bug] 通过AWS的Bedrock的claude3或者claude 3.5，无法分析图片](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3116)
   - This issue was related to a failure in base64 encoding with Anthropic 3.5 and was closed as a duplicate of issue #3001 <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3116)</sup>.

3. **Unsolved Discussion**: [我在服务器用docker部署后遇到了问题](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3107)
   - This discussion involves issues encountered when deploying with Docker <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3107)</sup>.

For the specific problem of the 'think' interface and loading issues, the `LobeThinking` component is responsible for rendering this interface. The relevant CSS and frontend components include styles for the container and title, as well as components like `Flexbox`, `Icon`, and various icons from the `lucide-react` library <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/components/MarkdownElements/LobeThinking/Render.tsx)</sup>.

Additionally, error handling for API calls to AWS Bedrock is managed by catching exceptions and throwing a custom `AgentRuntimeError` with detailed error information <sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/bedrock/index.ts)</sup>.

You might want to check if the issue persists after ensuring that the tool calling mechanism is correctly implemented, as per the changes made in the pull request that resolved similar display errors <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2733)</sup>.

I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem: [[Bug] Failed to deploy on Zeabur](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/710). The solution involved manually forking the repository, creating a project, and adding a new service on Zeabur. Additionally, syncing and enabling the sync workflow resolved the issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/710)</sup>.

The problem you're encountering with the "Module Not Found" error for `/app/docker.cjs` and the process exiting with code 1 is likely due to the `zbpack.json` configuration file specifying `"ignore_dockerfile": true` and `"serverless": true`. This configuration indicates that the deployment is intended to be serverless and not containerized, which may lead to issues with module resolution and dependencies expected in a Docker environment.

To resolve this, ensure that the necessary modules and dependencies are correctly configured for a serverless environment, or consider deploying using Docker if serverless deployment is not a strict requirement. Additionally, be aware of existing issues with Zeabur's support for Next.js middleware and rewrites, as noted in the [LobeChat deployment documentation](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/pull/2775?notification_referrer_id=NT_kwDOAdi2DrQxMDkyODQ4MDc2NTozMDk3OTU5OA#issuecomment-2146713899) <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/zeabur.mdx)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/zeabur.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @kylyzhh! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash those bugs together! 🤖

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem: [[Bug] 非 gpt-4-vision-preview 模型传图格式](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1245). The suggested solution was to ensure that the image URL is correctly parsed and converted to a base64 format. This involves using utility functions like `parseDataUri` and `imageUrlToBase64` to handle the image data properly.

Here is a code snippet that demonstrates how to handle image URLs:

```ts
case 'image_url': {
  const { mimeType, base64, type } = parseDataUri(content.image_url.url);

  if (type === 'base64')
    return {
      source: {
        data: base64 as string,
        media_type: mimeType as Anthropic.ImageBlockParam.Source['media_type'],
        type: 'base64',
      },
      type: 'image',
    };

  if (type === 'url') {
    const { base64, mimeType } = await imageUrlToBase64(content.image_url.url);
    return {
      source: {
        data: base64 as string,
        media_type: mimeType as Anthropic.ImageBlockParam.Source['media_type'],
        type: 'base64',
      },
      type: 'image',
    };
  }

  throw new Error(`Invalid image URL: ${content.image_url.url}`);
}
```

Ensure that the `imageUrlToBase64` function correctly converts the image URL to a base64 string and that the `parseDataUri` function correctly parses the data URI. If the image URL is not valid or cannot be converted, the function will throw an error <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/anthropicHelpers.ts)</sup>.

Additionally, the specific requirements and limitations for image formats and sizes when using the OpenAI API are as follows:

1. **Number of Images**: Must be between 1 and 10.
2. **Prompt Length**: Maximum length of 1000 characters.
3. **Image Quality**: For DALL-E 3, the quality can be specified as 'hd'.
4. **Image Sizes**: Must be one of the following:
   - 1792x1024
   - 1024x1024
   - 1024x1792
5. **Image Style**: For DALL-E 3, the style can be 'vivid' or 'natural' (default is 'vivid') <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/types/openai/image.ts)</sup>.

Make sure your images comply with these requirements to avoid the "invalid_image" error.

body: > > > 你的图片链接是啥样的 > > > > > > > > 我也有无法使用图片进行聊天的问题，只不过经过分析，我遇到的问题的原因是因为请求api时传递的图片URL路径多了一个桶名，导致上传给api接口的图片url不合法。 > > 在这个案例中，上传至Cloudflare R2图床的图片真实url应该为 > > https://pub-d832c662b0414d3082ebaef60f7f2c04.r2.dev/files/479985/2f3a278c-2808-4797-9ce2-065315e50a28.png > > 但实际请求时却是 > > https://pub-d832c662b0414d3082ebaef60f7f2c04.r2.dev/lobe-chat-database/files/479985/2f3a278c-2808-4797-9ce2-065315e50a28.png > > 很明显多了一个桶名`lobe-chat-database`，不知道是什么原因。 ![错误图片](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/57054419/373192264-b7fa0903-1511-4d2d-854d-43049d40c9f3.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..ZMIH_M-g5tHrJ_OMHmVJqVjFq9IPaNCSd7u7vcIOIpo) > > ### 📦 部署环境 > Docker Desktop > > ### 📌 软件版本 > 4.34.2 > > ### 💻 系统环境 > Windows11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 > > ### 🌐 浏览器 > Edge > > 附上我的`docker-compose.yml` > > ```yaml > services: > network-service: > image: alpine > container_name: lobe-network > ports: > - '${LOGTO_PORT}:${LOGTO_PORT}' # Logto > - '3002:3002' # Logto Admin > - '${LOBE_PORT}:3210' # LobeChat > command: tail -f /dev/null > networks: > - lobe-network > > postgresql: > image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16 > container_name: lobe-postgres > ports: > - "5432:5432" > volumes: > - './data:/var/lib/postgresql/data' > environment: > - 'POSTGRES_DB=${LOBE_DB_NAME}' > - 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}' > healthcheck: > test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U postgres'] > interval: 5s > timeout: 5s > retries: 5 > restart: always > networks: > - lobe-network > > logto: > image: svhd/logto > container_name: lobe-logto > network_mode: 'service:network-service' > depends_on: > postgresql: > condition: service_healthy > environment: > - 'TRUST_PROXY_HEADER=1' > - 'PORT=${LOGTO_PORT}' > - 'DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgresql:5432/logto' > - 'ENDPOINT=http://localhost:${LOGTO_PORT}' > - 'ADMIN_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:3002' > entrypoint: ['sh', '-c', 'npm run cli db seed -- --swe && npm start'] > > lobe: > image: lobehub/lobe-chat-database > container_name: lobe-database > network_mode: 'service:network-service' > depends_on: > postgresql: > condition: service_healthy > network-service: > condition: service_started > logto: > condition: service_started > > environment: > - 'APP_URL=http://localhost:3210' > - 'NEXT_AUTH_SSO_PROVIDERS=logto' > - 'KEY_VAULTS_SECRET=Kix2wcUONd4CX51E/ZPAd36BqM4wzJgKjPtz2sGztqQ=' > - 'NEXT_AUTH_SECRET=NX2kaPE923dt6BL2U8e9oSre5RfoT7hg' > - 'NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:${LOBE_PORT}/api/auth' > - 'LOGTO_ISSUER=http://localhost:${LOGTO_PORT}/oidc' > - 'DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgresql:5432/${LOBE_DB_NAME}' > - 'S3_ENDPOINT=${S3_ENDPOINT}' > - 'S3_BUCKET=${S3_BUCKET}' > - 'S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN=${S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN}' > - 'S3_ENABLE_PATH_STYLE=1' > env_file: > - .env > restart: always > > volumes: > data: > driver: local > > networks: > lobe-network: > driver: bridge > ``` > > 以及`.env` > > ```ini > # Cloudflare R2 配置 > S3_ENDPOINT=xxx > S3_BUCKET=lobe-chat-database > S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=xxxx > S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=xxxxx > S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN=https://pub-d832c662b0414d3082ebaef60f7f2c04.r2.dev # 公共 R2.dev 存储桶 > > # Logto secret > LOGTO_CLIENT_ID=xxx > LOGTO_CLIENT_SECRET=xxx > > # Proxy (如果需要) > # HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:7890 > # HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:7890 > > # OpenAI 配置 (如有需要) > # OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxx > # OPENAI_PROXY_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 > # OPENAI_MODEL_LIST=... > > # Lobe Chat配置 > LOBE_PORT=3210 > LOGTO_PORT=3001 > > # Postgres 数据库相关配置 > LOBE_DB_NAME=lobechat > POSTGRES_PASSWORD=xxx > ``` 我也遇到了相同的问题，后来发现是默认S3_ENABLE_PATH_STYLE=1了，Cloudflare R2直接设置成 0就可以了

### 🥰 Description of requirements

As title. I need to migrate the database while retaining the chat history, but this function does not seem to be supported at the moment.

Migration motivation:
Because I only set up an email address for Cloudflare Zero Trust at the beginning, and lobe's database uses the email address as an index, and subsequent logins will not update the account information, and there is no visual account editing function, making it impossible to change the username and avatar of this account later. It is a bit troublesome to manually delete the account and create a new account when entering the database to retain the chat record mapping. It would be much more convenient if you could export the chat records, migrate the database, and then import them.

### 🧐 Solution

Hope to add the function of exporting and importing chat records.

Hey there, @qinghuannn! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's tackle this together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found some similar discussions and issues that might be relevant to your problem:

1. body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering is due to the deprecation warning related to setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address, which is not permitted by RFC 6066. This behavior has been enforced in Node.js, and as a result, `https+ip` connections are being blocked.

To address this issue, you can bypass the TLS certificate validation by setting the `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` environment variable to `0`. This will allow the application to accept unverified certificates, which can be useful in a private or development environment.

Here is how you can set this environment variable:

### For Docker
In your Dockerfile:
```dockerfile
ENV NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0
```

Or in your `docker-compose.yml`:
```yaml
environment:
  - NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0
```

### For Local Development
You can set the environment variable when starting your application:
```bash
NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 npm run start
```

### Example Docker Run Command
```bash
docker run -e NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 <other parameters> <image name>
```

Please note that this method reduces security as it allows Node.js to accept unverified certificates. It is recommended to use this only in trusted environments and revert to the default settings after resolving the issue.

For more secure alternatives, consider:
1. Ensuring all certificates are correctly installed and trusted.
2. Using valid certificates issued by trusted certificate authorities.
3. Properly configuring the certificate chain to ensure Node.js can validate to the root certificate.

For further details, you can refer to the relevant code and documentation:
- [startServer.js](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/scripts/serverLauncher/startServer.js) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/scripts/serverLauncher/startServer.js)</sup>
- [Proxy with Unable to Verify Leaf Signature FAQ](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/faq/proxy-with-unable-to-verify-leaf-signature.mdx) <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/faq/proxy-with-unable-to-verify-leaf-signature.mdx)</sup>

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar unsolved discussion regarding Docker deployment issues that might be related to your problem. You can check it out [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1396) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1396)</sup>.

Regarding your specific issue with HTTPS and IP access in version v1.20.8, there is a known restriction in the LobeChat codebase that enforces the use of TLS for domains other than localhost. This means that HTTPS must be enabled to avoid interruptions in authentication by Authelia <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/authelia.mdx)</sup>.

Additionally, the deprecation warning (DEP0123) you are seeing indicates that setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address is not permitted by RFC 6066 and will be ignored in a future version. This could be contributing to the issue you are experiencing.

To resolve this, you might need to configure your Nginx setup to use a domain name instead of an IP address for HTTPS connections. If you need further assistance with Nginx configuration, please let me know!

1. **[OpenAI is not accessible with `getaddrinfo`](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3828)**: This discussion suggests ensuring the DNS configuration is correct and not overridden by Docker settings. It also recommends setting the DNS configuration file to read-only to prevent modifications <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3828)</sup>.
2. **[[Bug] OpenAI is not accessible](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3822)**: This issue was resolved by adding DNS settings in the `docker-compose` file. The user added the following lines:
    ```yaml
    dns:
      - 8.8.4.4
      - 8.8.8.8
    ```
    This change made the solution permanent <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3822)</sup>.

To troubleshoot your specific 404 error, follow these steps:

1. **Verify `OPENAI_PROXY_URL` Configuration**:
   - Ensure that the `OPENAI_PROXY_URL` is correctly set in your environment variables.
   - Confirm that the URL includes the `/v1` suffix if it is required by the OpenAI service endpoint.

2. **Check for Common Issues**:
   - Double-check the URL for any typos or incorrect paths.
   - Make sure the URL is accessible and correctly points to the OpenAI service.

3. **Consult Related Discussions**:

     - [Why is the return value blank after configuring environment variables in Docker?](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/623)

4. **Review Error Handling in Code**:
   - Check the error handling in your code to ensure that it properly captures and logs the error details. For example, the `LobeAi360AI` class in the LobeChat program has specific error handling for different types of errors, such as `ProviderBizError` and `InvalidProviderAPIKey`. <!-- Answer -->
To resolve the CORS error for a PUT request to your local server (`bilalbucke.localhost:9001`) in Docker on Ubuntu using Firefox, you need to ensure that the CORS headers are correctly configured on your server. Based on the provided `docker-compose.yml` file, it looks like you are using MinIO, which has CORS settings.

You need to configure the CORS settings for MinIO to allow requests from your local server. Here is how you can do it:

1. **Update the MinIO CORS configuration**: Ensure that the `MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` environment variable is set correctly to allow requests from your local server. In your `docker-compose.yml`, it should look like this:

    ```yml
    minio:
      image: minio/minio
      container_name: lobe-minio
      network_mode: 'service:network-service'
      volumes:
        - './s3_data:/etc/minio/data'
      environment:
        - 'MINIO_ROOT_USER=${MINIO_ROOT_USER}'
        - 'MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}'
        - 'MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN=http://bilalbucke.localhost:9001'
      restart: always
      command: >
        server /etc/minio/data --address ":${MINIO_PORT}" --console-address ":9001"
    ```

2. **Set up CORS configuration in MinIO**: You need to create a CORS configuration file and apply it to your MinIO server. Here is an example of a CORS configuration JSON file (`cors.json`):

    ```json
    [
      {
        "AllowedOrigins": ["http://bilalbucke.localhost:9001"],
        "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "PUT", "POST", "DELETE"],
        "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
        "ExposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
        "MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
      }
    ]
    ```

3. **Apply the CORS configuration**: Use the MinIO client (mc) to apply the CORS configuration to your MinIO server. First, install the MinIO client if you haven't already:

    ```sh
    wget https://dl.min.io/client/mc/release/linux-amd64/mc
    chmod +x mc
    sudo mv mc /usr/local/bin/
    ```

    Then, configure the MinIO client and apply the CORS settings:

    ```sh
    mc alias set myminio http://localhost:${MINIO_PORT} ${MINIO_ROOT_USER} ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    mc admin config set myminio/ api.cors < cors.json
    ```

By ensuring that the CORS settings are correctly configured, you should be able to resolve the CORS error for your PUT request <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

----    
### 📦 Deployment environment

Official Preview, Docker

### 📌 Software version

latest

### 💻 System environment

Windows

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 Problem description

When the set theme color is opposite to that of the system (lobechat is set to light color, and the windows color mode is set to dark), when refreshing the web page, the dark color will appear first and then the light color. I also found this problem in lobechat.com, local and self-built Docker.
I tracked it down and found that the reason for this situation is (lobechat's theme is light and the windows system color is dark):
1. Refresh the webpage when it is in light mode. This step will change the LOBE_THEME_APPEARANCE in the cookie to dark.
2. When refreshing the web page again, it will first change to dark color and then switch to light color, and LOBE_THEME_APPEARANCE will be changed to light
3. The above two steps will be followed later.

I'm seeing this issue in both Chrome and Edge browsers.

### 📷 Steps to reproduce

1. Select the color mode as dark in windows
2. Select the theme as light color in LobeChat (the LOBE_THEME_APPEARANCE value in the cookie is light)
3. Refresh the web page. This refresh will not change from dark to light, but will set the value of LOBE_THEME_APPEARANCE in the cookie to dark.

Hey @davletsh1n! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash that bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the AWS region not being correctly set or respected in your application. Here are a few things to check and consider:

1. **Environment Variable Configuration**: Ensure that the `AWS_REGION` environment variable is correctly set to `eu-north-1` in your Vercel environment settings. Double-check that there are no typos or misconfigurations.

2. **Payload Override**: In the code, the AWS region can be overridden by the payload if it contains an `awsRegion` value. Make sure that the payload does not unintentionally set the region to `us-east-1` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/api/chat/agentRuntime.ts)</sup>.

3. **Default Region**: The code defaults to `us-east-1` if no region is provided during the instantiation of the `BedrockRuntimeClient`. Ensure that the region is explicitly set to `eu-north-1` in all relevant parts of your code <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/bedrock/index.ts)</sup>.

4. **Check Code Logic**: Review the logic in your code where the AWS region is set and used, especially in the `getLlmOptionsFromPayload` function, to ensure it aligns with your environment settings <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/api/chat/agentRuntime.ts)</sup>.

By verifying these aspects, you should be able to resolve the region mismatch issue.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
A similar issue was discussed in a closed thread where the Groq API request was rejected due to IP restrictions. The suggested solution was to enable Groq for client-side requests <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2147)</sup>.

To address the region-based restriction, you can modify the `preferredRegion` setting to exclude regions where the service is unavailable, such as Hong Kong. Here's an example of how to configure the `preferredRegion`:

```ts
export const preferredRegion = [
  'icn1',
  'sin1',
  'hnd1',
  'kix1',
  'bom1',
  'cpt1',
  'pdx1',
  'cle1',
  'syd1',
  'iad1',
  'sfo1',
  'gru1',
];
```

By not including "Hong Kong (hkg1)" in the `preferredRegion` array, you can avoid using the unavailable region <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/api/chat/google/route.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @nikhil-pandey! 👋 I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash those bugs together while we wait for a human maintainer.

<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering is due to the use of the `max_tokens` parameter, which is not supported by the Azure OpenAI O1 models. Instead, you should use `max_completion_tokens`. 

To resolve this issue, you need to modify the request construction in the codebase to replace `max_tokens` with `max_completion_tokens` for the Azure OpenAI O1 models. This change should be made in the part of the code where the request parameters are set for Azure OpenAI models, specifically in the `LobeAzureOpenAI` class or wherever the request payload is being constructed <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/azureOpenai/index.ts)</sup>.

If you haven't explicitly set a max token limit, ensure that the default configuration or any conditional logic in the code does not automatically include `max_tokens` for these models. You might need to update the logic to conditionally set `max_completion_tokens` instead, based on the model being used.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with file uploads getting stuck at "Preparando para enviar..." (Preparing to send) could be related to several factors in the Lobe Chat system. Here are a few things to check and configure:

1. **MinIO Configuration**: Ensure that your MinIO setup is correctly configured with the necessary access keys, bucket policies, and CORS settings. Double-check that the `MINIO_ROOT_USER`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are correctly set and that the bucket policy allows the required actions <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local-logto/.env.example)</sup>.

2. **Network and Firewall Settings**: Verify that there are no network issues or firewall settings blocking the connection between your application and the MinIO server. Ensure that the S3 endpoint is accessible from your application.

3. **Docker Resource Allocation**: Make sure that Docker has sufficient resources allocated, especially memory and CPU, to handle file uploads and vector operations. This is crucial for PostgreSQL and PGVector to function properly <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/knowledge-base.mdx)</sup>.

4. **Logto and Authentication**: Confirm that Logto is properly configured for authentication and that there are no issues with user permissions that might affect file uploads <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local-logto/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

5. **Error Logs**: Check the logs for any error messages that might provide more insight into why the upload is getting stuck. This can help identify if there are specific errors occurring during the upload process.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider reviewing the configurations and logs for any discrepancies or errors that might be causing the upload to hang.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @davidelectricfree! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. I'm a bot 🤖 with a knack for solving tech issues.

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion where the `logto` service in a Docker Compose setup for `lobe-chat-db` automatically exits after starting. The issue was related to a version update of `logto`, and it was suggested to use the `svhd/logto:1.19.0` version to avoid errors <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4009)</sup>.

In your case, the error message indicates a timeout issue with the `pg` client. Here are some steps you can try to resolve this:

1. **Check Database Connectivity**: Ensure that the `postgresql` service is running and accessible. You can verify this by checking the logs of the `postgresql` container to ensure it is healthy and ready to accept connections.

2. **Adjust Timeout Settings**: If possible, try increasing the timeout settings for the `pg` client in the `logto` service. This might involve modifying the configuration files or environment variables related to the database connection.

3. **Verify Environment Variables**: Double-check the environment variables, especially `DB_URL`, to ensure they are correctly set and pointing to the right database host and port.

4. **Use Compatible Versions**: As mentioned in the similar discussion, consider using a specific version of the `logto` image that is known to work without issues, such as `svhd/logto:1.19.0`.

5. **Network Configuration**: Ensure that the network configuration allows the `logto` service to communicate with the `postgresql` service. The `network_mode` should be correctly set to allow this communication.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might want to look into the specific configuration of your Docker Compose setup and ensure all services are correctly defined and able to communicate with each other.

To address the `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` error during file uploads in your Docker Compose setup on a Synology NAS, consider the following steps:

1. **CORS Configuration**: Ensure that the `MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` environment variable is correctly set to allow requests from your LobeChat application. It should match the domain and port of your application. For example:
   ```yaml
   environment:
     - "MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN=http://192.168.50.114:${LOBE_PORT}"
   ```
   This setting allows cross-origin requests from your LobeChat domain <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Network Configuration**: Verify that your network settings in the `docker-compose.yml` file are correctly configured. Ensure that all services can communicate over the specified ports and network. The `network_mode` and `ports` settings should be correct and consistent across services.

3. **Resource Constraints**: Check if there are any resource constraints (CPU, memory) on your Synology NAS that might be causing the connection to reset. Ensure that your NAS has sufficient resources to handle the services.

4. **Logs and Errors**: Review the logs of the involved containers (`minio`, `lobe`, etc.) for any errors or warnings that might provide more insight into the issue.

5. **Retry Mechanism**: Note that the application does not have an explicit retry mechanism for file uploads. If network errors occur, the file is removed from the upload list without retrying <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/chat/action.ts)</sup>.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider testing the setup on a different network or environment to rule out network-specific problems.

1. **Bucket Policy Configuration**: Ensure that the bucket policy allows the necessary actions. The policy should look like this:

   ```json
   {
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:GetBucketLocation"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe"]
       },
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe"],
         "Condition": {
           "StringEquals": {
             "s3:prefix": ["files/*"]
           }
         }
       },
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject", "s3:GetObject"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe/files/**"]
       }
     ],
     "Version": "2012-10-17"
   }
   ```

2. **CORS Configuration**: Ensure that CORS is configured correctly to allow cross-origin requests from your domain. This can be set in the MinIO WebUI under `Configuration - API - Cors Allow Origin`, or in the Docker Compose file under `minio - environment - MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN`.

3. **Access Keys**: Verify that the correct `Access Key` and `Secret Key` are set in your `.env` file under `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.

4. **Endpoint Configuration**: Ensure that the `S3_ENDPOINT` is correctly configured without any suffix path, as this can prevent file access. For example:

   ```shell
   S3_ENDPOINT=http://192.168.50.114:${MINIO_PORT}
   ```

5. **ACL Settings**: Check if `S3_SET_ACL` is set to `public-read` if required by your use case. If your service provider does not support individual ACLs, set `S3_SET_ACL` to `0`.

6. **Path Style Access**: If using MinIO, ensure `S3_ENABLE_PATH_STYLE` is set to `1` to enable path-style access, which is the default for MinIO.

7. **Restart Services**: After making changes, restart the services using:

   ```sh
   docker compose up -d
   ```

   Avoid using `docker compose restart lobe` as it will not reload the environment variables.

By ensuring these configurations are correct, you should be able to resolve the 403 Forbidden status during the upload process <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/s3.mdx)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
To support `.yml` files for chunking, you need to update the `getType` method in the `ChunkingLoader` class to recognize `.yml` as a valid file extension. Here's how you can do it:

1. **Locate the `getType` Method**: This method is responsible for determining the file type based on the file extension.

2. **Add Support for `.yml`**: Modify the method to include a condition for `.yml` files. You can treat `.yml` the same as `.yaml`. Here's an example of how you might update the method:

   ```ts
   private getType = (filename: string): LangChainLoaderType | undefined => {
       if (filename.endsWith('yaml') || filename.endsWith('yml')) {
         return 'yaml';
       }
       // ... existing conditions
   }
   ```

By adding this condition, the system will recognize `.yml` files as `yaml` and handle them accordingly. This should resolve the issue you're experiencing with unsupported file types for `.yml` files.

NEXT_AUTH_SECRET=<your_generated_secret>

AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET=<your_github_client_secret>
NEXTAUTH_URL=<your_callback_url>
```

Regarding the proxy settings, these are optional and should only be uncommented and configured if you need to use a proxy. If you don't require a proxy, you can leave these lines commented out <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/production/zitadel/.env.example)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The "Access Denied" error when accessing the S3 bucket could be due to several reasons:

1. **Incorrect Access Keys**: Ensure that `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are correctly configured.

2. **Bucket Policy**: Verify that the bucket policy allows the necessary actions, such as `s3:GetObject` for the specific resource path.

3. **Public Access Domain**: Make sure the `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` is publicly accessible and allows cross-origin requests if needed.

4. **Endpoint Configuration**: Check that `S3_ENDPOINT` is correctly set without any suffix path.

5. **ACL Settings**: If `S3_SET_ACL` is set to `public-read`, ensure the service provider supports it, or set it to `0` if not supported.

Review these configurations to resolve the access issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/s3.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/minio-bucket.config.json)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @cookieY! 👋 I'm here to help you with bugs, questions, and becoming a contributor. Let's squash some bugs together!

<!-- Answer -->
A similar issue was discussed where the Dalle-3 text2image feature returned a 400 error with the message "Not support internal host proxy." This happens because the proxy implementation blocks requests to internal IP addresses. The error occurs when a DNS lookup resolves to a private IP address, which is not allowed by the proxy <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(backend)/webapi/proxy/route.ts)</sup>.

To address this, ensure that the proxy settings are correctly configured and that the request is not resolving to a private IP. You might need to adjust your network or proxy settings to allow the necessary external requests.

The issue you're experiencing with chat names staying as "Default Topic" when using the Azure backend might be related to the `createTopic` function. Additionally, ensure that any configuration settings related to topic naming are correctly set for the Azure backend. These settings can be found in the configuration files, such as `setting.json`, which includes options for automatic topic creation and naming models <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/en-US/setting.json)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/pl-PL/setting.json)</sup>.

The system uses an `imageList` in the message content to manage images, where each image has an `id`, `url`, and `alt` text. This setup should allow the system to handle multiple images <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/__tests__/chat.test.ts)</sup>.

However, if the model continues to describe the first image or fails to recognize the second one, it could be a bug in the image context management. There might be a need to review the logic that updates the context when a new image is processed, as this could be causing the issue.

To address this, you might want to check if the image IDs are being correctly updated and if the context-switching logic is functioning as expected. Additionally, ensure that the error handling mechanisms are logging any issues that occur during image processing <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(backend)/webapi/text-to-image/[provider]/route.ts)</sup>.

For the Docker container exiting with status 139, this typically indicates a segmentation fault. Here are some steps you can try:

1. **Check System Compatibility**: Ensure your system meets all the requirements for running the LobeChat Docker image, including dependencies like PostgreSQL with the PGVector plugin.

2. **Inspect Logs**: Use `docker logs lobechat` to check for any error messages that might provide more insight into the issue.

3. **Resource Allocation**: Ensure your Docker environment has sufficient resources (CPU, memory) allocated.

4. **Update Docker**: Consider updating Docker to a more recent version if possible, as compatibility issues might be resolved in newer releases.

5. **Rebuild the Image**: If you have customized the Docker image, try rebuilding it to ensure all dependencies are correctly installed.

If these steps don't resolve the issue, further investigation into the specific error logs might be necessary.

The issue you're experiencing is due to a conflict between models with the same name from different providers. The system should differentiate models using unique identifiers, but it seems there's a problem with this process in your setup.

To resolve this temporarily, you can remove the conflicting model from GitHub, as you've mentioned. However, a more permanent solution would involve ensuring that each model has a unique identifier in the system, even if they share the same name. This is typically handled by the `getModelCardsById` function, which uses unique IDs to distinguish models <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/modelList/selectors/modelProvider.ts)</sup>.

You might want to check if the unique identifiers are correctly implemented and used in your configuration. If the issue persists, reviewing the logic in the model selection and configuration components might help identify where the conflict arises.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @zzdx713! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you need assistance with. Let's tackle this together!

<!-- Answer -->
To resolve the Docker build error related to the missing `/app/.next/standalone` directory, ensure the following:

1. **Build Script**: Verify that the `build:docker` script in your `package.json` is correctly configured. It should include `DOCKER=true next build` to generate the standalone output <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/package.json)</sup>.

2. **Next.js Configuration**: In your `next.config.mjs`, ensure the `output` property is set to `'standalone'` when building with Docker. This is controlled by the `buildWithDocker` variable, which should be set to `true` when the `DOCKER` environment variable is `'true'` <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/next.config.mjs)</sup>.

3. **Dependencies**: Make sure all necessary dependencies are installed before running the build command. The Dockerfile uses `pnpm i` to install dependencies, so ensure `pnpm` is correctly set up.

4. **Build Output**: Confirm that the build process completes without errors and that the `.next/standalone` directory is created in the `/app` directory.

5. **Dockerfile Configuration**: Ensure the Dockerfile is correctly set up to copy the standalone directory. The `COPY --from=builder /app/.next/standalone /app/` line should be present and correctly configured.

If the issue persists, check the build logs for any errors that might indicate why the directory is not being created.

<!-- Answer -->
To resolve the 405 error and the "Unexpected end of JSON input" SyntaxError in the `createShareGPTUrl` function, try the following:

1. **405 Error (Method Not Allowed):**
   - Verify that the endpoint `https://sharegpt.com/api/conversations` supports the `POST` method. If not, use the correct HTTP method.
   - Double-check the URL for any typos or incorrect paths.

2. **"Unexpected end of JSON input" SyntaxError:**
   - This error usually occurs when the response body is empty or not valid JSON. Ensure the API returns a valid JSON response.
   - Check if the API requires additional headers or authentication that might be missing.

Here's a code snippet to handle the response and avoid the SyntaxError:

```ts
const res = await fetch(SHARE_GPT_URL, {
  body: JSON.stringify({ ...conversation, items }),
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  method: 'POST',
});

if (!res.ok) {
  throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${res.status}`);
}

const data = await res.json();

if (!data.id) throw new Error('Failed to create ShareGPT URL');

return `https://shareg.pt/${data.id}`;
```

This checks if the response is OK before parsing the JSON, helping diagnose request issues <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/share.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/chat/slices/share/action.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/__tests__/share.test.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
The error message "connect ECONNREFUSED 81.12.30.45:443" indicates that the application is trying to connect to a service at the specified IP address and port, but the connection is being refused. This could be due to several reasons:

1. **Incorrect Configuration**: Ensure that the database connection settings, such as the host, port, username, and password, are correctly configured in your environment variables or configuration files. Verify that the `DATABASE_URL` is set correctly.

2. **Network Issues**: Check if there are any network issues preventing the connection. Ensure that the server hosting the database is accessible from your application environment.

3. **Firewall or Security Groups**: Make sure that any firewalls or security groups allow traffic on the necessary ports (e.g., 5432 for PostgreSQL).

4. **Database Service**: Verify that the PostgreSQL service is running and listening on the correct port.

5. **WebSocket URL**: The error log mentions a WebSocket URL. Ensure that this URL is correct and that the WebSocket service is running and accessible.

Review these areas to identify and resolve the connection issue.

The issue where only the first image can be successfully uploaded and sent in a chat topic using Docker on Windows with Firefox might be related to several factors:

1. **File Upload Blacklist**: Ensure that subsequent images are not being filtered out due to a blacklist.

2. **Error Handling**: Check for any errors logged during upload, such as `UNAUTHORIZED` or network errors, which might cause the file to be removed from the upload list.

3. **URL Generation**: Verify that `previewUrl` and `base64Url` are correctly generated for each image. Issues here might prevent subsequent uploads.

4. **State Management**: Ensure that the state is correctly updated for each file upload, avoiding race conditions or state conflicts.

5. **Network or CORS Issues**: Check for any network restrictions or CORS issues that might affect subsequent uploads.

Review these areas in the code to identify potential causes for the issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/chat/action.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @SmileMachine, I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have! Let's get to the bottom of this together.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue with the PWA installation not triggering on Chrome across different platforms could be related to several factors. Here are a few potential causes and things to check:

1. **PWA Installation Conditions**: Ensure that the conditions for triggering the PWA installation event are met. The `pwaInstallHandler` requires the `canInstall` flag to be true, `hidePWAInstaller` to be false, and `isShowPWAGuide` to be true for the installation process to initiate <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/PWAInstall/Install.tsx)</sup>.

2. **PWA_INSTALL_ID**: Verify that the `PWA_INSTALL_ID` is correctly set in the DOM. The installation dialog is triggered using this ID, and it should match the expected element <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/usePWAInstall.test.ts)</sup>.

3. **Platform Detection**: Check if the `usePlatform` hook correctly detects the platform and supports PWA installation. This hook determines if the browser and OS support PWA installation <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/usePlatform.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/usePlatform.ts)</sup>.

4. **Chrome Configuration**: Ensure there are no specific configurations or permissions in Chrome that might be preventing the PWA installation. Although no specific configuration issues were identified, it's worth checking browser settings related to PWA support.

If these aspects are correctly configured and the issue persists, further investigation into the `pwa-install-handler` library or recent changes in version 1.22.6 might be necessary, although no specific issues were identified in the available information.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to an error that occurs when trying to chat after logging in for the first time. This might be due to asynchronous operations affecting the initialization of the chat interface. Specifically, the `enableAuth` value might be incorrect during initialization because of an asynchronous fetch, which can impact the `isLoginOnInit` state used to initialize the agent store and user state <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/layout/GlobalProvider/StoreInitialization.tsx)</sup>.

Additionally, there are event listeners or hooks in place that should update the chat interface state upon successful login. In the `ClerkLogin` component, functions like `resend` and `deleteMessage` are called when the user is signed in, which are likely responsible for updating the chat interface <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/Error/ClerkLogin/index.tsx)</sup>.

A potential workaround is to refresh the page after logging in, as you've noted that this resolves the issue. This refresh might help in reinitializing the state correctly.

<!-- Answer -->
To identify the entry point of your custom web app created from the Lobe Chat open-source code, you should look at the `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD` instructions in the Dockerfile. The entry point is set to execute the Node.js application with the following command:

```bash
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/node"]
CMD ["/app/startServer.js"]
```

This indicates that the entry point of your application is the `startServer.js` script located in the `/app` directory. Ensure that this script is correctly configured and accessible when deploying your application on cPanel <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/Dockerfile)</sup>.

The entry point for the Lobe Chat application is specified in the `package.json` file, which uses the `next start` command to start the application on port 3210. This is defined under the `scripts` section as:

```json
"start": "next start -p 3210"
```

This indicates that the application is a Next.js app, and the entry point is typically the `pages` directory, specifically `pages/index.js` or `pages/index.tsx` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/package.json)</sup>.

If you need further assistance or want to discuss this with the developers, a maintainer has already been looped in to help with your query.

Instead, you should use `max_completion_tokens`. To resolve this issue, modify the request construction in the codebase to replace `max_tokens` with `max_completion_tokens` for the Azure OpenAI O1 models. This change should be made in the part of the code where the request parameters are set for Azure OpenAI models, specifically in the `LobeAzureOpenAI` class or wherever the request payload is being constructed <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4248)</sup>.

The issues you're encountering with the `createShareGPTUrl` function seem to be related to several errors:

1. **405 Status Code**: This indicates that the server does not support the HTTP method used for the request. The `createShareGPTUrl` function uses a `POST` method, so ensure that the server endpoint is configured to accept `POST` requests <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/de-DE/error.json)</sup>.

2. **SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input**: This error typically occurs when the response body is not valid JSON. It might be due to an incomplete response from the server. Ensure that the server is returning a complete and valid JSON response.

3. **Message Channel Closed**: This error suggests that the asynchronous response was not received before the message channel closed. This could be due to network issues or server-side delays. Check the server logs for any errors or delays in processing the request.

To address these issues, verify the server configuration to ensure it supports `POST` requests, check the server response for completeness and validity, and investigate any potential network issues that might be causing delays or interruptions.

<!-- Greeting -->
@fdg157 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助您解决问题、回答疑问并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的过程中帮助您。

<!-- Answer -->
To address the connectivity check failure in LobeChat when using a locally proxied Ollama service with restricted IP access, you need to configure Ollama for cross-origin access. This involves setting the `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` environment variable to allow access from any origin. Here are the steps based on your operating system:

### On macOS:
1. Set the environment variable using `launchctl`:
   ```bash
   launchctl setenv OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*"
   ```
2. Restart the Ollama application.

### On Windows:
1. Exit the Ollama program from the taskbar.
2. Edit system environment variables from the Control Panel.
3. Create or edit the `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` environment variable for your user account, setting the value to `*`.
4. Save the changes and restart the system.
5. Run Ollama again.

### On Linux:
1. Edit the systemd service:
   ```bash
   sudo systemctl edit ollama.service
   ```
2. Add the following under `[Service]`:
   ```bash
   [Service]
   Environment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0"
   Environment="OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*"
   ```
3. Save and exit.
4. Reload systemd and restart Ollama:
   ```bash
   sudo systemctl daemon-reload
   sudo systemctl restart ollama
   ```

### Using Docker:
1. Run the Docker container with the environment variable:
   ```bash
   docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -e OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*" -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
   ```

Additionally, ensure that the `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` in your LobeChat configuration is set to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, as this is the default host used by the Ollama service. If you have customized the base URL, make sure it matches the configuration in your Ollama service setup. These steps should help resolve the connectivity issue by allowing cross-origin requests to the Ollama service <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/providers/ollama.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/ollama.ts)</sup>.

Hey @xingyingshuailiangzheng! I'm here to help you with your software issue. Let's work together to solve the problem while we wait for a human maintainer.

<!-- Answer -->
I found two similar closed issues related to the "Missing publishableKey" error:

1. [Bug: "Error: @clerk/nextjs: Missing publishableKey." despite the correct ENVs being set](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3086)
2. [Docs: clerk配置后Missing publishableKey](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3080)

The suggested solution is to ensure that the `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` environment variable is correctly set in your `.env` file. It should look like this:

```plaintext
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=your_publishable_key_here
```

Make sure the key is correctly formatted and matches the one from your Clerk dashboard. Additionally, verify that your Next.js application is loading environment variables from the `.env` file properly. If deploying on a platform like Vercel, ensure these environment variables are also set in the deployment settings <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/auth.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/vercel.mdx)</sup>.

If you are using Docker, remember that the `NEXT_PUBLIC_XXX` variable must be injected into the Docker image during the build process. body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering with the Vercel deployment of the lobe-chat project is due to the missing `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable. To resolve this, you need to add this environment variable to your Vercel project settings. Here’s how you can do it:

1. **Create and Configure Webhook in Clerk**: 
   - Go to your Clerk dashboard and create a webhook endpoint for your Vercel project. The endpoint should be something like `https://your-project.vercel.app/api/webhooks/clerk`.
   - Subscribe to the necessary user events (`user.created`, `user.deleted`, `user.updated`).

2. **Retrieve the Webhook Secret**:
   - After creating the webhook, find the webhook secret in the Clerk dashboard. It will be displayed in the bottom right corner of the webhook configuration page.

3. **Add the Webhook Secret to Vercel**:
   - Go to your Vercel project settings.
   - Navigate to the "Environment Variables" section.
   - Add a new environment variable with the key `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and the value as the webhook secret you retrieved from Clerk.

```shell
CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

By adding the `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to your Vercel environment variables, you should be able to resolve the deployment failure. Ensure that the URL in the webhook configuration starts with `https://` to maintain the integrity of the URL, as this is essential for the webhook to function correctly <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/vercel.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/clerk.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
@CaffeineCM 你好！我是[ Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助你解决 bug、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者处理你的问题时提供帮助。

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar issue related to handling image URLs in the `lobe-chat` framework. The framework converts image URLs to base64 format internally, and an 'invalid_image_url' error can occur if the URL does not conform to expected formats or cannot be processed correctly. This might happen if the URL does not result in a valid base64 conversion or if the URL type is not recognized <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/anthropicHelpers.ts)</sup>.

To resolve a similar issue, it was suggested to add an environment variable `LLM_VISION_IMAGE_USE_BASE64=1`. This might help in resolving the "invalid image" problem <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4375)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @ArcCal! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions for lobe-chat. Let's tackle this together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar open issue regarding a persistent upgrade notification in the lobe-chat repository. The issue is titled "[Please turn off the upgrade red point after I close the upgrade tip](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1872)" and was last updated on August 21, 2024. The suggested solution was to fix the issue, but it remains open <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1872)</sup>.

Regarding your specific issue with the installation prompt, the lobe-chat codebase uses the `zustand` state management library to manage UI state for prompts <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/contributing/Basic/Architecture.md)</sup>. Additionally, there is an event listener that responds to user actions on the installation prompt. This listener updates the system status to hide the PWA installer when the prompt is dismissed <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/PWAInstall/Install.tsx)</sup>.

Unfortunately, there is no specific information available about a configuration option or flag to permanently disable the installation prompt. You might want to check the event listener implementation to see if you can modify it to achieve the desired behavior.

The issues you're experiencing with CORS and LaTeX rendering in LobeChat can be addressed by reviewing your Nginx configuration and ensuring proper CORS settings.

1. **CORS Configuration**: The error message indicates a CORS issue, which might be due to incorrect configuration. In your Nginx configuration, you have added `add_header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' '*' always;`. While this allows all origins, it might not be sufficient if other headers or methods are required. You might need to add more specific CORS headers, such as:

   ```nginx
   add_header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' '*';
   add_header 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' 'GET, POST, OPTIONS';
   add_header 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' 'DNT, X-CustomHeader, Keep-Alive, User-Agent, X-Requested-With, If-Modified-Since, Cache-Control, Content-Type';
   ```

   Ensure that these headers are placed in the correct context within your Nginx configuration.

2. **KaTeX and LaTeX Rendering**: The duplication issue with LaTeX formulas might be related to how the CSS for KaTeX is being loaded. Since you mentioned a CORS issue with CSS files, ensure that the CSS files are accessible and not blocked by CORS policies. Verify that the URLs for these resources are correct and that they are being served with the appropriate headers.

3. **Nginx Configuration**: Since you are using a custom Nginx configuration, ensure that it aligns with the recommended settings for LobeChat. If possible, refer to any official documentation or examples provided by LobeChat for guidance.

4. **Testing**: After making changes to your Nginx configuration, clear your browser cache and test the application again to see if the issues persist.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider checking the server logs for more detailed error messages that might provide further insights.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion that might be relevant to your issue. In a previous discussion, it was noted that the `CUSTOM_MODELS` environment variable is specifically for the OpenAI provider, and if you have also set Google environment variables, it might lead to unexpected behavior <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1741)</sup>.

Regarding your specific issue with the `GOOGLE_MODEL_LIST`, there are a few potential reasons why the filtering might not work as expected:

1. **Incorrect Parsing of Model String**: Ensure that the model string is correctly formatted. The string should be properly formatted with commas separating model entries and using `+` or `-` to indicate addition or removal.

2. **Handling of 'all' Keyword**: If the model string includes `-all`, it sets `removeAll` to `true`, which will remove all models. This might not be the intended behavior if you expect only specific models to be removed.

3. **Unknown Capabilities**: If the model string includes unknown capabilities, they are ignored with a warning. This might lead to unexpected behavior if the filtering logic relies on specific capabilities <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/parseModels.ts)</sup>.

Make sure that the `GOOGLE_MODEL_LIST` is correctly formatted and that the models you want to add are specified correctly. If the issue persists, you might want to check the logs for any warnings or errors related to the model parsing.

### 🐛 Problem description

When editing a historical conversation (not the last one) in multiple long conversations, you will jump directly to the bottom of the answer. At this time, you need to scroll up to find the edited content. It is speculated that the distance to the top is always used, and the height of the text box is limited when editing, causing the content to be edited to become shorter, and the place with the same height as the top becomes the bottom (or lower).

### 📷 Steps to reproduce

Open a session and add two messages, each message `"test\n"*200`. Then click to edit the first message to reproduce.

### 🚦 Expected results

The edit button is at the top of the single message so this problem can be avoided/

Ability to set the non-folding height of the edit box (it is best if the edit button is suspended so that you can turn it to where it is and modify it)/

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the scrolling behavior when editing a message in a long conversation. When you edit a message that is not the last one, the interface jumps to the bottom, making it difficult to find the content you want to edit. This might be due to the way the height of the text box is controlled during editing, which can affect the scrolling position.

Currently, the height of the text box is controlled by the `DraggablePanel` component, which has defined minimum and maximum heights. This could be causing the issue where the content appears to jump to the bottom when editing <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/chat/(workspace)/@conversation/features/ChatInput/Desktop/index.tsx)</sup>.

To address this, you might consider implementing a mechanism to keep the edit button visible or floating while scrolling, which would allow you to edit messages more conveniently. However, there is no existing functionality or component in the repository that provides this feature <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/components/AutoScroll.tsx)</sup>.

The error message you're encountering, "the length of messages must be an odd number," suggests that the payload being sent to Baidu's API has an even number of messages, which is not allowed by the API's requirements. To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the number of messages in your request payload is odd.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and fix this issue:

1. **Check Message Count**: Verify the number of messages in the payload you are sending. Ensure that it is an odd number.

2. **Adjust Payload**: If the number of messages is even, consider adding or removing a message to make it odd. This could be a system message or a placeholder if necessary.

3. **Review Code**: Look into the part of your code where the message payload is constructed. Ensure that the logic correctly handles the message count according to Baidu's API requirements.

If you need further assistance, you might want to look into the specific part of the codebase that constructs and sends message payloads to Baidu's API, which is handled by the `LobeWenxinAI` class <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/wenxin/index.ts)</sup>.

When the `HUGGINGFACE_MODEL_LIST` is not configured, the application defaults to displaying models from the `LOBE_DEFAULT_MODEL_LIST`. This list includes a variety of models from different providers, but it seems that in your case, only a single model is being displayed. This could be due to a configuration issue or a limitation in how the application retrieves and displays models when the list is not explicitly set.

To resolve this, you might want to explicitly set the `HUGGINGFACE_MODEL_LIST` to include the models you wish to display. This can be done by configuring the list with the specific models you want to enable. If the issue persists, it could be related to how the application handles the retrieval of models from Hugging Face when the list is not specified, which might require further investigation into the application's configuration or codebase.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
在代码库中，消息对象包含一个 `sessionId` 字段，该字段与用户和助手的消息相关联。您可以在 `src/server/services/dataImporter/__tests__/fixtures/messages.json` 文件中找到示例，其中每条消息都有一个 `sessionId`，用于跟踪会话及其对应的响应。例如：

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "do you know ChatGPT?",
  "sessionId": "inbox",
  "id": "C5CiFuWL"
},
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "...",
  "parentId": "C5CiFuWL",
  "sessionId": "inbox",
  "id": "GNfOJrZW"
}
```

这种模式表明，`sessionId` 用于跟踪对话和相应的响应。您可以通过查看这些数据结构来提取每个回答的会话ID <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/services/dataImporter/__tests__/fixtures/messages.json)</sup>。

For example:

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "do you know ChatGPT?",
  "sessionId": "inbox",
  "id": "C5CiFuWL"
},
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "...",
  "parentId": "C5CiFuWL",
  "sessionId": "inbox",
  "id": "GNfOJrZW"
}
```

This pattern shows that the `sessionId` is used to track conversations and corresponding responses. You can extract the session ID for each answer by looking at these data structures <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/services/dataImporter/ __tests__/fixtures/messages.json)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
要彻底删除对话历史并确保导出的助手 JSON 配置文件中不包含任何历史消息，可以按照以下步骤操作：

1. 在设置中找到“危险”部分。
2. 选择“清除所有会话消息”。
3. 点击“立即清除”按钮。
4. 系统会提示确认清除所有聊天数据，确认后将会清除所有会话数据，包括助手、文件、消息、插件等。
5. 清除成功后，系统会提示“已清除所有会话消息”。

这样可以确保在导出的助手 JSON 配置文件中不包含任何历史消息<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/zh-CN/setting.json)</sup>。

To completely delete the conversation history and ensure that the exported Assistant JSON configuration file does not contain any historical messages, you can follow these steps:

1. Find the "Danger" section in settings.
2. Select Clear all conversation messages.
3. Click the "Clear Now" button.
4. The system will prompt to confirm the clearing of all chat data. After confirmation, all session data, including assistants, files, messages, plug-ins, etc. will be cleared.
5. After the clearing is successful, the system will prompt "All session messages have been cleared."

This ensures that no historical messages are included in the exported assistant JSON configuration file<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/zh-CN/setting .json)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
It seems like you're encountering an "UNAUTHORIZED" error when deploying LobeChat using Docker Compose. Here are some steps and considerations that might help resolve the issue:

1. **Verify Environment Variables**: Ensure that all necessary environment variables are correctly set in your `.env` file. This includes `NEXT_AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_CASDOOR_ID`, `AUTH_CASDOOR_SECRET`, and `AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER`. These are crucial for authentication to work properly with Casdoor <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/casdoor.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Casdoor Configuration**: Double-check the Casdoor application settings. Make sure the callback URL is correctly set to `http://192.168.8.245:3210/api/auth/callback/casdoor` as per your local network setup. This URL should match the `AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER` environment variable <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/casdoor.mdx)</sup>.

3. **CORS Settings**: Ensure that CORS settings are correctly configured for MinIO and Casdoor. The `MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` should allow requests from your LobeChat instance URL, which is `http://192.168.8.245:3210` in your case <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

4. **Check Docker Logs**: Review the logs for each Docker service to identify any specific errors or warnings that might provide more context on the issue. This can help pinpoint whether the problem lies with Casdoor, MinIO, or another service.

5. **Restart Services**: After making changes to the configuration, ensure you restart the Docker services to apply the updates. You can do this with `docker-compose down` followed by `docker-compose up -d`.

6. **Network Configuration**: Ensure that your Docker network settings are correctly configured and that there are no firewall rules blocking communication between the services.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider checking similar issues or discussions for additional insights. For example, there was a similar issue related to `UNAUTHORIZED` errors in tRPC handlers, which was resolved by ensuring the authentication service was correctly configured and the necessary environment variables were set <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4186)</sup>.

I found a similar closed issue regarding image upload problems with the GPT-4o model. The issue was resolved by upgrading to the latest version and clearing the browser's data and history. It was suggested that there might have been a bug related to the search and adding an online model not originally supported. Additionally, refreshing the model list in the settings allowed the user to upload images again <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2497)</sup>.

In your case, the error message indicates that the context length exceeded the model's maximum limit of 128,000 tokens. This could be due to the way images are being uploaded as byte streams, which might be inflating the token count. You might want to check if the image is being converted to base64 format before sending it to the OpenAI API, as this is the method used in the lobe-chat framework <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/ollama/index.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/google/index.ts)</sup>.

To address the issue, consider the following steps:
1. Ensure that the image is being converted to base64 format before uploading.
2. Check if there are any recent updates or changes in the codebase related to image processing that might affect this behavior <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup>.
3. Try reducing the image size or resolution to see if it helps in staying within the context length limit.

These steps might help in resolving the issue with image uploads exceeding the context length.

I found some relevant information regarding the issues you're experiencing with the Gemini function calls in Lobe Chat.

1. **400 Bad Request Error**: This error might be due to an invalid JSON payload. The error message suggests that the JSON payload contains fields that are not supported by the Gemini model, such as `maxItems`, `minItems`, and `default`. This indicates that the schema used in the function call might not be compatible with the Gemini model's expectations <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/tools-calling/google.mdx)</sup>.

2. **500 Internal Server Error**: This could be related to the poor tool-calling capability of the Gemini models. It is recommended not to enable plugins for Gemini due to these limitations <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/tools-calling/google.mdx)</sup>.

Additionally, there is a known issue where the Gemini model returns an incorrect plugin name in the JSON output, which prevents LobeChat from recognizing the plugin. This could also contribute to the errors you're encountering <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/tools-calling/google.mdx)</sup>.

To address these issues, you might consider disabling plugins for the Gemini model, as this has been suggested as a workaround in similar cases <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3251)</sup>.
