I don’t think this makes any sense, does it? Its applicable scenario is generally a single-function chat robot, such as a company's customer service, which needs to call the API multiple times in a short period of time, and the prompts for multiple calls have the same prefix.
This project is generally for personal use. Although different assistants have different built-in system prompts, (1) the user may not call the assistant frequently within 5 minutes; (2) the system prompts can be changed.
If every chat is written to the cache but misses within 5 minutes, the overall cost will increase by 25%
Anthropic supports up to 4 cache control points. Allowing users to choose where to insert cache control points will disproportionately increase the user's understanding cost, because other model servers do not support hint caching, or support it in a very different way.

body:
Need this too.
场景：
1. 测试Prompt的时候需要，需要5分钟内频繁使用相同Prompt。
2. 解决复杂（或创造性强）问题的过程中，同一个问题我会让Sonnet回答多次，为了：
（1）多个llm的回答帮助我从多方面思考
（2）减少幻觉负面影响
（3）长对话过程中（这里的长指的是单轮对话的输入或llm的输出长度），节省成本。


**另外，即使没有上述情境，只要用户要多轮对话，那就会节省成本**：
第二轮对话的时候把第一轮对话按cache_control提交，那么在第三轮对话的时候，前第一轮对话就可以hit cach ，第二轮对话内容write cach。
依次类推：第N轮对话的时候 1到N-2 轮的对话内容都可以hit cach，第N-1轮对话write cach。
成本会大幅下降。
以上是建立在claude的cach逻辑上的，即按message块去缓存。

Need this too.
Scenario:
1. When testing prompts, you need to use the same prompt frequently within 5 minutes.
2. In the process of solving complex (or creative) problems, I will ask Sonnet to answer the same question multiple times in order to:
(1) Multiple llm’s answers helped me think from many aspects
(2) Reduce the negative impact of hallucinations
(3) During long conversations (long here refers to the input length of a single round of conversation or the output length of llm), costs are saved.


**In addition, even if there is no above situation, as long as the user has multiple rounds of dialogue, it will save costs**:
In the second round of dialogue, submit the first round of dialogue according to cache_control. Then in the third round of dialogue, the previous first round of dialogue can be hit cach, and the content of the second round of dialogue can be write cach.
And so on: in the Nth round of dialogue, the dialogue content of rounds 1 to N-2 can be hit cach, and the N-1st round of dialogue can be write cach.
Costs will drop significantly.
The above is based on claude's cache logic, that is, caching according to message blocks.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The error `ERR_JWT_EXPIRED` indicates that the JWT token has expired. In the Lobe Chat framework, the expiration time for JWT tokens is set to 100 seconds after they are issued <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/jwt.ts)</sup>. This means that if the token is not refreshed or renewed within this time frame, it will expire, leading to the error you're encountering.

To resolve this issue, you can consider the following steps:

1. **Token Renewal**: Implement a mechanism to refresh the JWT token before it expires. This typically involves setting up a refresh token system or re-authenticating the user to issue a new token.

2. **Increase Expiration Time**: If appropriate for your use case, you can increase the expiration time of the JWT token by modifying the `duration` variable in the `createJWT` function within the `src/utils/jwt.ts` file. This will give users more time before the token expires <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/jwt.ts)</sup>.

3. **Check System Time**: Ensure that the system time on your server and client is synchronized. Discrepancies in system time can lead to premature expiration of tokens.

4. **Inspect Token Handling**: Verify that the token is being correctly stored and sent with requests. If the token is missing or not included in requests, it may lead to authentication failures.

If you need further assistance with implementing these changes, feel free to ask!

@echo off

w32tm /resync

w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:"time.windows.com" /syncfromflags:manual /reliable:yes /update
w32tm /resync

pause
```
执行完毕后，可以正常使用了

To resolve the issue of Vercel not being able to automatically upgrade after forking a repository, follow these steps:

1. **Delete the Original Repository**: If you initially deployed the project without forking, delete that deployment.

2. **Fork the Original Project**: Use the <kbd>Fork</kbd> button on the original project's GitHub page to create a fork.

3. **Redeploy on Vercel**: Deploy the forked repository on Vercel.

4. **Enable GitHub Actions**: After forking, manually enable Workflows on the Actions page of your forked project and start the Upstream Sync Action.

5. **Manual Sync if Needed**: If you encounter a sync failure, manually click "Update Branch" once.

These steps should help resolve errors like "The provided GitHub repository can't be found" or "The provided GitHub repository does not contain the requested branch or commit reference" by ensuring that Vercel is correctly linked to a forked repository with enabled workflows <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/upstream-sync.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @nova-mindcorp! I'm here to help you out with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's get this issue sorted out together.

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issue of Lobe Chat displaying responses in a tiny font and window, you can check the following configurations:

1. **Font Size and Window Size Configuration**: The font size and window size for chat responses are defined in the `src/const/layoutTokens.ts` file. You can adjust the constants like `CHAT_PORTAL_WIDTH`, `CHAT_PORTAL_MAX_WIDTH`, and `CHAT_PORTAL_TOOL_UI_WIDTH` to modify the window size. The font size is dynamically set using the `useUserStore` hook and `userGeneralSettingsSelectors.fontSize` in the `src/features/PluginsUI/Render/MarkdownType/index.tsx` file <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/const/layoutTokens.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/PluginsUI/Render/MarkdownType/index.tsx)</sup>.

2. **User Settings for Appearance**: Lobe Chat allows customization of chat response appearance through user settings. You can switch between light and dark modes, customize theme colors, and choose between conversation bubble and document modes for chat scenes. These settings might help in adjusting the appearance to your preference <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/features/theme.mdx)</sup>.

3. **Rendering Process**: The initial tiny response followed by a larger one might be due to the streaming nature of the response rendering. The `fetchSSE` method processes data chunks incrementally, which can cause the initial small display before the full response is rendered <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/contributing/Basic/Chat-API.md)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/chat/slices/aiChat/actions/generateAIChat.ts)</sup>.

By adjusting these settings, you should be able to achieve a more readable and appropriately sized chat response display.

I found a similar closed issue that might help you resolve the problem. The issue was related to an "Access Denied" error when accessing the S3 bucket, which could be due to several reasons:

1. **Incorrect Access Keys**: Ensure that `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are correctly configured.
2. **Bucket Policy**: Verify that the bucket policy allows the necessary actions, such as `s3:GetObject` for the specific resource path.
3. **Public Access Domain**: Make sure the `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` is publicly accessible and allows cross-origin requests if needed.
4. **Endpoint Configuration**: Check that `S3_ENDPOINT` is correctly set without any suffix path.
5. **ACL Settings**: If `S3_SET_ACL` is set to `public-read`, ensure the service provider supports it, or set it to `0` if not supported.

Review these configurations to resolve the access issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4291)</sup>.

@retaw106 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助你解决bug，回答问题，并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的过程中帮助你。

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar issue related to voice input not working under certain conditions. In a previous discussion, it was noted that using HTTP instead of HTTPS might cause issues with voice input due to browser restrictions. Switching to HTTPS could potentially resolve the problem <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3249)</sup>.

Regarding the 'terminated' `TypeError`, this might occur if there is an attempt to access properties or methods on a `null` or `undefined` object. This could happen if the WebSocket provider or its associated objects are not properly initialized or have been destroyed. Ensure that the WebSocket connections are correctly set up and that any cleanup logic does not prematurely destroy necessary resources <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/client/core/sync.ts)</sup>.

For further troubleshooting, you might want to check if there are any specific configurations or dependencies related to voice input that might not be compatible with Firefox or Android browsers, as this information wasn't directly available in the repository.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello, @BravoDD44! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you may have. Let's tackle this issue together!

<!-- Answer -->
The login error you're experiencing when accessing the knowledge base after deploying the server database version using Docker is likely due to the authentication setup. Here are some relevant discussions and solutions:

1. **Authentication Service Limitation**: The official documentation notes that you cannot use Clerk as an authentication service when deploying LobeChat using Docker or Docker Compose due to the inability to expose `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` using Docker environment variables. If you're using Clerk, consider switching to another authentication provider or deployment method, such as Vercel, or building your own Docker image <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Alternative Authentication Setup**: The documentation suggests using Casdoor as a local authentication service when deploying with Docker Compose. Ensure that Casdoor is configured correctly according to the instructions provided in the documentation <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker.mdx)</sup>.

3. **Similar Issues**: There are similar discussions about login issues and Docker deployments:
   - A closed issue where using the localhost version of Docker Compose resulted in login errors. The solution involved using specific configuration files for Docker Compose <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3664)</sup>.
   - An unsolved discussion about redirect/unknown-session errors when using Docker Compose for LobeChat <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4518)</sup>.

Make sure your environment variables and authentication settings are correctly configured. If you're using Auth0, verify that the callback URLs and other settings are correctly set up in your Auth0 dashboard.


<!-- Dosu Comment Footer -->

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @mrshu! 👋 I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have while waiting for a human maintainer. Let's squash those bugs together!

<!-- Answer -->
The error "unable to find user nextjs: no matching entries in passwd file" suggests that the 'nextjs' user is not being created or recognized in the Docker environment. This user is supposed to be created in the Dockerfile for Lobe Chat to run the application with a non-root user for security reasons.

To troubleshoot this issue, ensure that the Dockerfile includes the necessary steps to create the 'nextjs' user. The relevant section should look like this:

```dockerfile
RUN \
    # Add nextjs:nodejs to run the app
    addgroup -S -g 1001 nodejs \
    && adduser -D -G nodejs -H -S -h /app -u 1001 nextjs \
    # Set permission for nextjs:nodejs
    && chown -R nextjs:nodejs /app /etc/proxychains4.conf
```

Additionally, verify that the Docker Compose file includes the instruction `USER nextjs` to specify that the container should run as the 'nextjs' user <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/Dockerfile)</sup>.

If these steps are already in place, try rebuilding the Docker image to ensure that all changes are applied correctly.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello, @kindmesdilabso! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let me know how I can assist you with the issue you've posted.

<!-- Answer -->
I couldn't find any specific section in the codebase where the `ctrl + alt + backspace` hotkey is defined or handled, nor any event listeners or handlers that might interfere with it <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/287)</sup>. Additionally, there is no documentation or comments regarding potential conflicts with system processes for hotkeys like `csrss.exe` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/287)</sup>.

However, there is a fallback mechanism for clearing the current session if the hotkey fails. The `clearSessions` method in the `SessionAction` interface can be used to reset sessions to default. This method is triggered in the user interface by a button, which can be used as an alternative to manually clear the sessions <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/session/slices/session/action.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/settings/common/features/Common.tsx)</sup>.

If the hotkey conflict persists, you might consider customizing the hotkeys. The hotkeys are defined in the `src/const/hotkeys.ts` file, which allows for customization of hotkeys such as `regenerate`, `saveTopic`, and `zenMode` <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/const/hotkeys.ts)</sup>.

Hello @Jazzy96! I'm here to assist you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Feel free to reach out while we wait for a human maintainer.

<!-- Answer -->
这个问题可能与 `LobeArtifact` 模块中的 `Render` 组件的逻辑有关。具体来说，只有第一个 artifact 正常显示，而第二个和第三个以纯文本形式显示，可能是因为以下条件未满足：

1. `isGenerating` 状态对于这些 artifacts 不是 `true`。
2. `hasChildren` 条件不满足，即 artifacts 没有内容可显示。
3. `isArtifactTagClosed` 状态为 `true`，表示 artifact 标签被认为是关闭的。

要解决这个问题，您需要确保所有要显示的 artifacts 的 UI 打开条件正确设置。这可能需要检查状态管理逻辑，以确保 `isGenerating`、`hasChildren` 和 `isArtifactTagClosed` 状态为每个 artifact 正确更新。此外，确保 `openArtifactUI` 函数为每个 artifact 适当触发<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/components/MarkdownElements/LobeArtifact/Render/index.tsx)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey there, @ggatesdew! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's tackle this issue together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the "Auto Generate" feature outputting in Chinese instead of the user's preferred language might be related to how the language preference is being detected or applied. Here are a few areas to investigate:

1. **Language Detection and Preference**: Ensure that the language detection mechanism is correctly identifying and applying the user's language preference. The application uses the `createI18nNext` function with the `i18next` library and `LanguageDetector` plugin to determine the user's language preference, which is stored in cookies <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/helpers.ts)</sup>.

2. **Fallback Mechanism**: Check if the fallback mechanism is inadvertently defaulting to Chinese. The system should fall back to a default language if the preferred language is not available. This default is determined by the `DEFAULT_LANG` constant, which should be set correctly to avoid unexpected language outputs <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/translation.ts)</sup>.

3. **Translation Files**: Verify that the translation files for the preferred language (e.g., English) are complete and correctly configured. Any discrepancies in these files could lead to incorrect language output.

4. **Code Logic**: Review the logic in the `AutoGenerateInput.tsx` file to ensure that the translation function `t` is being used correctly to fetch the appropriate language strings <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/AgentSetting/AgentMeta/AutoGenerateInput.tsx)</sup>.

By checking these areas, you might identify the root cause of the issue. If the problem persists, consider reviewing recent changes in the codebase that might have affected language handling.

To resolve the error "column 'accessed_at' does not exist" after updating to version v1.28.3, ensure that the database migrations have been applied correctly. Follow these steps:

1. **Check Migration Status**: Verify that the migration script `0010_add_accessed_at_and_clean_tables.sql` has been executed. Check the migration status in your database to confirm if this specific migration has been applied.

2. **Apply Migrations**: If the migration has not been applied, run the migration command to apply it. This will add the `accessed_at` column to the necessary tables.

3. **Verify Database Schema**: After applying the migration, ensure that the `accessed_at` column exists in the tables mentioned in the migration script.

If the migration script is correctly applied, the error should be resolved. If issues persist, check your database connection and migration setup in your CI environment on Vercel <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/server/migrations/0010_add_accessed_at_and_clean_tables.sql)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
@sunshinexiaozhu 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个能够帮助你解决错误、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。在等待人类维护者的过程中，我将竭诚为您服务。

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar issue related to the 'TypeError: fetch failed' error in the Lobe Chat codebase. This error is often associated with network issues, incorrect URLs, or certificate verification problems, especially when using a proxy server. The error message typically includes a cause with the code 'UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE' <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/faq/proxy-with-unable-to-verify-leaf-signature.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

Here are some steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Check Network Configuration**: Ensure that your network settings are correct and that there are no connectivity issues between your server and the external services it needs to access.

2. **Verify URLs**: Double-check the URLs used in your configuration files to ensure they are correct and accessible.

3. **Certificate Verification**: If you are using a proxy server, make sure that the certificates are correctly configured and trusted by your system. You might need to add the certificate to your trusted store if it's self-signed.

4. **Nginx Configuration**: Review your Nginx configuration to ensure it is correctly set up as a reverse proxy for the services. You can refer to the recommended Nginx setup for Lobe Chat when using a domain name <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose.mdx)</sup>.

5. **Logs and Error Messages**: Check the detailed logs for any additional error messages that might provide more context on the failure.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider looking into similar discussions or issues for additional insights.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello, @coulsontl! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's tackle this together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the historical range separator line being displayed even when the limit for historical messages is not reached is likely due to the logic that controls its visibility. The separator line is displayed based on the `enable` prop. If this prop is set to `true`, the separator line will be rendered regardless of the number of messages <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/components/History/HistoryDivider.tsx)</sup>.

To address this, you could modify the logic to only display the separator line when the number of messages exceeds the set limit for summarization. This would provide a clearer signal to users that summarization will occur.

Regarding the automatic summarization not being disabled despite changing the settings, ensure that the `"enableCompressHistory"` setting is correctly configured in the `locales/en-US/setting.json` file. This setting controls whether the automatic summarization feature is enabled or disabled <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/locales/en-US/setting.json)</sup>. If the setting is correctly configured and the issue persists, there might be a bug in the implementation that needs further investigation.

To address the "CheckExpectedDim" error, consider the following steps:

1. **Verify Input Dimensions**: Ensure that the input data being processed matches the expected dimensions required by the embedding function. This might involve checking the data preprocessing steps to ensure consistency.

2. **Check Configuration**: Review any configuration settings related to embeddings or vector operations to ensure they are correctly set up for your specific use case.

3. **Debugging**: Use the `node --trace-warnings` command to trace where the warning about duplicate labels for `console.time()` is being generated. This might help identify any logical errors in the code that could be contributing to the issue.

4. **Review Code**: Look into the `vector.c` file around line 72 to understand what the `CheckExpectedDim` routine is doing and why it might be failing.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, further investigation into the specific implementation details of the embedding process in your environment may be necessary.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing, where the assistant settings reset when creating the first message, might be related to how the settings are managed and persisted in the application. The function `handleReset` is responsible for resetting assistant settings, which might be inadvertently triggered during the process of creating a new message <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/settings/common/features/Common.tsx)</sup>.

Additionally, there have been recent changes in the codebase that could affect the persistence of settings, such as the `upgradeToV11` function, which modifies user settings during a migration <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/client/core/db.ts)</sup>. This could potentially impact how settings are saved and retrieved.

Hey @wjsoj! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's work together to solve this issue.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the `EditableMessage` component in the Assistant chat interface seems to be related to how the `defaultValue` is handled in the `MessageInput` component. The current implementation retains the previous value, which causes the input box to not reflect the updated content after a second edit.

Here are a couple of potential solutions:

1. **Modify the `EditableMessage` Component:**
   - You could add a unique `key` prop to the `EditableMessage` component in the `SystemRoleContent.tsx` file. This would force a re-render of the component whenever the key changes, ensuring that the input box displays the updated content. However, this approach might cause the modal to flicker, which could affect the user experience.

2. **Update the `MessageInput` Component:**
   - Another approach is to modify the `MessageInput` component in the `lobe-ui` library to listen for changes to the `defaultValue` prop. This would involve updating the state whenever `defaultValue` changes, ensuring that the input box reflects the latest content. While this solution might add complexity to the UI component, it would provide a more seamless user experience.

Both solutions have their trade-offs, and the best approach depends on the desired user experience and the complexity you're willing to introduce into the codebase. If you're comfortable with the potential flicker, the first solution might be simpler to implement. Otherwise, updating the `MessageInput` component to handle `defaultValue` changes could provide a more robust solution.

It's possible that these changes have affected the search functionality.

Ensure that the `displayTopics` selector is correctly handling the search state and displaying the appropriate results <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/chat/slices/topic/selectors.ts)</sup>. <!-- Answer -->
To change the port from 9000 to 9010 for the `lobe-network` in your Docker deployment, you need to modify the `docker-compose.yml` file. Specifically, update the port mapping for the `network-service` and the `minio` service. Here is how you can do it:

1. Update the `ports` section for the `network-service`:
   ```yaml
   services:
     network-service:
       ...
       ports:
         - '9010:9010' # MinIO API
         - '9001:9001' # MinIO Console
         - '${CASDOOR_PORT}:${CASDOOR_PORT}' # Casdoor
         - '${LOBE_PORT}:3210' # LobeChat
       ...
   ```

2. Update the `command` for the `minio` service to use the new port:
   ```yaml
   minio:
     ...
     command: >
       server /etc/minio/data --address ":9010" --console-address ":9001"
   ```

3. Ensure that the environment variable `MINIO_PORT` is set to `9010` in your `.env` file or directly in the `docker-compose.yml` file:
   ```yaml
   environment:
     - 'MINIO_PORT=9010'
   ```

These changes will map the external port 9010 to the internal port 9010 for the MinIO API, resolving the port conflict <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/zitadel/docker-compose.yml)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

To resolve the issue where the user avatar does not update on `lobe.example.cn` after changing it in Casdoor, despite Casdoor's API returning the correct avatar information, you should ensure that the `profile` function in the `LobeCasdoorProvider` is correctly mapping the avatar URL from Casdoor to the `image` field used by the application.

Here's the relevant code snippet:

```typescript
profile(profile) {
  return {
    email: profile.email,
    emailVerified: profile.emailVerified ? new Date() : null,
    id: profile.id,
    image: profile.avatar, // Ensure this is correctly set
    name: profile.displayName ?? profile.firstName ?? profile.lastName,
    providerAccountId: profile.id,
  };
}
```

Make sure that `profile.avatar` contains the updated avatar URL and that this value is being used wherever the avatar is displayed in the application. If the avatar is still not updating, check if there is any caching mechanism in place that might be serving an outdated image <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/next-auth/sso-providers/casdoor.ts)</sup>.

1. **Session Management**: Ensure that the session is being properly invalidated upon logout. This might involve clearing cookies or local storage where session tokens are stored.

2. **Auth0 Logout URL**: Make sure that the logout process is correctly configured to call the Auth0 logout endpoint. This endpoint should clear the session on the Auth0 side.

3. **Browser Cache**: Sometimes, browser caching can cause issues with session persistence. Try clearing the browser cache or testing in an incognito window to see if the issue persists.

4. **Single Sign-On (SSO)**: If SSO is enabled, the behavior you're seeing might be expected, as SSO can automatically log users back in without prompting for credentials.

5. **Application Configuration**: Double-check the application configuration to ensure that all necessary settings for logout are correctly implemented.

Hey there, @ilovelxy! 👋 I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions while you wait for a human maintainer. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar issue that might be related to the problem you're experiencing. The issue titled "[Bug] docker部署时next-auth不可用" was closed and suggested configuring the `NEXTAUTH_URL` variable according to the documentation <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2881)</sup>.

For your specific issue with the `client_id=undefined` error, ensure that your `.env` file is correctly configured with the necessary environment variables. Here are the steps you should follow:

1. **Check Environment Variables:**
   - Ensure that `AUTH_GITHUB_ID` and `AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET` are correctly set in your `.env` file. These should be the Client ID and Client Secret from your GitHub OAuth application.
   - Verify that `NEXTAUTH_URL` is set to the correct callback URL, which should match the one configured in your GitHub app (`http://localhost:3210/api/auth/callback/github`).

2. **GitHub OAuth Application Configuration:**
   - Double-check that the callback URL in your GitHub OAuth application settings matches the `NEXTAUTH_URL` in your `.env` file.

3. **Generate a Secret:**
   - Make sure `NEXT_AUTH_SECRET` is set. You can generate a secret using a command like `openssl rand -base64 32`.

These steps should help resolve the `client_id=undefined` error and the 404 page issue after logging in. If the problem persists, ensure that all environment variables are correctly loaded in your Docker setup.

callback不一定必须是公网能访问的地址。一般来说，oauth提供商要求的callback url的作用是，限定在oauth登录完成后，重定向到的URL，也就是登录之后跳转到哪里。跳转是在客户端执行的，只要客户端可以访问该URL即可。

HTTP 404说明服务器找不到该页面。如果404是LobeChat给出的，说明LobeChat中不存在该路径。如果404是其他服务给出的，说明Callback URL填写错误，定向到了非LobeChat的网页。

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello, @YiyangLu! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's work together to solve this issue.

<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering, "SignatureDoesNotMatch," typically indicates an issue with the signature calculation for the S3 request. This can happen if the signing method or the parameters used for generating the signature are not compatible with the specific S3 provider, in this case, bitiful.com.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Verify Credentials**: Double-check that the access key and secret key are correct and have the necessary permissions for the operations you're trying to perform.

2. **Check Endpoint Configuration**: Ensure that the endpoint URL is correctly configured for bitiful.com. Different S3-compatible providers might have different endpoint formats.

3. **Review Signature Version**: Some S3-compatible providers may require a specific signature version (e.g., v2 or v4). Verify if bitiful.com requires a specific version and ensure your configuration matches this requirement.

4. **Path vs. Virtual Hosted Style**: Check if bitiful.com requires path-style or virtual-hosted-style URLs and configure your requests accordingly.

5. **Custom Signing Method**: If bitiful.com has specific requirements for signing requests, you might need to implement a custom signing method. Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific documentation in the Lobe Chat framework for custom signing methods, so you may need to refer to bitiful.com's documentation for guidance.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to consult bitiful.com's documentation or support for more specific guidance on their S3 implementation.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey, @claudehotline! I'm Dosu, and I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's tackle this issue together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with file upload failures in Lobe Chat when using MinIO seems to be related to DNS resolution errors, specifically the `ENOTFOUND` error for the hostname `lobechat.claudextxo.top`. This error indicates that the DNS server is unable to resolve the specified hostname.

Here are some steps and considerations that might help resolve this issue:

1. **Check DNS Configuration**: Ensure that your DNS settings are correctly configured. The DNS server specified (`192.168.50.2`) should be able to resolve the hostname `lobechat.claudextxo.top`. You might want to verify that this DNS server is operational and correctly configured.

2. **Verify Hostname**: Double-check the hostname `lobechat.claudextxo.top` to ensure it is correct and accessible. You can try pinging this hostname from your server to see if it resolves correctly.

3. **Network Configuration**: Ensure that your network settings allow for proper DNS resolution. This includes checking firewall settings, network routes, and any proxy configurations that might interfere with DNS queries.

4. **MinIO and Lobe Chat Configuration**: Make sure that the configurations for MinIO and Lobe Chat are correctly set up, especially the environment variables related to S3 and MinIO. This includes `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_BUCKET`, and any authentication keys.

5. **Internal Authentication**: If you have internal authentication mechanisms enabled, such as Clerk or NextAuth, ensure that they are not interfering with the server's ability to make RPC calls. Proper authentication headers or tokens might be required for these calls to succeed <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/const/auth.ts)</sup>.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might want to look into similar issues that have been reported and resolved. For instance, there were issues related to file chunking errors that were resolved by configuring the `APP_URL` to ensure the server could access it directly, even with authentication layers in place <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3573)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3545)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion and issue related to Microsoft Entra ID errors in Lobe Chat:

1. A similar discussion titled "Problem Of Microsoft Entra ID :在zeabur平台上使用docker部署服务端数据库版本时使用Microsoft Entra ID部署时回调地址无响应" was resolved by correcting a domain error <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3420)</sup>.
2. A closed issue titled "[Bug] Microsoft Entra ID 身份验证服务报错" was resolved by addressing a Docker image problem <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3388)</sup>.

For your specific issue with the AADSTS50011 error, here are some troubleshooting steps you can follow:

1. **Ensure Correct Redirect URI**: Double-check that the redirect URI in your Microsoft Entra ID application matches exactly with the one specified in your `lobe-chat.env` file. It should be set to `https://your-domain/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id` if that's the path your application uses <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/microsoft-entra-id.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Modify Redirect URIs**: If you haven't already, modify the Redirect URIs in the Microsoft Entra ID app registration to include the exact URI shown in the error message. This is crucial for resolving redirect URI mismatches <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/microsoft-entra-id.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

3. **Check Environment Variables**: Ensure that all environment variables in your `lobe-chat.env` file are correctly set, especially `NEXTAUTH_URL`, which should match the callback URL configured in your Microsoft Entra ID settings <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/microsoft-entra-id.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

4. **Add Users**: Adding "LobeChat" as an owner in the Microsoft Entra ID app registration is not typically necessary for resolving redirect URI issues. Focus on ensuring that the redirect URIs and environment variables are correctly configured.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the redirect URI mismatch error. If the issue persists, consider reviewing the Microsoft documentation for additional troubleshooting tips.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey there, @ilovefreesw! I'm here to help you with bug fixes, answer your questions, and guide you on your journey to becoming a contributor. Let's tackle this issue together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar unsolved discussion titled "[Getting Error After Deploying Private Agent Market](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4705)" which might be related to the issue you're experiencing <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4705)</sup>. 

The error you're encountering, "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'category')", suggests that the 'category' property is not being defined or accessed correctly in the agent object. This could be due to a mismatch in the expected structure of the agent object or an issue with how the data is being fetched or processed.

To troubleshoot, you might want to check the following:

1. Ensure that the `AGENTS_INDEX_URL` is correctly set and accessible. This environment variable is crucial for setting the base URL for accessing agent data <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/modules/AssistantStore/index.ts)</sup>.

2. Verify the structure of the agent object being returned from your Vercel deployment. Make sure that the 'category' property is included and correctly defined.

3. Review the code handling the agent click event to ensure it properly checks for undefined properties and handles them gracefully. The code includes checks for certain properties like `activeAgentId`, but you might need to add similar checks for 'category' <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/agent/slices/chat/action.ts)</sup>.

If these steps don't resolve the issue, consider looking into the agent object structure and how it's being processed in the codebase.

It's possible that the data isn't being properly saved or restored after hibernation due to how these storage mechanisms are managed during system power state changes.

Unfortunately, there isn't specific information available about handling system events like hibernation in the repository. However, you might want to check if there are any browser settings or extensions that could be affecting data persistence. Additionally, ensuring that the browser and the application are up to date might help resolve the issue.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @anphex! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have regarding lobechat-database-docker. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
It seems like you're encountering a network connectivity issue between the Casdoor and LobeChat containers and the Postgres database. This type of error often indicates that the containers are unable to communicate over the network, which could be due to several reasons such as network misconfiguration or firewall settings.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Check Docker Network Configuration**: Ensure that all your containers are on the same Docker network. The default network configuration for the Docker Compose setup in the lobe-chat repository uses a custom network named `lobe-network` with the `bridge` driver <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup>. Verify that your containers are connected to this network.

2. **Verify Container Health**: Make sure that the Postgres container is healthy and running. You can check the status of your containers using `docker ps` and inspect the logs of the Postgres container for any errors using `docker logs <container_id>`.

3. **Firewall Settings**: Ensure that there are no firewall rules blocking the communication between the containers. A similar issue was resolved by opening the necessary ports in the firewall <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4539)</sup>.

4. **Service Dependencies**: Check the `depends_on` configuration in your Docker Compose file to ensure that services start in the correct order. The `postgresql` service should be healthy before other services like Casdoor and LobeChat attempt to connect to it <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

5. **Network Connectivity**: You can test the network connectivity between containers using Docker's `exec` command to run network tools like `ping` or `telnet` from one container to another.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might want to review the Docker Compose file and any custom configurations you have applied to ensure they align with the expected setup.

body:
I just want to add my solution for anyone trying to Deploy it on a Virtualmin Managed Server. I do not remember changing any config related to FirewallD and docker, so I think the flaw is by design from Virtualmin. Here is the solution achieved with the help of Claude Sonnet 3.5 November edition:

> The core issue was a conflict between Docker's network management and firewalld zones. Here's what happened:
> 
> The main error was:
> 
> CopyFailed to program NAT chain: ZONE_CONFLICT: 'docker0' already bound to 'trusted'
> The problem occurred because:
> 
> Docker manages its own networking and creates its own firewall rules
> We had accidentally assigned the docker0 interface to the trusted zone in firewalld
> This created a conflict because the same network interface (docker0) was being managed by two different systems
> 
> It's like having two traffic cops trying to direct traffic at the same intersection - they'll conflict with each other!
> The fix involved:
> 
> Removing the docker0 interface from the trusted zone
> Cleaning up the Docker network configurations
> Letting Docker manage its own networking through its default docker zone
> 
> Best practices going forward:
> 
> Let Docker manage its own networking through the docker zone
> Don't manually assign Docker's interfaces to other firewalld zones
> If you need to add specific rules, add them to the docker zone rather than trusted
> 
> This is why it started working on the clean test network we created - it didn't have any conflicting zone assignments. The solution ensured that only one system (Docker) was managing the container networking, removing the conflict.

body:
> **终于搞定了！！折腾了一周多** _实现了casdoor 替代logto，用域名访问lobe服务器版，一切正常使用。反代使用的nginx proxy manager。_ 简单说下如何配置： casdoor部分的代码参考这个[#4080 (comment)](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4080#issuecomment-2367372987) 按照https://lobehub.com/zh/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose 里的【发布到生产（IP 模式）】流程。把docker-compose.yml里的logto部分换成casdoor，再把里面的本地IP全部换成域名即可。
> 
> 我的主要问题是443端口不能用，使用的非443，所以遇到了上传不了文件，查看不了存储桶之类的问题。现在才发现是因为https对应wss,而wss必须使用443端口。基本上所有的教程都是默认域名后缀就是443，所以照猫画虎始终搞不定。 因此核心的要素在这里，针对minio的9001和9000的两个域名，nginx proxy manager的advanced里面要填入以下内容：
> 
> location / { proxy_pass http://192.168.18.1:9000; #填入docker 宿主机本地地址, api的就是9000, UI的就是9001 proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $http_host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; }
> 
> 然后就可以了！

非常感谢 按照您说的解决了这个问题

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issue with Microsoft Entra ID authentication not working correctly in your LobeChat setup, here are some steps and considerations based on similar discussions and configurations:

1. **Ensure Correct Environment Variables:**
   - Make sure that the `APP_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, and `PROXY_URL` (if used) are set correctly. They should all point to your domain, ensuring consistency. For example:
     ```bash
     APP_URL=https://your-domain/
     NEXTAUTH_URL=https://your-domain/api/auth
     ```

2. **Nginx Configuration:**
   - Your Nginx configuration seems mostly correct, but ensure that the `proxy_set_header` directives are properly set to forward headers correctly. You might want to add or adjust:
     ```nginx
     proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
     proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
     proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port $server_port;
     ```

3. **Check Microsoft Entra ID Setup:**
   - Verify that the Redirect URI in your Microsoft Entra ID application matches exactly with `https://your-domain/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id`.
   - Ensure that the Client ID, Client Secret, and Tenant ID are correctly set in your environment variables.

4. **Session Management:**
   - If the session is not showing the user as logged in, it might be related to how sessions are managed or cookies are set. Ensure that your domain settings allow cookies to be set and that there are no issues with cross-domain cookies.

5. **Docker Logs and Debugging:**
   - Since the Docker logs show no errors, consider increasing the verbosity of the logs if possible to capture more detailed information about the authentication process.

6. **Example Configuration:**
   - For a generic use case, ensure that all URLs and domain names are consistent across your configuration files and environment variables. This consistency is crucial for the authentication flow to work correctly.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might want to look into any specific error messages or logs from the browser's developer console during the authentication process, as they can provide more insights into what might be going wrong.

- `curl -v https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration` and switch the <tenant id> to your tenant id.

<!-- Answer -->
I couldn't find specific information about changes in version v1.32.4 that might have affected the default settings for the history message count limit. However, there are similar issues that have been discussed previously. For instance, there was a request to set environment variables for limiting the history message count and enabling history message length compression threshold. The solution was to use the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` environment variable with a configuration like `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG="enableHistoryCount=true;historyCount=13;enableCompressThreshold=true;compressThreshold=8"` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1717)</sup>.

If the default setting for the history message count has changed in v1.32.4, you might need to manually adjust it using the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` environment variable to suit your preferences.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
@Shukino20001015 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助解决错误、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在这里帮助你等待人类维护者的过程中。

<!-- Answer -->
I found some similar discussions that might help with your issue:

1. **[Bug] Docker Compose部署无法使用**: This discussion was resolved by addressing a firewall issue. The user initially couldn't log in due to a firewall problem, which was resolved by opening the necessary port <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4539)</sup>.

2. **LobeChat 因授权问题无法连接至MinIO服务器**: This discussion highlights the importance of having a login system configured, as the lack of it can lead to authorization failures <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4137)</sup>.

3. **[Bug] next-auth fetch failed with third auth provider**: This issue was resolved by using a `PROXY_URL`, which might be relevant if you're encountering fetch errors with NextAuth <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3847)</sup>.

Regarding your specific issue with Casdoor configuration not persisting across service restarts, I couldn't find a direct solution in the available data. However, ensuring that your Docker volumes are correctly set up to persist data might help. This typically involves checking your Docker Compose configuration to ensure that volumes are mapped correctly for Casdoor's data storage.

For the NextAuth configuration error, make sure all required environment variables are correctly set. You can refer to the specific environment variables needed for NextAuth in the Lobe Chat setup <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/production/logto/.env.example)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/zitadel/.env.example)</sup><sup>[[6]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/auth.mdx)</sup>.

If the Casdoor configuration reset is causing the authentication failure, ensuring persistent storage for Casdoor's configuration might resolve the issue. You might need to check if the Casdoor service is writing its configuration to a persistent volume.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @Ziqi-Yang! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the image icon being in shadow gray and the inability to use the image/file attachment functionality, despite `Anthropic: Claude 3.5 Sonnet` being marked as supporting visual recognition, could be related to the conditions that control the image upload feature. The state of the image icon is controlled by the `canUploadImage` variable, which determines whether the image upload option is enabled or disabled. If `canUploadImage` is `false`, the image upload option is disabled, and the icon appears in shadow gray <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Upload/ServerMode.tsx)</sup>.

To troubleshoot this issue, you should check the following:

1. Ensure that the model is correctly configured to support vision capabilities. The `vision` property in the model configuration should be set to `true` for `Claude 3.5 Sonnet` <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/config/modelProviders/openrouter.ts)</sup>.

2. Verify that the `canUploadImage` variable is correctly set. This variable is determined by the `useUserStore` hook, which checks if the current model supports vision capabilities. If this hook is not returning the expected value, it might be causing the issue.

3. Double-check any recent changes or updates in the codebase that might affect the model's capabilities or the conditions for enabling the image upload feature.

If these checks do not resolve the issue, further investigation into the codebase or debugging logs might be necessary to identify any underlying problems.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @kaikanertan! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
The error "ProviderBizError: Incorrect API key provided" typically indicates an issue with the API key itself rather than the `XAI_PROXY_URL` environment variable. This error is generated when a 400 error status is encountered, specifically related to authentication errors with the API key <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/cloudflare/index.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/errorResponse.test.ts)</sup>.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot this issue:

1. **Verify the API Key**: Double-check that the API key you are using is correct and has not expired. Ensure there are no typos or formatting issues.

2. **Check Environment Variable Configuration**: Ensure that the `XAI_PROXY_URL` and other related environment variables are correctly set in your Docker environment. You can verify this by checking your `.env` file and ensuring it is correctly referenced in your Docker setup.

3. **Restart Docker Services**: After making changes to environment variables, restart your Docker services to ensure the new configurations are applied.

4. **Logs and Debugging**: Check the application logs for any additional error messages or clues that might indicate why the API key is being rejected.

If the issue persists after these checks, it might be helpful to review any recent changes in the environment variable handling or consult the documentation for any specific requirements related to the `XAI_PROXY_URL`.

I couldn't find specific information about troubleshooting TTS issues in the Lobe Chat repository. However, I can provide some general guidance based on the integration details of the TTS feature in Lobe Chat.

1. **Check Configuration**: Ensure that the TTS settings in the Lobe Chat application are correctly configured. You can do this by opening the `Settings` panel, navigating to the `Text-to-Speech` settings, and verifying that the correct speech service and AI model are selected.

2. **Dependencies**: Make sure that all necessary dependencies for the TTS feature are installed and compatible with your Docker and Windows environment. Although specific dependencies weren't listed, ensuring your environment is up-to-date can help.

3. **Logs and Errors**: Check the application logs for any error messages related to TTS. This might give you more insight into what might be going wrong.

4. **Docker Configuration**: Verify that your Docker setup is correctly configured to support audio processing, as this might affect the TTS functionality.

If these steps don't resolve the issue, you might want to look into the [similar discussion](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3249) about TTS issues, although it remains unsolved <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3249)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
在 Vercel 上遇到 TTS 功能问题时，您可以尝试以下步骤来排查问题：

1. **检查环境变量**：确保在 Vercel 上配置的环境变量正确无误，特别是与 TTS 服务相关的 API 密钥和配置。

2. **验证权限和认证**：根据错误信息，可能是由于权限不足或认证无效导致的。请检查您的认证设置，确保访问代码和 OAuth 配置正确无误。Lobe Chat 使用 `LOBE_CHAT_AUTH_HEADER` 和 `OAUTH_AUTHORIZED` 来处理认证，确保这些头信息在请求中正确设置<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(backend)/webapi/plugin/gateway/route.ts)</sup>。

3. **查看日志**：虽然您在 Vercel 上没有看到相关的错误日志，但可以尝试增加日志记录的详细程度，或者在本地环境中运行应用以捕获更多详细的错误信息。

4. **检查 TTS 服务配置**：确保在 Lobe Chat 的设置面板中选择了正确的 TTS 服务和语音选项。可以通过 `useTTS` 钩子来配置和选择 TTS 服务<sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/useTTS.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/AgentSetting/AgentTTS/index.tsx)</sup>。

如果这些步骤仍然无法解决问题，建议在本地环境中进行调试，以便更详细地查看错误信息和日志。这样可以帮助您更好地理解问题的根源。

<!-- Answer -->
在 Vercel 上配置 TTS 环境变量时，您需要确保以下几点：

1. **环境变量设置**：在 Vercel 的项目设置中，您可以添加环境变量。通常，TTS 服务需要 API 密钥或其他认证信息。虽然具体的环境变量名称和值可能因使用的 TTS 服务而异，但通常包括类似 `API_KEY` 或 `TTS_SERVICE_URL` 的变量。

2. **TTS 服务配置**：根据 Lobe Chat 的默认配置，TTS 服务使用的是 OpenAI。您可以在设置面板中确认 TTS 服务的选择和配置。默认配置如下：

   ```typescript
   export const DEFAUTT_AGENT_TTS_CONFIG: LobeAgentTTSConfig = {
     showAllLocaleVoice: false,
     sttLocale: 'auto',
     ttsService: 'openai',
     voice: {
       openai: 'alloy',
     },
   };
   ```

   确保在 Vercel 上配置的环境变量与此配置兼容<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/const/settings/agent.ts)</sup>.

3. **认证和权限**：确保在请求中正确设置了认证头信息，例如 `LOBE_CHAT_AUTH_HEADER` 和 `OAUTH_AUTHORIZED`，以便服务器能够正确处理请求。

如果您不确定需要哪些具体的环境变量，建议查看您所使用的 TTS 服务的官方文档，以获取详细的配置指南。这样可以确保您在 Vercel 上正确配置了所有必要的环境变量。

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello, @zsio! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let me know how I can assist you while we wait for a human maintainer. [Dosu](https://dosu.dev)

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issue of streaming not being supported for o1 models, you can modify the streaming parameter in the code. In the `LobeOpenAI` configuration, the `stream` parameter is set to `true` by default if it is not already defined. You can change this to disable streaming for o1 models.

Here's how you can do it:

1. Locate the `handlePayload` function in the `LobeOpenAI` configuration.
2. Modify the line where the `stream` parameter is set:

```typescript
export const LobeOpenAI = LobeOpenAICompatibleFactory({
  baseURL: 'https://api.openai.com/v1',
  chatCompletion: {
    handlePayload: (payload) => {
      const { model } = payload;

      if (o1Models.has(model)) {
        return pruneO1Payload(payload) as any;
      }

      // Change this line to disable streaming
      return { ...payload, stream: payload.stream ?? false };
    },
  },
  debug: {
    chatCompletion: () => process.env.DEBUG_OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETION === '1',
  },
  provider: ModelProvider.OpenAI,
});
```

By setting `stream: payload.stream ?? false`, you ensure that streaming is disabled for models that do not support it, such as the o1 models <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/openai/index.ts)</sup>.

To resolve this issue, you should verify and update the API endpoint configuration for the Qwen provider. Additionally, check if there are any environment variables that might be overriding the endpoint for Qwen. If you have set any such variables, make sure they point to the correct Qwen API endpoint.

If the issue persists, consider checking for any recent changes in the Lobe Chat database or configuration files that might have affected the Qwen API integration.

The error you're encountering, `unsupported_country_region_territory`, suggests that the API request is being blocked due to location restrictions. This is likely related to the endpoint configuration for the Qwen API.

In the Lobe Chat codebase, the Qwen API endpoint is configured using the `LobeQwenAI` class, where the default `baseURL` is set to `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts)</sup>. If the endpoint has changed to `https://api.openai.com/v1`, it might be due to a misconfiguration or an update that altered the endpoint settings.

To resolve this issue, you should verify the `baseURL` configuration in your setup. Ensure that the `baseURL` is correctly set to the intended Qwen API endpoint. If your host cannot directly access OpenAI, make sure the endpoint is set to the correct Qwen API URL that your environment supports.

Additionally, Lobe Chat handles errors related to unsupported locations by checking for a 403 status code and categorizing it under `LocationNotSupportError` <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.test.ts)</sup>. This indicates that the error handling mechanism is correctly identifying the issue as a location-based restriction.

> 基于类似于 ChatGPT 这样的消息编辑来进行分支对话似乎更好

基于消息编辑做分支会违背我们的基础设定（任何之前的上下文都可以自由修改和编辑），这个并不合理。

更合适的方式是针对「重新生成」这个按钮，做分支切换。而要达成这一步，需要在数据结构上新增一种 message group ，来承载同一个消息的多次生成结果。

有了message group 这个概念后，chatgpt 这种分支形式就可以兼容上，而且像多模型的比对也能比较容易地实现出来。

----    
> It seems better to have branched conversations based on message editing like ChatGPT

Branching based on message editing would violate our basic settings (any previous context can be freely modified and edited), which is unreasonable.

A more appropriate way is to switch branches by targeting the "Regenerate" button. To achieve this step, a new message group needs to be added to the data structure to carry multiple generation results of the same message.

With the concept of message group, branch forms such as chatgpt can be compatible, and comparisons of multiple models can also be implemented relatively easily.

body:
Slightly off topic. I'd really like to have the @ feature in ChatGPT. This feature can be consider as two forks that converge *visually* into one conversation. 

For example, this conversation on UI:
1. User: Hi! What's the weather?
2. Weather Agent: It's sunny
3. User: @ trip-agent Plan a trip for me
4. Trip Agent: Since today is sunny, let's head to a nearby park!

The actual content of Weather Agent's chat history is:
1. System: (Weather Agent System Prompt.......)
2. User: Hi! What's the weather?
3. Assistant: (Calling Tool)
4. Weather Tool: Sunny
5.  Assistant: It's sunny
6.  User: @ trip-agent Plan a trip for me
7.  Assistant with name "Trip Agent": Since today is sunny, let's head to a nearby park!

while the content Trip Agent sees is:
1. System: (Trip Agent System Prompt.......)
2. User: @ weather-agent Hi! What's the weather?
3. Assistant with name `Weather Agent`: It's sunny
4. User: Plan a trip for me
5. Assistant: (Calling Tool)
6. Map Tool: .....
7. Assistant: Since today is sunny, let's head to a nearby park!

I think this @ feature is even more powerful than Forkable Chat since it enables interaction with *different* agents in one chat, in contrast to interacting with *one* agent multiple times.

My real use case is that I need to write film scripts with a script writer agent, and after the script is good enough, I need another agent (midjourney prompt agent) to help me write image prompts for Midjourney, based on the complete script and whole conversation, to generate an image storyboard.

For the issues you're experiencing with the search and time plugins in version v1.34.1, here are some insights that might help:

1. **Search Plugin**: Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific information on how the search plugin should handle subsequent operations based on search results. This might require further investigation or checking the plugin's implementation details.

2. **Time Plugin Infinite Loop**: There isn't specific information available about the conditions that could cause the time plugin to enter an infinite loop. However, reviewing the plugin's error handling and logging mechanisms might provide some clues. Lobe Chat implements error handling and logging for plugins, which can help diagnose issues like infinite loops. The `internal_updatePluginError` function is used to update the plugin error state and log errors, which might be useful for troubleshooting <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/chat/slices/plugin/action.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar open issue related to the "SignatureDoesNotMatch" error when uploading files to an S3-compatible storage service. The suggested solution involves several steps to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. Verify that the access key and secret key are correct and have the necessary permissions.
2. Ensure the endpoint URL is correctly configured.
3. Check if the service requires a specific signature version and ensure your configuration matches this requirement.
4. Determine if the service requires path-style or virtual-hosted-style URLs and configure your requests accordingly.
5. If the service has specific requirements for signing requests, you might need to implement a custom signing method. Refer to the service's documentation for guidance.

This issue was discussed in [this thread](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4710) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4710)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @danbus! 👋 I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash those bugs together!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the chat module's handling of image-only messages. According to the current implementation, the chat module processes messages by checking if there is an `imageList` or `fileList` present. If a message contains images, it constructs the content by combining the text content with any file context, including image URLs. This suggests that the system expects some accompanying text with the image to process the message correctly <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/chat.ts)</sup>.

To address this issue, you might need to modify the system to handle image-only messages without requiring text. This could involve adjusting the logic in the `processMessages` function to allow messages with only images to be processed without additional text content.

Hey @duoartisan! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's tackle this together!

<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering, "Invalid URL string," when using the Qwen provider on a Vercel deployment, might be related to the base URL configuration for the Qwen provider. In the Lobe Chat codebase, the default base URL for the Qwen provider is set to `'https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1'` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts)</sup>. 

Since this issue does not occur on `chat-preview.lobehub.com`, it suggests that there might be a difference in how the URL is being handled or configured in your Vercel deployment. Here are a few things you can check or try:

1. **Environment Variables**: Ensure that the environment variables, especially those related to the Qwen provider's API key and base URL, are correctly set in your Vercel deployment.

2. **Configuration Differences**: Compare the configuration settings between your Vercel deployment and the `chat-preview.lobehub.com` to identify any discrepancies, particularly in how URLs are constructed or handled.

3. **Recent Changes**: Note that there was a bug fix related to "Qwen baseUrl calling" in version 1.34.1, which might be relevant to your issue <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup>. Ensure that your deployment includes this fix.

4. **Code Review**: Review the code in `src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts` to ensure that the base URL is being set correctly and that there are no overrides or modifications that could lead to an invalid URL string <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts)</sup>.

By addressing these areas, you may be able to resolve the URL string error in your Vercel deployment.

The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the '使用客户端请求模式' (client request mode) feature. When this feature is disabled, requests to xAI result in a 403 error, indicating that the service is not available in your region. This error is handled in the code by returning an error object with the error type `AgentRuntimeErrorType.LocationNotSupportError` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/groq/index.ts)</sup>.

To resolve this, you might need to ensure that the client request mode is enabled, as it appears to allow requests to be made directly from the browser, potentially bypassing regional restrictions. Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be documentation or environment settings in the Docker setup that explicitly control this feature, so it might require further investigation into the codebase or configuration files to find a way to enable it by default.

If you haven't found a way to toggle this feature through environment variables, it might be necessary to look into the code to see if there's a way to set this option programmatically or through a configuration file.

目前逻辑确实存在一些冲突。
正确逻辑应该是
* 「限制历史消息数」—— 按钮关闭：等于不限制历史消息数量，system prompt + 所有历史消息+当前输入的 prompt 拼接请求模型。
* 「限制历史消息数」——按钮开启：
	* 	数量设置为0：不携带任何历史消息。仅将 system prompt + 用户当前输入的 prompt 拼接请求模型
	*  数量设置为 n：携带 n 条历史消息。即将 system prompt + n 条历史消息 + 用户当前输入的 prompt 拼接请求模型

但现在看起来的 bug 是当「限制历史消息数」——按钮开启 且 数量设置为 0 时, 等价于按钮关闭了，所有历史消息都会携带上。

----    
There are indeed some conflicts in logic at the moment.
The correct logic should be
* "Limit the number of historical messages" - button off: equal to no limit on the number of historical messages, system prompt + all historical messages + currently input prompt splicing request model.
* "Limit the number of historical messages" - button is turned on:
* Set the quantity to 0: no historical messages are carried. Only the system prompt + the prompt currently entered by the user are spliced ​​into the request model
* The quantity is set to n: n historical messages are carried. That is, the system prompt + n historical messages + the prompt currently entered by the user will be spliced ​​into the request model

But now it seems that the bug is that when the "Limit the number of historical messages" - the button is turned on and the number is set to 0, it is equivalent to the button being turned off, and all historical messages will be carried.

Hello @BrandInSKQ! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's see if we can solve this issue together.

<!-- Answer -->
Network problems when creating an OpenAI link with the Qwen model in Lobe Chat can be caused by several factors. Here are some steps to troubleshoot and resolve the issue:

1. **Check API Key Configuration**: Ensure that the API key is correctly configured in the environment variables or settings. Any typo or incorrect key can lead to network issues.

2. **Proxy Settings**: If you are using a proxy, verify that the `OPENAI_PROXY_URL` is correctly set. Incorrect proxy settings can cause connectivity problems.

3. **Port Conflicts**: Make sure that the port used by Docker is not in conflict with other services. The default port is `3210`, but you can change it if needed.

4. **Network Connectivity**: Check your network connection to ensure there are no interruptions or restrictions that might affect the connection to the OpenAI service.

5. **Docker Configuration**: Verify that Docker is properly configured and running. Sometimes, restarting Docker can resolve network-related issues.

6. **Logs and Error Messages**: Check the logs for any specific error messages that might provide more insight into the network problem. This can help identify if the issue is with the server, client, or network configuration.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider reviewing the `.env.example` file for any additional configuration settings that might be required for your specific setup <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker.zh-CN.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering, "messages: at least one message is required," typically indicates that the request to the Claude model is missing the necessary message data. This can happen if the message construction process fails to include any user messages or if the plugin interaction does not properly pass the required data back to the Claude model.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve this issue:

1. **Check Message Construction**: Ensure that the message construction logic is correctly assembling the messages before sending them to the Claude model. The `buildAnthropicMessages` function should be properly formatting and including all necessary user messages.

2. **Plugin Interaction**: Verify that the "搜索引擎" plugin is correctly handling the transition back to the Claude model. The plugin should ensure that the response includes at least one valid message to avoid triggering the "invalid_request_error."

3. **Update and Sync**: Since you mentioned updating the Topic feature, ensure that all components are correctly synchronized and that no recent changes have inadvertently affected the message handling logic.

4. **Error Handling**: Review any error handling mechanisms in place to catch and log issues during the message construction and plugin interaction phases. This can help identify where the process might be failing.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to delve deeper into the specific implementation details of the plugin and message handling logic to identify any discrepancies or bugs.

5. **Testing in a Non-Docker Environment**: If possible, test the same configuration in a non-Docker environment to see if the issue persists. This can help determine if the problem is specific to the Docker setup.

@zhangnanchao Hello there! I'm here to help you with bugs, questions, and becoming a contributor. Let's squash those bugs together! 🤖

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion regarding Logto login issues in the lobe-chat repository. The discussion is titled "[请问 logto 登录的问题，可否帮忙看下，下面提供了具体的配置](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4221)" and it was last updated on September 30, 2024. The suggested solution in a related closed issue was to configure the `NEXTAUTH_URL` variable according to the documentation <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4221)</sup>.

For your specific issue with user registration and login errors after using Logto, ensure that all environment variables are correctly set, especially those related to Logto and authentication. Here are some key variables to check:

- `AUTH_LOGTO_ID`: Ensure this is set to the correct Client ID from your Logto application.
- `AUTH_LOGTO_SECRET`: Ensure this is set to the correct Client Secret from your Logto application.
- `AUTH_LOGTO_ISSUER`: This should be set to the correct OpenID Connect issuer URL.
- `NEXTAUTH_URL`: This should be set to the correct callback URL, such as `https://lobe.example.com/api/auth`.

Additionally, verify that your Logto application is configured with the correct redirect URIs and CORS settings as outlined in the documentation <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/logto.mdx)</sup>. If the problem persists, double-check your Docker and Nginx configurations to ensure they align with the expected setup for the lobe-chat application.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
To resolve the "400 Bad Request" error and the "UnknownAction: Cannot parse action at /api/auth/providers" issue when configuring LobeChat with Authelia, ensure the following:

1. **Correct Configuration in Authelia**: Verify that the `identity_providers` section in your Authelia configuration file is correctly set up. Specifically, check that the `id`, `secret`, and `redirect_uris` are correctly configured. The `redirect_uris` should match the callback URL used by LobeChat, such as `https://lobechat.example.com/api/auth/callback/authelia`. Note that the `secret` in Authelia should be a hashed value, and its plaintext equivalent should be used in LobeChat.

   ```yaml
   identity_providers:
     oidc:
       - id: lobe-chat
         description: LobeChat
         secret: '$pbkdf2-sha512$310000$c8p78n7pUMln0jzvd4aK4Q$JNRBzwAo0ek5qKn50cFzzvE9RXV88h1wJn5KGiHrD0YKtZaR/nCb2CJPOsKaPK0hjf.9yHxzQGZziziccp6Yng'  # The digest of 'insecure_secret'.
         public: false
         authorization_policy: two_factor
         redirect_uris:
           - https://lobechat.example.com/api/auth/callback/authelia
         scopes:
           - openid
           - profile
           - email
         userinfo_signing_algorithm: none
   ```

2. **Environment Variables in LobeChat**: Ensure that the environment variables in LobeChat are correctly set. The `AUTH_AUTHELIA_ID`, `AUTH_AUTHELIA_SECRET`, and `AUTH_AUTHELIA_ISSUER` should match the values configured in Authelia. The `AUTH_AUTHELIA_SECRET` should be the plaintext version of the hashed secret used in Authelia.

   ```plaintext
   AUTH_AUTHELIA_ID=lobe-chat
   AUTH_AUTHELIA_SECRET=insecure_secret
   AUTH_AUTHELIA_ISSUER=https://auth.example.com
   NEXTAUTH_URL=https://lobechat.example.com/api/auth
   ```

3. **TLS Configuration**: Ensure that TLS is enabled for your domain, as Authelia requires TLS for domains other than localhost.

By ensuring these configurations are correct, you should be able to resolve the authentication errors <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/authelia.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/auth/next-auth/authelia.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

body:
Okay, after many attempts I managed to fix issue. For me the key was to set `NEXTAUTH_URL=https://lobechat.example.com/api/auth`.

`https://chat.example.com/api/auth/callback/cloudflare-zero-trust` is incorrect for this env var and will lead to errors, same for authelia. In cloudflare dashboard or authelia config callback is same as in documentation.

Also when working with cloudflare it is important to save app configuration at the bottom of page.

tip: restart from scratch, follow lobe guides step by step without modifications, this helped me to narrow down the issue

Another note: I verified minio correctness and settings, check that you can open objects in the bucket via admin console. If objects will not load and you will encounter 403 error in browser network tab, verify minio CORS settings, also check [this](https://min.io/docs/minio/linux/integrations/setup-nginx-proxy-with-minio.html?ref=docs-redirect)

You can take a look at my configuration: [lobe](https://github.com/stone-w4tch3r/devops/tree/main/selfhosting/lobechat), [authelia](https://github.com/stone-w4tch3r/devops/tree/main/selfhosting/authelia), [minio](https://github.com/stone-w4tch3r/devops/tree/main/selfhosting/minio). Also in same repo there is a caddy config, but it is split into multiple files and may be not easy to understand

<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @Gray19970! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem: [[Bug] 根据教程设置子目录路径 ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH，重新构建生成docker镜像运行不成功。](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1303). This issue was resolved by a pull request that fixed support for `PROXY_URL` in Docker with proxychains-ng <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1303)</sup>.

To ensure `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` works correctly in your Docker setup, you need to build a custom Docker image with overridden `NEXT_PUBLIC` environment variables. This can be done using GitHub Actions by setting up a workflow to build and push the Docker image, specifying `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` as a build argument. You should also add `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` to your GitHub Repository settings under Secrets and variables > Actions > Repository secrets <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey @tsingfenger! 👋 I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let's squash those bugs together!

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion regarding an embedding error related to token limits: [Embedding Error: Requested 9064 tokens instead of 8192 tokens](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4654). This discussion is still open and was last updated on November 11, 2024 <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4654)</sup>.

In the lobe-chat codebase, handling token limits involves calculating the total token usage and comparing it against the maximum allowed tokens for a model. The code calculates tokens used by different components such as system roles, tools, chat inputs, and history summaries. It then sums these to get the total token usage, which is compared to the maximum tokens allowed for the model <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Token/TokenTag.tsx)</sup>.

To address the issue you're facing, you might need to ensure that the total token count in your prompt does not exceed the model's maximum context length of 8192 tokens. Consider breaking down your input into smaller chunks or reducing the size of the prompt to fit within the limit.
