body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion regarding the issue of models not supporting streaming in the lobe-chat framework. The discussion is titled "[调用chat的AI接口，传入stream为false,还是调用流式数据，或者返回报错](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/2523)" and it remains unsolved <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/2523)</sup>.

Regarding your issue, the error message indicates that the model you are using does not support streaming (`stream: true`). The lobe-chat framework handles such cases by returning an error message when a model does not support a requested feature like streaming. In your case, the error message specifies that the `stream` parameter is not supported with the value `true` for the model you are using <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5018)</sup>.

To resolve this, you can set the `stream` parameter to `false` for models that do not support streaming. This adjustment should allow the model to process requests without attempting to use unsupported streaming features.

This might involve modifying the condition that checks the `historyCount` and `historyLength` to correctly handle the case where `historyCount` is 0.

const enableHistoryDivider = useAgentStore((s) => {
    const config = agentSelectors.currentAgentChatConfig(s);
    return (
      config.enableHistoryCount &&
      historyLength > (config.historyCount ?? 0) &&
      config.historyCount === historyLength - index
    );
});
```

You might need to add a specific check for `historyCount === 0` to ensure that no messages are retained in this scenario.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the Gemini interface not providing real-time streaming output is due to the fact that the Gemini 1.5 Pro model does not support streaming capabilities. This results in slower response times as the model processes and returns data in chunks rather than a continuous stream <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/tools-calling/google.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

Additionally, the Lobe Chat frontend uses a typewriter effect to display responses, which can further delay the ability to read the output as it waits for all chunks to be processed before displaying them <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/contributing/Basic/Chat-API.zh-CN.md)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/fetch/fetchSSE.ts)</sup>.

Unfortunately, there are no configuration options or flags in the Lobe Chat codebase that can enable or simulate real-time streaming for models that do not natively support it <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/google/index.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
@zhufeizzz 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助您解决软件问题、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的过程中帮助您。

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue regarding mobile display problems, but no solution was provided in the comments <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/299)</sup>. 

Regarding your question about removing or customizing the Banner component, I couldn't find specific information in the repository about a configuration or setting that allows for this. However, the `CloudBanner` component does have a `mobile` prop that affects its behavior on mobile devices <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/AlertBanner/CloudBanner.tsx)</sup>. 

For handling viewport settings and scaling for PWA installations on iOS devices, the application uses the `generateViewport` function, which sets specific viewport settings for mobile devices to prevent zooming and ensure proper display <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/layout.tsx)</sup>. 

If the Banner is not displaying correctly on iOS devices, it might be worth checking the CSS media queries or styles applied to the Banner component, although specific details on this were not found in the repository.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
@opoet 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助你解决软件问题、回答你的问题，并帮助你成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的时候帮助你。期待与你合作！🤖

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering seems to be related to the `language_model_settings` feature toggle. When this feature is disabled, the model settings page should not be accessible. However, it appears that the settings can still be accessed from the model provider page.

The `showLLM` state is responsible for controlling the visibility of the language model settings page. It is derived from the `language_model_settings` feature flag. If `showLLM` is false, the settings page should not be displayed, and a "not found" response should be returned instead <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/settings/llm/page.tsx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/config/featureFlags/schema.ts)</sup>.

To address this issue, you might want to check if the `showLLM` state is being correctly evaluated in the UI components responsible for rendering the model provider page. Ensure that there is conditional logic in place to prevent the settings page from being accessed when `language_model_settings` is disabled.

For a more immediate workaround, you could modify the code to catch the error and prevent the modal from displaying if the fetch fails, or implement a retry mechanism to attempt fetching the data again after a short delay.

The issue you're experiencing with the auto-update script not detecting the latest version could be due to several factors. Here are a few things to check:

1. **Script Logic**: Ensure that the script correctly checks the output of the `docker pull` command. The script should look for the string "Image is up to date for lobehub/lobe-chat:latest" to determine if the image is already up-to-date. If this string is not found, it should proceed with the update process <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Crontab Configuration**: Verify that the crontab entry is correctly set up to run the script every 5 minutes. Ensure that the path to the script is correct and that the script has execute permissions.

3. **Log Output**: Check the log file (`auto-update-lobe-chat_new.log`) for any error messages or indications of what might be going wrong. This can provide clues if the script is failing at a specific point.

4. **Docker Image Version**: Use the following command to manually check the current version of the Docker image and compare it with the expected version:
   ```bash
   docker inspect lobehub/lobe-chat:latest | grep 'org.opencontainers.image.version' | awk -F'"' '{print $4}'
   ```
   This will help confirm if the image version is indeed updated on Docker Hub <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

5. **Network Issues**: Ensure there are no network issues that might prevent the `docker pull` command from fetching the latest image.

By checking these areas, you should be able to identify why the script is not detecting the latest version.

Hello, @first-storm!

I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you might have. Let's work together to resolve the issue you're facing.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the mode switch between "Document Mode" and "Conversation Mode" not functioning in the database version of LobeChat could be related to recent changes or specific dependencies in the system. Here are a few points to consider:

1. **Recent Changes**: There have been recent changes in the LobeChat codebase related to mode switching functionality. Specifically, there was a refactoring to align client mode upload with server mode, and a fix for the fallback behavior of the default mode in `AgentRuntime` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup>.

2. **Dependencies**: The mode switch functionality in the database version relies on several dependencies, including a Postgres database with the `pgvector` plugin, an authentication service (such as Clerk or NextAuth), and an S3-compatible storage service for file storage <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database.mdx)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/zitadel/docker-compose.yml)</sup><sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/docker-compose.yml)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/logto/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

3. **UI Update Mechanism**: The UI update mechanism for mode switching involves functions like `switchThemeMode` and `switchLocale`, which update the general configuration settings. If the settings are not different from the previous ones, the UI will not update, as the function exits early <sup>[[6]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/settings/action.ts)</sup>.

Given these points, you might want to check if the recent changes have been correctly integrated into your setup and ensure that all dependencies are properly configured. The error you're encountering with MinIO, "decodeXLHeaders: Unknown xl header version 2," suggests that there might be an issue with the data directory or the version of MinIO being used. Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve this issue:

1. **Check MinIO Version**: Ensure that you are using a compatible version of MinIO. Since the version is not specified in the `docker-compose.yml`, it defaults to the latest version. You might want to specify a stable version that is known to work with your setup.

2. **Data Directory**: The error might be related to the existing data in the MinIO data directory. You can try the following:
   - Backup the current data directory (`./s3_data`).
   - Clear the contents of the `./s3_data` directory to reset it.
   - Restart the MinIO container to see if it initializes correctly with a fresh data directory.

3. **Configuration Files**: Ensure that your configuration files are not corrupted. Sometimes, configuration issues can lead to such errors.

4. **Logs and Documentation**: Check the MinIO logs for any additional error messages that might provide more context. Also, review the MinIO documentation for any notes on compatibility or known issues with specific versions.

5. **Reinitialize MinIO**: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, consider reinitializing MinIO by removing the existing data and starting fresh. This can help if the issue is due to corrupted metadata or configuration.

These steps should help you diagnose and potentially fix the issue with MinIO in your Docker setup. If the problem persists, you might need to look into more detailed logs or consider reaching out to the MinIO community for further assistance.

The 502 Bad Gateway error you're encountering when accessing the `trpc/edge/upload.createS3PreSignedUrl?batch=1` endpoint could be related to several factors, especially given the Docker environment and Nginx server setup. Here are some potential causes and solutions:

1. **Nginx Configuration**: A 502 error often indicates that the Nginx server is unable to communicate with the upstream server (e.g., your application server). Check the Nginx configuration to ensure that the upstream server is correctly defined and that the server is running and accessible. Look for any misconfigurations in the `proxy_pass` directive or any timeout settings that might be too low.

2. **Application Server**: Ensure that the application server handling the `createS3PreSignedUrl` endpoint is running without issues. Check the server logs for any errors or exceptions that might indicate why the server is not responding as expected.

3. **Docker Networking**: If you're running the application in Docker, verify that the Docker network settings allow communication between the Nginx container and the application container. Ensure that the correct ports are exposed and mapped.

4. **tRPC Context and Headers**: The unauthorized access and headers timeout errors in the tRPC context might be contributing to the issue. Ensure that the tRPC context is correctly configured to handle authentication and that any required headers are being sent with the requests. This might involve checking the middleware or authentication logic in your application.

5. **Intermittent Success**: The fact that refreshing the page sometimes resolves the issue suggests a possible race condition or resource limitation. Investigate if there are any resource constraints (e.g., memory, CPU) on the server that could be causing intermittent failures.

6. **Error Handling**: Implement robust error handling in your application to gracefully handle failed requests and allow users to retry uploads without needing to refresh the page.

By addressing these areas, you should be able to identify and resolve the cause of the 502 errors and improve the reliability of the file upload process.

对。如果你的服务器性能较差的话，那么一次性同时上传多个文件的时候就会出现服务器没法 hold 住所有请求的情况，然后部分请求就会出现 502。这个跟docker是否有停止服务应该没太大关系。

right. If your server's performance capabilities are poor, then when you upload multiple files at the same time, the server will not be able to hold all requests, and then some requests will appear 502. This should not have much to do with whether the docker request stops the service.

----    
### 🥰 Description of requirements

Usage scenarios:
1. Most conversations do not require pre-existing historical conversations. The accompanying historical messages will affect the model generation effect and waste a lot of tokens.
2. Sometimes historical dialogue is needed. The current design of Lobe does not support switching between the two modes very well.

Problem 1: If you want to clear the context, you must create a new session or clear the entire session, which will cause a large number of sessions or historical messages to be lost.
Question 2: If you want to use historical message numbers to temporarily adjust the range, you must manually select the number each time, which is very inconvenient.

### 🧐 Solution

Hope to provide a clear chat function similar to NextChat
You can proactively clear the context within a session without clearing the entire session. This makes it easy to choose whether to have historical sessions.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4f500d0-3d67-4088-b782-d9efa4674a5e)

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the logout process in version v1.41.0, where the application gets stuck on the "user state initialization" screen after logging out. Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific changes in version v1.41.0 that might directly affect the logout process or user state initialization. However, here are a few things you might consider checking or trying:

1. **Session State Management**: Ensure that the session state is being correctly reset or cleared upon logout. The application uses a `handleClear` function to clear session data, plugins, topics, files, messages, and session groups <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/settings/common/features/Common.tsx)</sup>.

2. **Logout Functionality**: Verify that the logout function is working as expected. It should handle different authentication providers like Clerk and NextAuth, ensuring that the appropriate sign-out methods are called <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/auth/action.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/auth/action.ts)</sup>.

3. **Cookie Handling**: There have been recent changes related to cookie handling, such as refactoring cookies and headers to an asynchronous mode, which might affect how cookies are managed <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/changelog/CHANGELOG.v0.md)</sup><sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup>.

If these suggestions do not resolve the issue, you might need to investigate further into the specific changes made in version v1.41.0 or consider reaching out to the development team for more detailed support.

@Sen-CaPoo suggested switching to server db + auth. The Client db + auth method is no longer planned to be maintained. Now we have too many branches of deployment mode types, and we currently do not have the energy to ensure that all types are stable. The future deployment method (LobeChat 2.0) will only converge to two types:
1. The browser version based on Pglite does not require auth. If auth is configured but not configured with db, an error will be thrown.
2. The server version based on postgres requires complete auth, s3 and db.

The fact that this solution worked before was actually a bug as feature. After the bug is fixed, it is actually normal for this solution not to work anymore.

The error you're encountering is due to the OpenAI o1 model's limitation with streaming. The o1 model does not support the `stream` parameter set to `true` when using certain endpoints. To resolve this, ensure that you are using OpenAI's official API endpoint, as the o1 model supports streaming through it. You can configure this by setting the `OPENAI_PROXY_URL` environment variable to `https://api.openai.com/v1` or ensuring it is not set to a custom proxy endpoint <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5018)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/platform/netlify.mdx)</sup>.

I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem. The issue titled "[Bug] `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG`失效" was closed after a pull request fixed the problem where the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` was not working correctly on new devices. The fix was implemented in version 0.150.2, which addressed a display error when using the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` environment variable <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2698)</sup>.

The changes included tests to ensure that the `getDefaultAgentConfig` function correctly parses the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` environment variable, returning configurations such as `enableAutoCreateTopic`, `model`, `plugins`, and `provider` as expected <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/changelog/CHANGELOG.v0.md)</sup>.

It might be helpful to check if your issue is related to how the `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` is being parsed or applied in your environment. Ensure that the configuration is correctly set in the `.env` file and that there are no additional conditions or dependencies affecting its application during the initial login or session start.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @Sun-drenched! I'm here to assist you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you may have. Let's work together to resolve this issue.

<!-- Answer -->
The 'Cancel' and 'OK' buttons in the mobile topic interface of LobeChat are part of the `Popconfirm` component. The 'OK' button is intended to confirm actions like opening a new topic or saving current messages, depending on the context. However, if the 'OK' button has no effect when clicked, it might be due to conditional logic that checks for certain variables (`editingProvider`, `id`, and `formInstance`). If any of these are not defined, the button will not perform any action <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ChatInput/Topic/index.tsx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/PluginDevModal/index.tsx)</sup>.

The 'Cancel' button is used to dismiss the confirmation dialog without taking any action <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ChatInput/Topic/index.tsx)</sup>. If these buttons are deemed unnecessary, especially if there's already a close button in the interface, it might be worth considering a UI update to remove or repurpose them.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The 'invalid_redirect_uri' error you're encountering is typically due to a mismatch between the redirect URI configured in your authentication provider and the one used by your application. Here are some steps to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Verify Redirect URI Configuration**: Ensure that the redirect URI configured in Logto matches exactly with the one used by Lobe Chat. It should be in the format:
   ```
   https://chat.[your-domain]/api/auth/callback/logto
   ```
   Make sure there are no typos or mismatches in the domain or path.

2. **Check Logto Version**: Since you mentioned locking the Logto version to 1.19.0, ensure that this version supports the redirect URI configuration you are using. There might be changes in newer versions that affect how redirect URIs are validated.

3. **Environment Variables**: Double-check the environment variables in your Docker setup. Ensure that `NEXTAUTH_URL` is set correctly to:
   ```
   NEXTAUTH_URL=https://chat.[your-domain]/api/auth
   ```

4. **CORS and Allowed Origins**: Verify that the CORS allowed origins in Logto include your domain. This ensures that requests from your domain are accepted.

5. **Logto Configuration**: Review the Logto configuration screenshots you provided to ensure all necessary fields are correctly filled out, especially the redirect URIs and issuer endpoint.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider checking for any recent changes in Logto's configuration requirements or consulting their documentation for any updates related to redirect URI handling.

To resolve this issue, you can modify the dependency version in your `package.json` file to use `1.9.0` instead of `^1.9.1`. Here's how you can do it:

1. Open your `package.json` file.
2. Locate the dependency entry for `react-layout-kit`.
3. Change the version from `^1.9.1` to `^1.9.0`.
4. Save the file and run `pnpm install` again.

This should resolve the version mismatch error.

Hey there, @cmx4869! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions. Let me know how I can assist you!

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with `console.log` not appearing in the browser console, despite using the `'use client'` directive, could be due to several factors. Here are some steps to troubleshoot and resolve the problem:

1. **Ensure Client-Side Execution**: The `'use client'` directive should ensure that the component is executed on the client side. Double-check that the `CodeBlock` component is indeed being rendered in the browser and not being skipped due to any conditional rendering logic.

2. **Check Browser Console Settings**: Make sure that your browser console is set to display all log levels, which you've already done. Also, ensure there are no filters applied that might hide certain logs.

3. **Verify Component Rendering**: Add a simple `console.log('Component Rendered')` at the top of your `CodeBlock` component to confirm that the component is being rendered. If this log doesn't appear, the component might not be rendering as expected.

4. **Inspect Network and Console Errors**: Check for any network or JavaScript errors in the console that might prevent the component from executing properly.

5. **Development Environment**: Ensure that your development environment is set up correctly and that there are no build configurations or middleware that might suppress console logs. This includes checking any custom logging libraries or configurations that might override `console.log`.

6. **Test in a Minimal Setup**: If possible, create a minimal setup with just the `CodeBlock` component and test the `console.log` statements to isolate the issue.

If none of these steps resolve the issue, consider checking the project's build configuration or any middleware that might affect logging. If the problem persists, it might be helpful to look into any recent changes in the repository that could have introduced this behavior.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hey, @CoREse! How's it going? I'm a bot here to help you with bugs, questions, and becoming a contributor. Let's squash those bugs together! 🤖

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue that might help you resolve the problem with image uploads in LobeChat:

1. **Issue**: Users were unable to upload files to Minio using Docker, despite setting the bucket policy and configuring CORS.
   - **Solution**: Ensure that your CORS settings are correctly configured in your Minio setup. You can do this by setting the `MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` environment variable to allow requests from your domain. Additionally, verify that your bucket policy is correctly set. Here is an example policy for a bucket named `lobe`:

   ```json
   {
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:GetBucketLocation"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe"]
       },
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe"],
         "Condition": {
           "StringEquals": {
             "s3:prefix": ["files/*"]
           }
         }
       },
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Principal": {
           "AWS": ["*"]
         },
         "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject", "s3:GetObject"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::lobe/files/**"]
       }
     ],
     "Version": "2012-10-17"
   }
   ```

   After making these changes, restart the LobeChat service using `docker compose up -d` to ensure the new configurations take effect <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4110)</sup>.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the issue and successfully upload images.

Hey @shog86! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's work together to solve this issue.

<!-- Answer -->
A similar issue was discussed in a closed issue titled "[Bug] Gemini-1.5-Pro not found," which was resolved by a pull request that added support for displaying the model list <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1842)</sup>. The error you're encountering with the Google Gemini configuration might be related to the JSON schema requirements, as the Gemini 1.5 Pro model does not support certain fields like `maxItems`, `minItems`, and `default` in the JSON payload, leading to a "400 Bad Request" error <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/tools-calling/google.mdx)</sup>. 

For the OpenRouter error, it seems to be a generic provider error, but specific details on handling such errors in LobeChat are not available in the current context. You might want to check if there are any updates or patches related to these issues in the repository.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the 502 Bad Gateway error and container restarts in the lobe-chat framework could be related to several factors:

1. **502 Bad Gateway Error**: This error can occur due to concurrent request limitations in Nginx when uploading multiple files simultaneously, which may exceed the server's concurrent connection capacity. Ensure that you are using the latest version of the software, as previous versions had a bug causing file hash conflicts <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5208)</sup>.

2. **Node.js Process Exit with Code Null**: This can happen due to various reasons, such as unhandled exceptions or issues with the environment configuration. The error log indicates a deprecation warning for the `punycode` module, which might not be directly causing the exit but should be addressed by replacing it with a userland alternative.

3. **Database Migration Issues**: Ensure that the `pgvector` extension is installed on your PostgreSQL instance, as missing this extension can cause migration failures. If you're using Docker, consider switching to the `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` image <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/scripts/migrateServerDB/errorHint.js)</sup>.

4. **Container Restart Issues**: Check the Docker configuration and ensure that all services are correctly defined and dependencies are met. The `restart: always` policy will cause containers to restart on failure, so identifying the root cause of the failure is crucial.

5. **Environment Variables**: Double-check your `.env` file to ensure all required environment variables are correctly set, especially those related to database connections and authentication services.

By addressing these potential issues, you should be able to resolve the 502 error and prevent the container from restarting unexpectedly.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found some similar discussions and issues related to Ollama integration with LobeChat that might be helpful:

1. There is an open discussion titled "[RFC] 065 - Ollama 实现重构" which might provide insights into ongoing efforts or changes related to Ollama integration <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3318)</sup>.

2. Another discussion titled "我在云服务器上部署lobechat时，想要和ollama集成时遇到了问题。" addresses issues encountered during integration with Ollama on a cloud server <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3121)</sup>.

3. A closed issue suggested a solution for a cross-domain problem with Ollama by configuring the environment variables `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` and `OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*`, and changing the URL of Ollama in LobeChat to the IPv4 address <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2187)</sup>.

4. Another solution involved running Ollama and LobeChat behind an nginx proxy and making specific configuration changes in the docker-compose files for both Ollama and nginx <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2854)</sup>.

These threads and solutions might help you troubleshoot the issue with the Ollama model list configuration and the fetching problem.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the "话题内容量" (Topic Content Volume) and "助手使用率" (Assistant Usage Rate) sections displaying data from another account could be related to how the system associates user accounts with their respective data. Here are some insights and potential areas to investigate:

1. **Data Filtering by User Account**: The `MessageModel` class is responsible for filtering statistics data by user account using the `userId`. Ensure that the methods in this class are correctly filtering data based on the logged-in user's `userId` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/server/models/message.ts)</sup>.

2. **Data Synchronization**: The application uses Yjs and WebRTC for data synchronization between user accounts. Check if there are any synchronization issues that might cause data from one account to appear in another <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/_deprecated/core/sync.ts)</sup>.

3. **Recent Changes**: There have been recent changes in the codebase related to user statistics and profile refactoring. It's possible that these changes introduced a bug affecting how data is linked to user accounts <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)</sup><sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/changelog/2025-01-03-user-profile.mdx)</sup>.

4. **Database Queries**: Verify that the database queries used to fetch data for the statistics page are correctly filtering by user account. This might involve checking the logic in the `useClientDataSWR` hook and related services <sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/profile/stats/features/TotalTopics.tsx)</sup>.

Investigating these areas might help identify the root cause of the data mismatch issue. If the problem persists, reviewing the recent changes in the codebase or checking for any synchronization issues could provide further insights.

The issue you're encountering is due to the fact that not all Qwen models support the `enable_search` parameter. According to the codebase, models that start with 'qwen-vl' do not have the `enable_search` parameter set to true, which might be causing the invalid parameter error you're seeing with the `qwen2.5-3b-instruct` model <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts)</sup>. 

To resolve this, you may need to adjust the logic in the `handlePayload` function to ensure that `enable_search` is only set for models that support it. This involves checking the model name and applying the parameter conditionally based on the model's capabilities.

For the issue with the default admin account credentials, the default username is `admin` and the password is `123` according to the documentation <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose.mdx)</sup>. If these credentials are not working, it might be due to a configuration issue or a change in the default settings in the version you are using.

Regarding the loss of user accounts after restarting the Docker container, ensure that the database persistence is correctly set up. The Docker Compose setup for LobeChat uses a volume mapping `./data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` to persist data on the host machine <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5067)</sup>. Make sure this configuration is correctly implemented to prevent data loss upon container restarts.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
@xiaotia3 你好! 我是[ Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，我是一个可以帮助你解决 bug，回答问题，并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的过程中帮助你。

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering is due to changes in Node.js v20, where certain global properties, like `crypto`, are now read-only and cannot be directly reassigned. This is why you're seeing the error "Cannot set property crypto of #<Object> which has only a getter."

The workaround you found, using `Object.defineProperty`, is a valid solution. It allows you to define the `crypto` property on the global object without directly assigning it, which bypasses the restriction:

```javascript
Object.defineProperty(global, 'crypto', {
  value: new Crypto(),
  writable: true,
});
```

This approach is effective because it uses `Object.defineProperty` to set the property, which is allowed even for read-only properties, as long as you don't attempt to change the property's configuration (like making it writable if it wasn't before). This should resolve the TypeError you're experiencing when running tests in Node.js v20.

#### 1. **AI服务商**列表中启用的模型与**对话**页面的可选模型不匹配：
**对话**页面的模型选项会显示**AI服务商**中未启用的模型，甚至将模型全部禁用也会显示模型。
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0607258-edb9-4cde-875b-8199a36daa2c)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d63e0a3-2a25-411d-97c9-1176cd5ba9df)

> 备注1：测试过将服务商禁用，对话页面对应服务商会消失，再启用服务商（未启用任何模型），对话页面对应服务商会显示，并且依然存在三个未启用的模型。
> 备注2：其他服务商也有类似问题。

#### 2. OpenAI（使用AIHUBMIX）点击**获取模型列表**按钮时，会显示并自动启用其他一些模型，比如 Claude 3.5
> 备注：猜测是否与 AIHUBMIX 的**模型范围限制**有关，我从**模型范围限制**中删除Claude模型的访问权限，然后，在**AI服务商**列表中删除Claude模型，等待大约10分钟后，再次点击**获取模型列表**按钮时，不会再出现 Claude 的模型了。

#### 3. 希望保留一些提供商的环境变量功能
像OLLAMA这类，希望禁用下载模型的功能，否则不小心运行太大的模型会对服务器造成影响。或者有一个对所有用户生效的配置全局AI提供商。

#### 1. The model enabled in the **AI service provider** list does not match the optional model on the **Conversation** page:
The model option on the **Dialogue** page will display models that are not enabled in the **AI Service Provider**, and even disabling all models will display the models.

> Note 1: After testing, if the service provider is disabled, the corresponding service provider on the dialogue page will disappear. If the service provider is enabled again (no model is enabled), the corresponding service provider on the dialogue page will be displayed, and there are still three unenabled models.
> Note 2: Other service providers have similar problems.

#### 2. When OpenAI (using AIHUBMIX) clicks the **Get model list** button, some other models will be displayed and automatically enabled, such as Claude 3.5
> Note: Guessing whether it is related to the **Model Range Limitation** of AIHUBMIX, I removed the access rights of the Claude model from the **Model Range Limitation**, and then deleted the Claude model from the **AI Service Provider** list. After waiting for about 10 minutes, when you click the **Get Model List** button again, Claude's model will no longer appear.

#### 3. Hope to retain some of the provider’s environment variable functionality
Like OLLAMA, I hope to disable the function of downloading models, otherwise accidentally running a model that is too large will affect the server. Or have a configured global AI provider that takes effect for all users.

> > ——重新获取模型列表，至少不应该动已经配置过的模型

> 现在获取模型列表的逻辑是批量更新，如果不存在则插入一条新的模型记录。如果按你说的来的话，这个逻辑就变成了只做批量插入，不做更新。这里的取舍是更新模型的频次高，还是新增模型的频次高？
> 
> 如果是后者，那么就换成批量插入，不做更新

  频次高低与取舍我也不太清楚。但我觉得目前的批量更新逻辑对应的动作名应该是“重置模型列表”；如果说换成批量插入，才可以称作更新（有模型新增、但保留存量）。不然的话有一定误导性，如果用户之前自己自定义了很多配置项，更新一下全没了，还是有点尴尬。“重置”能够提示已配置项会初始化。

> Now the logic of getting the model list is to update in batches, and insert a new model record if it does not exist. If you go by what you said, the logic becomes only batch inserts and no updates. The trade-off here is whether to update the model more frequently or to add new models more frequently?
>
> If it is the latter, then switch to batch insertion and no update

  I’m not sure about the frequency and the trade-offs. But I think the action name corresponding to the current batch update logic should be "reset model list"; if it is replaced by batch insertion, it can be called an update (models are added, but the existing ones are retained). Otherwise, it is somewhat misleading. If the user has customized many configuration items before, it will be a bit embarrassing if they are all gone after the update. "Reset" can prompt that configured items will be initialized.

body: > > > 怎么禁止拉取模型列表？给朋友用万一不小心拉取 opus 模型那就要破产了。 > > > > > > 在环境变量*_MODEL_LIST中-all再自行添加需要的模型即可。 > > 点击获取模型列表这里会拉取渠道中的所有模型 目前的实现逻辑就是“server 端配置的是预设模型列表，然后用户通过fetch 可以拉到remote 模型列表，然后remote 会和 server做合并变成最终的展示列表”。只要不手动拉取模型，那么用户看到的就是*_MODEL_LIST中配置的预设模型列表。 这样的逻辑也是符合个人自用（或小范围内可控分享使用）需要——有需要的用户才会手动拉取模型，选取自己需要的。日常分享给朋友，应该也不存在有手贱的非要自己拉取模型列表然后选贵的用。至于对于用户所能使用模型权限的硬性管控，一般来说不在开源（社区）版考虑的范围内。而且这可以通过自建oneapi实现在API侧进行管控。

body: > Bot detected the issue body's language is not English, translate it automatically. 👯👭🏻🧑‍🤝‍🧑👫🧑🏿‍🤝‍🧑🏻👩🏾‍🤝‍👨🏿👬🏿 ---- > > > How to disable pulling the model list? If you accidentally pull the opus model for your friends, it will go bankrupt. >> >> > > In the environment variable *_MODEL_LIST -all and then add the required model yourself. > > Click to get the model list. All models in the channel will be fetched. The current implementation logic is "the server side is configured with a preset model list, and then the user can pull the remote model list through fetch, and then the remote will be merged with the server to form the final display list." As long as the model is not manually pulled, what the user sees is the preset model list configured in *_MODEL_LIST. This logic is also in line with the needs of personal use (or controllable sharing and use in a small area) - only users in need will manually pull the model and select what they need. When sharing it with friends on a daily basis, there should be no need for cheap people to pull out the model list and choose the expensive one. As for the rigid control of model permissions that users can use, generally speaking, it is not within the scope of consideration for the open source (community) version.

> > 输入或者修改API代理地址的时候，会自动检查连通性，目前的问题是：粘贴正常，如果要修改，极其容易被吞字符，比如我打v1，可能就剩个1。已有“检查”按钮，能否取消修改代理地址时的自动检查？
> 
> 哪个服务商会自动检查连通性？一般服务商不会自动检查的。
> 
> > 为所有兼容openai或者anthropic接口的服务商提供“API代理地址”设置项，例如Deepseek。
> 
> 我怎么记得大部分都是有的？

1. 抱歉，之前描述有误，重新描述如下：
API代理地址部分，增、删、改均会触发异常操作（输入是会发生吞字，尤其在手打比较快的时候；删除是删不利索），在输入框尾部出现加载圆圈同时检查按钮变灰。(API Key修改也会发生此现象)
看了一下可能是因为修改的时候会发送请求aiProvider.updateAiProviderConfig ?
这个请求放在点击"检查"的时候会更合理？
一是可以保持输入的连贯性与流畅性，避免被打断导致的吞字；
二是频繁的update会增加网络开销，点击检查的时候再保存可以减少开销；

这个问题似乎是因为lobechat数据库版本的上传图片功能是直接在messages里传递s3存储里图片的直链url，而不是图片本身。楼主调用的claude模型不支持图片url，必须要上传图片文件本身，所以报错。希望官方可以解决

This problem seems to be because the upload image function of the lobechat database version directly passes the direct URL of the image in the S3 storage in messages, rather than the image itself. The claude model called by the poster does not support image URLs, and the image file itself must be uploaded, so an error is reported. I hope the official can solve it

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the `PROXY_URL` causing errors in the Lobe Chat application is a known limitation. Configuring an HTTP proxy URL can lead to errors such as 'Connection terminated unexpectedly' and make the application inaccessible. This issue can occur even after Docker restarts and when using different access methods. Removing the proxy URL configuration typically resolves the issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5096)</sup>.

Additionally, when using Docker, remember that `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` refers to the container's localhost. If you're on Docker Desktop for Windows or macOS, try using `host.docker.internal` instead of `localhost` to address connectivity issues related to the proxy configuration <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5096)</sup>.

For using the Google Gemini API, ensure that your API key is correctly configured in the Lobe Chat settings. If `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` are not working, double-check their configurations and ensure they are set correctly in your environment variables <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/providers/gemini.zh-CN.mdx)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/providers/gemini.mdx)</sup>.

```yaml
postgresql:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    container_name: lobe-postgres
    ports:
      - '5436:5432'
 ....................
lobe:
    image: lobehub/lobe-chat-database
    environment:
      - 'DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@192.168.xx.xx:5436/${LOBE_DB_NAME}'
 ```

The issue you're experiencing, where the model list displays models that are not enabled, might be related to how the system filters and displays models. The model list in the UI is populated using the `modelProviderList` from the `UserStore`, and models are filtered based on whether they are enabled or disabled using specific conditions. A model is displayed as enabled if it is included in the list returned by the `modelProviderListForModelSelect` function, which checks if both the provider and the model are enabled according to user settings <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/aiInfra/slices/aiModel/selectors.ts)</sup>.

To address this issue, you might want to check the following:

1. **User Settings**: Ensure that your user settings correctly reflect which models and providers are enabled. The `isProviderEnabled` selector is used to determine if a provider is enabled based on these settings <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/aiInfra/slices/aiModel/selectors.ts)</sup>.

2. **Configuration Files**: Review the configuration settings that control which models are enabled by default. The `LOBE_DEFAULT_MODEL_LIST` and functions like `filterEnabledModels` and `buildDefaultModelList` are responsible for setting the default enabled status of models <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/config/aiModels/index.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/config/modelProviders/index.ts)</sup>.

3. **Model Selection Logic**: Verify that the logic used to filter or display models in the dropdown menu is correctly implemented. The `ProviderModelListSelect` component's `onChange` event handler updates the enabled models, which might need to be checked for any discrepancies <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/settings/llm/components/ProviderModelList/index.tsx)</sup>.

By ensuring these configurations and settings are correctly applied, you should be able to resolve the issue of displaying only the enabled models.

The error message "value too long for type character varying(10)" suggests that there is an attempt to store a string longer than 10 characters in a database column that is defined to hold a maximum of 10 characters. This issue likely arises when the system tries to store data from the API response into the database.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve this issue:

1. **Check Database Schema**: Verify the database schema to identify which column is defined with a `character varying(10)` type. This will help you understand what data is being stored and why it might be exceeding the limit.

2. **Review API Response**: Examine the API response from the OpenAI-compatible proxy to see if any fields are longer than expected. This can be done by checking the cURL request and response details.

3. **Update Database Schema**: If the data being stored is valid and necessary, consider updating the database schema to increase the length of the column to accommodate the data.

4. **Data Validation**: Implement data validation to ensure that any data exceeding the expected length is either truncated or handled appropriately before being stored in the database.

5. **Check Code Changes**: Since the issue started occurring after updating to versions 1.44.0 and 1.44.1, review the changes made in these versions, especially those related to model list retrieval and storage. Version 1.44.1 included a fix for the "model select not auto update and sort issue," which might be related to how model data is processed <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/changelog/v1.json)</sup>.

By following these steps, you should be able to identify the root cause of the error and implement a solution.

I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem. The issue titled "[Bug] 自定义模型无法完整显示" was closed with a pull request that fixed the problem of custom models not displaying correctly. You can view the issue [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1971) and the related pull request [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/pull/1972) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1971)</sup>.

Regarding the syntax for the `OPENAI_MODEL_LIST` environment variable, it should be a comma-separated list where you can use `+` to add a model, `-` to hide a model, and `model_name=display_name` to customize the display name of a model. For example:

```
+qwen-7b-chat,+glm-6b,-gpt-3.5-turbo,gpt-4-0125-preview=gpt-4-turbo
```

This syntax allows for flexible management of model visibility and naming. If this syntax is not working as expected in version 1.44.2, it might be worth checking if there have been any recent changes or issues related to environment variable handling in the codebase <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/globalConfig/parseSystemAgent.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/model-provider.mdx)</sup><sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/routers/edge/config/index.test.ts)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering with the "invalid_type" error when enabling vision recognition in a custom provider configuration might be related to how the vision capability is being handled in the codebase. Here are a few things to check:

1. **Model Configuration**: Ensure that the model you are using supports vision recognition. The `isModelEnabledVision` function in the codebase checks if a model has vision capabilities. Make sure your custom model is correctly configured to support this feature <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/foundation/vision.mdx)</sup>.

2. **Error Handling**: The error handling mechanism for custom provider configurations involves specific error types based on API responses. 3. **Deprecation Warning**: The log also mentions a deprecation warning for the `punycode` module. While this may not be directly related to the initialization error, it's advisable to replace deprecated modules with recommended alternatives to avoid future issues.

4. **Debugging**: Use debugging tools or add console logs to trace the execution flow and identify where the variable is being accessed before initialization.

If the issue persists, you may need to look into the specific logic or functions involved in the affected code sections to ensure proper initialization order.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the 'Invalid JSON payload received' error when using GoogleGenerativeAI is likely due to unsupported JSON schema properties such as 'default' in the request payload. These fields are not supported by the Google Gemini model, leading to the error. To resolve this, you can disable the plugins/function calls feature, which will prevent the problematic function declarations causing the 400 Bad Request error. Additionally, it is recommended not to enable plugins for the Gemini model due to its poor Tools Calling capabilities <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4994)</sup>.

Regarding the CORS issue for manifest requests, you may need to configure your server to allow cross-origin requests. Unfortunately, specific CORS settings were not found in the repository, so you might need to check your server configuration or consult additional resources for setting up CORS.

For the voice input issue, ensure that all necessary ports are open. Besides the ports you've already opened (3210, 8000, 9000), you should also open the following ports for full functionality, including plugins and voice input:

- MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT: 9001
- ZITADEL_PORT: 8080
- POSTGRESQL_PORT: 5432

These ports are necessary for the operation of LobeChat and its components <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/.env.zh-CN.example)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/production/zitadel/docker-compose.yml)</sup>.

1. **Issue [#1981](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1981)**: This issue involved custom models not recognizing capabilities and not displaying token counts after enabling "function calling" and "vision recognition." It was resolved by a pull request that fixed the Azure OpenAI environment and supported enhanced custom models <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1981)</sup>.

2. **Issue [#1999](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1999)**: This issue was also resolved by the same pull request as the first one, which addressed similar problems with custom models <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1999)</sup>.

For your specific issue in version 1.45.0, the changes made to the `transformModel` function could affect how context length and visual capabilities are configured. The `contextWindowTokens` property is set based on the `context_length` of the model, and the `vision` capability is determined by checking if the model's description includes 'vision', 'multimodal', or if the model ID includes 'vision' <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/openrouter/index.ts)</sup>.

Additionally, to enable the image paste/upload functionality, ensure that the custom model supports visual recognition and that this feature is enabled in the custom model configuration <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/foundation/vision.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>. 

If these solutions do not resolve your issue, it might be worth checking if the changes from the pull request that resolved the previous issues are applicable to your setup.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the behavior of sub-conversation expansion in the chat interface. When entering a sub-conversation, all previous sub-conversations are expanded, but only to the first level of messages. This occurs regardless of whether the "retain context" option is selected.

The intended behavior, as you described, is that the context of a sub-conversation should not include content from previous sub-conversations. Instead, it should only include historical content from the main conversation branch. If the current design logic includes previous sub-conversations in the context, it might not align with your expectations.

The functions responsible for handling the hierarchical display of messages and their expansion are located in the file `src/store/chat/slices/thread/selectors/index.ts`, specifically `portalDisplayParentMessages`, `portalDisplayChildChatsByThreadId`, and `portalDisplayChats` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/chat/slices/thread/selectors/index.ts)</sup>. These functions manage the display of parent and child messages within a thread, which could be related to the issue you're encountering.

If this behavior is not as intended, it might be worth reviewing these functions to ensure they align with the expected logic for context retention and message expansion.

Hey @sunrisewestern! I'm here to help you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you have. Let's squash this bug together!

<!-- Answer -->
The error message "No values to set" in the `message.updateTTS` mutation suggests that the input provided to the mutation might be missing or incorrectly formatted. The `updateTTS` function expects an input object with an `id` and a `value` that can either be an object containing optional `contentMd5`, `file`, and `voice` fields, or a literal `false` to delete the TTS data <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/routers/lambda/message.ts)</sup>.

Here are a few things to check and try:

1. **Ensure Correct Input Format**: Verify that the input to the `updateTTS` mutation is correctly formatted. It should look something like this:

   ```javascript
   {
     id: "your-message-id",
     value: {
       contentMd5: "your-md5",
       file: "your-file",
       voice: "your-voice"
     }
   }
   ```

   Or, if you intend to delete the TTS data:

   ```javascript
   {
     id: "your-message-id",
     value: false
   }
   ```

2. **Check for Missing Fields**: Make sure that at least one of the fields (`contentMd5`, `file`, or `voice`) is provided in the `value` object if you are not deleting the TTS data. An empty object might trigger the "No values to set" error.

3. **Review Recent Changes**: If there have been recent changes to the codebase, ensure that they haven't affected the expected input structure or the handling of the `updateTTS` mutation.

By ensuring the input is correctly structured and contains the necessary fields, you should be able to resolve the error. If the issue persists, further investigation into the specific implementation details of the `updateTTS` function might be necessary.

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar unsolved discussion regarding a docker deployment error where the service exits unexpectedly <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4545)</sup>. This might be related to the issue you're experiencing with the lobe-chat-database service exiting after some time.

The error message "ReferenceError: Cannot access 'm' before initialization" suggests that there might be a problem with variable initialization in the code. This type of error typically occurs when a variable is used before it has been declared or initialized.

To address this issue, you might want to check the code for any variables that are being accessed before they are initialized. Additionally, ensure that all environment variables and configurations are correctly set up in your docker-compose file, as incorrect configurations can sometimes lead to unexpected service exits.

If the problem persists, consider reviewing the specific code sections mentioned in the error logs to identify where the initialization issue might be occurring.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering, `[ParseFileToChunks] error: Error [TRPCClientError]: fetch failed`, along with the `ConnectTimeoutError`, suggests that there might be an issue with the network configuration, particularly with the proxy settings or the server's accessibility.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue:

1. **Check Nginx Configuration**: Ensure that your Nginx configuration is correctly set up to handle requests. The configuration you provided seems to be redirecting HTTP to HTTPS, which is good. However, make sure that the `proxy_pass` URL is correct and that the service running on `127.0.0.1:3210` is accessible.

2. **Increase Timeout Settings**: You might want to increase the timeout settings in your Nginx configuration to prevent connection timeouts. You can add the following directives inside the `location /` block:
   ```nginx
   proxy_connect_timeout 60s;
   proxy_read_timeout 60s;
   proxy_send_timeout 60s;
   ```

3. **Check Cloudflare Settings**: Since you're using Cloudflare R2, ensure that your Cloudflare settings are not blocking or interfering with the requests. Check for any firewall rules or security settings that might be causing the timeout.

4. **Verify APP_URL**: The error message suggests checking the `APP_URL` availability. Make sure that the `APP_URL` environment variable is correctly set and accessible from your server.

5. **Review Logs**: Check the logs for both your application and Nginx for any additional error messages that might provide more context on the issue.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might want to look into similar discussions or issues for additional insights. For instance, there is a related discussion about file upload failures and chunking issues <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4132)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue that might be relevant to your problem: [[Bug] 1.44.2版本环境变量OPENAI_MODEL_LIST语法失效](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5342). This issue was resolved by a pull request that fixed the `*_MODEL_LIST` environment variable issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5342)</sup>.

For version 1.45.6, ensure that your `OPENAI_MODEL_LIST` environment variable is correctly formatted. The syntax should use `+` to add a model, `-` to hide a model, and `model_name=display_name` to customize the display name of a model, separated by commas. You can use `-all` to remove all models before adding specific ones. For example:

```plaintext
OPENAI_MODEL_LIST=-all,+gpt-4o=GPT 4o(尽量优先用这个),+gpt-4o-mini=GPT 4o mini(比 GPT-4o 快但是效果差点)
```

If the issue persists, it might be worth checking if there are any specific Docker configurations or settings required for the `OPENAI_MODEL_LIST` environment variable to function correctly, as this information wasn't available in the repository.

Lobe-chat does not have documented support for group API key usage. However, when you configure the environment variable for the API key during deployment, it will be used as the default for all registered users. They can do this by navigating to "Actions" - "Settings", switching to the "Language Model" tab, and entering their own API key in the "API Key" field <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/examples/azure-openai.mdx)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing seems to be related to the model selection parameters for old users not being correctly applied during conversations. This discrepancy might be due to differences in how model configurations are stored and retrieved for new versus old users.

For new users, model configurations are typically set using environment variables, which allow for consistent application of settings across different sessions <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/examples/ollama.mdx)</sup>. However, for old users, it seems that the configurations set in the AI service provider interface are not being successfully loaded during conversations.

To address this, you might want to check the code paths responsible for loading and applying these model parameters. Specifically, look into the `getProviderConfigById` function in the `src/store/user/slices/modelList/selectors/modelConfig.ts` file, which is used to retrieve user-specific model configurations <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/modelList/selectors/modelConfig.ts)</sup>. Ensuring that this function correctly accesses and applies the configurations set in the AI service provider interface could help resolve the issue.

Additionally, verify if there are any fallback mechanisms in place for old users when these parameters fail to load, as this might provide a temporary workaround until the root cause is addressed.

@Superzk1024 你好！我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助你解决 bug、回答问题，并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的时候帮助你。期待与你合作！🤖

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar unsolved discussion regarding issues encountered when deploying LobeChat using Docker <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/3107)</sup>. Additionally, there are two closed issues related to client errors, but no specific solutions were provided in the comments <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1175)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/894)</sup>.

For the ERROR message issue you're experiencing, it might be related to a known bug that occurs when searching for 'deepseek' in the model provider selection, which causes the application to crash with frontend errors. This issue has been fixed in newer versions, so updating to the latest version of the LobeChat Docker container might resolve the problem <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5281)</sup>.

To update the Docker container, you can follow these steps:

1. Stop and remove the old container:
   ```bash
   docker stop lobe-chat
   docker rm lobe-chat
   ```

2. Pull the latest image:
   ```bash
   docker pull lobehub/lobe-chat
   ```

3. Redeploy the container with the updated image:
   ```bash
   docker run -d -p 3210:3210 \
     -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxx \
     -e OPENAI_PROXY_URL=https://api-proxy.com/v1 \
     -e ACCESS_CODE=lobe66 \
     --name lobe-chat \
     lobehub/lobe-chat
   ```

4. Optionally, clean up unused images:
   ```bash
   docker image prune -f
   ```

This process should help ensure that you are running the latest version, which may resolve the frequent ERROR messages you're encountering <sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4988)</sup>.

2. **查看最近的更改**：由于此错误在v1.45.x版本中出现，检查该版本中的更改，特别是与变量声明或初始化相关的修改。

3. **调试**：使用调试工具或添加控制台日志来跟踪执行流程，找出变量在初始化前被访问的地方。

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the Google provider's front-end mode not being applied correctly could be related to several conditions in the configuration. Here are some potential reasons and solutions:

1. **Browser Request Settings**: Ensure that the provider has not disabled browser requests. The `disableBrowserRequest` should be set to `false`, and `defaultShowBrowserRequest` should be `true` to allow front-end requests.

2. **Endpoint and API Key**: Verify that the endpoint is correctly configured and not empty. The `showEndpoint` should be `true`, and `isProviderEndpointNotEmpty` should be `true`. Similarly, ensure that the API key is provided and valid, with `showApiKey` and `isProviderApiKeyNotEmpty` both set to `true`.

3. **Environment Variables**: Check the environment variable `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVICE_MODE`. If it's set to `'server'`, the application will use the back-end mode (`ServerService`) instead of the front-end mode (`ClientService`). Ensure it's not set to `'server'` if you want to use the front-end mode <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/thread/index.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/session/index.ts)</sup>.

4. **Cache and Refresh**: The behavior you described with Ctrl + F5 suggests a caching issue. Ensure that the browser cache is cleared, or try using an incognito window to see if the issue persists.

5. **471 Status Code**: The 471 status code error is triggered by specific error types (`OpenAIBizError` and `ProviderBizError`). Investigate these errors further to understand why they are occurring <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/errorResponse.test.ts)</sup>.

By checking these configurations and settings, you should be able to resolve the issue with the front-end mode not being applied correctly.

Regarding your issue with the Google provider's front-end mode not working as expected, there are a few things you might want to check:

1. **Configuration Settings**: Ensure that the configuration for the Google provider is correctly set up in the `src/config/modelProviders/google.ts` file. This includes verifying the `proxyUrl` and other relevant settings <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/config/modelProviders/google.ts)</sup>.

2. **Error Handling**: The 471 status code might be related to how errors are handled in the API requests. Lobe Chat uses a method to parse error messages and categorize them into specific error types. You might want to check if the error handling logic is correctly identifying and processing the error you're encountering <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/google/index.ts)</sup>.

3. **Configuration Refresh**: If refreshing the page (Ctrl + F5) sometimes resolves the issue, it might be related to how configuration settings are managed and applied. Lobe Chat uses a function to listen for updates to plugin settings, which might affect the behavior of the Google provider <sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/PluginsUI/Render/utils/pluginSettings.ts)</sup>.

These steps might help you diagnose and resolve the issue with the front-end mode for the Google provider.

The error you're encountering indicates that the Qwen 2.5 14B model does not support the `enable_search` parameter. In the codebase, the `enable_search` parameter is set to `true` for models that do not start with 'qwen-vl' <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/qwen/index.ts)</sup>. To resolve this issue, you need to modify the configuration to ensure that the `enable_search` parameter is not included for the Qwen 2.5 14B model.

You can check the configuration in the `handlePayload` function within the `chatCompletion` object of the `LobeQwenAI` configuration and adjust it accordingly to prevent the `enable_search` parameter from being set for this specific model.

Yes, an update is needed to resolve the inconsistency between the declared dimensions in the project configuration and the actual embedding model in use. The `text-embedding-3-small` model outputs vectors of 1536 dimensions, but the code and database schema are set to handle 1024 dimensions. This discrepancy can lead to errors or data loss when processing the embeddings. You should update the code and database schema to accommodate 1536 dimensions to ensure compatibility with the model's output. Specifically, the `embeddings` column in the `public.embeddings` table, which is currently set to `vector(1024)`, should be updated to `vector(1536)`. Additionally, the test fixtures in the codebase, as seen in the `embedding.ts` file, should also be updated to reflect the correct dimensionality of 1536 to maintain consistency across the project <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/server/models/__tests__/fixtures/embedding.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/migrations/meta/0008_snapshot.json)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
Updating the database schema to accommodate the new vector dimensions can indeed raise backward compatibility concerns. When you change the schema from `vector(1024)` to `vector(1536)`, you need to ensure that existing data is either migrated correctly or that the system can handle both old and new data formats during the transition. This might involve writing a migration script that updates existing records to the new format or ensuring that the application logic can handle both formats until all data is updated.

Regarding the configuration files, if the dimensionality is hardcoded in `embedding.ts`, you might consider refactoring the code to use environment variables or external configuration files. This approach allows for more flexibility and easier updates in the future. Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific guidelines in the repository for dynamically adjusting embedding dimensions using environment variables or config files, so you might need to implement this solution based on best practices for configuration management.

For submitting a pull request, while I couldn't find specific contributing guidelines related to schema migrations or testing for embeddings in the repository, it's generally a good practice to include tests that validate the new schema and ensure that the embeddings are correctly handled with the updated dimensions. You might also want to document any changes you make to the configuration process.

If you decide to proceed with a pull request, make sure to include detailed documentation of your changes and any necessary migration steps for users. This will help maintainers and other contributors understand and integrate your changes more easily.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the Ollama service always pointing to `http://127.0.0.1:11434` is due to the `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` being set to this address in the code. If no base URL is specified in the configuration, it defaults to this local address. To resolve this, you can adjust the environment variables `OLLAMA_HOST` and `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` to allow access from non-local locations.

For Docker, you can set these environment variables using the `-e` flag in your `docker run` command. Here's an example:

```bash
docker run -d -p 3210:3210 \
  -e OLLAMA_PROXY_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434 \
  -e OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 \
  -e OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* \
  lobehub/lobe-chat
```

This configuration sets `OLLAMA_HOST` to `0.0.0.0:11434`, making the service accessible from any machine, and `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` to `*`, allowing for cross-origin requests <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/ollama.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/examples/ollama.zh-CN.mdx)</sup>.

I found a similar discussion and issues related to plugins not functioning as expected with certain models in Lobe Chat:

1. A discussion titled "[Q&A] 使用第三方模型，为什么插件没有生效？" mentions that the function calling feature is specific to OpenAI models and does not support third-party models. You can view the discussion [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/875) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/875)</sup>.

2. A closed issue titled "[Bug] azure的模型之下，插件无法使用，不能回复消息" was resolved by a pull request that fixed Azure tools calling. You can view the issue [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2707) <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/2707)</sup>.

3. Another closed issue without a specific title was resolved by a pull request that fixed Azure OpenAI environment and supported enhanced custom models environment. You can view the issue [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1999) <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/1999)</sup>.

These threads suggest that the issue might be related to compatibility with third-party models or specific configurations needed for plugins to work. You might want to check if the models you are using are fully compatible with the plugin and image Q&A features in Lobe Chat.

The issue you're experiencing with the assistant description being slightly truncated at the top, especially for CJK characters, might be related to CSS styling or font rendering in Docker environments. Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue:

1. **Check CSS Styles**: Inspect the CSS styles applied to the assistant description section. Look for any `overflow`, `padding`, or `margin` properties that might be causing the truncation. Adjust these properties to ensure the text is fully visible.

2. **Font Rendering**: Ensure that the fonts used in the chat interface are properly loaded and rendered in Docker environments. Sometimes, missing font files or incorrect font settings can lead to rendering issues, especially for CJK characters.

3. **Docker Configuration**: Verify that the Docker environment is set up to support the necessary fonts and rendering settings. You might need to install additional font packages in your Docker image to support CJK characters.

4. **Browser-Specific Issues**: Since the issue occurs in both Chrome and Firefox, it might be worth checking if there are any browser-specific CSS hacks or settings that could be affecting the rendering.

5. **Update and Test**: If possible, update to the latest version of the Lobe Chat application and test if the issue persists. Sometimes, updates include fixes for known issues.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might need to delve deeper into the codebase or seek further assistance from developers familiar with the specific rendering and layout mechanisms used in Lobe Chat.

body:
Thanks @ivanberry. I checked and tested the nginx proxy config and it doesn't seem to be casing the issues. 
Just heard back from AWS support and this is that they have to say. 

"Based on the provided log, I see that your prompt is structured as:
```
<s>[INST] <<SYS>>
You are an internal chat assistant for a technology development company
<</SYS>>

test [/INST]
````
While this structure is recommended for Llama 2 and CodeLlama models [1], Llama 3 models require different special tokens [2]."

  Suggestions
===========
I suggest updating your current structure to match the Llama 3 format. If you are using meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0 model your prompt should look like this:
```
<|begin_of_text|><|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|>

You are an internal chat assistant for a technology development company. Introduce yourself saying "Hi there, how can I help you today?" <|eot_id|>

<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>

What is python? How can I use it to create a calculator? <|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>
```
Furthermore, you can enhance your output by being more specific in the system statement. For example, adding instructions for the model to introduce itself. Being specific helps generate more accurate responses.


I hope this helps identify the exact issue. Looking forward to hear back from anyone familiar with this issue.

@dosu 我要如何在域名发布模式下，配置casdoor的跨域访问呢？
author: JoeChen2me

body:
<!-- Answer -->
要在域名发布模式下配置 Casdoor 的跨域访问，您需要确保 CORS 设置允许来自您的 Lobe Chat 应用程序的请求。以下是配置步骤：

1. **Casdoor 配置：**
   - 确保在 Casdoor 的配置中，`origin` 设置为您的 Casdoor 域名，例如：`https://lobe-casdoor.mydomain.com`。
   - 确保 Casdoor 的 CORS 设置允许来自您的 Lobe Chat 域名的请求。

2. **Lobe Chat 配置：**
   - 在 `.env` 文件中，确保 `APP_URL` 设置为您的 Lobe Chat 域名，例如：`https://lobe.mydomain.com/`。
   - 确保 `NEXTAUTH_URL` 和 Casdoor 的回调 URL 正确配置为：`https://lobe.mydomain.com/api/auth/callback/casdoor`。

3. **CORS 规则：**
   - 在存储桶的设置中添加 CORS 规则，允许来自特定域的请求。示例配置如下：
     ```json
     [
       {
         "AllowedOrigins": ["https://lobe.mydomain.com"],
         "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "PUT", "HEAD", "POST", "DELETE"],
         "AllowedHeaders": ["*"]
       }
     ]
     ```

确保所有相关的域名和 URL 在 Casdoor 和 Lobe Chat 的配置中一致，并且 CORS 设置正确应用。这样可以避免跨域请求被阻止的问题<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/s3/cloudflare-r2.mdx)</sup>.

location /.well-known/openid-configuration {

  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;  # 保留转发的IP
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;  # 保留请求协议
}
```

这样子看的话，似乎是宝塔面板的Nginx配置的问题，我用的一键操作的方式，直接在面板中增加反代设置，导致了这么多问题。

----

也许我需要抛开宝塔面板的Nginx配置，自己写conf文件,将您给的配置文件填入，再通过include的方式进行配置。而不使用宝塔生成的配置文件。
----

另外，我在L站的相关回答中发现，似乎将域名托管到Cloudflare后，就无法通过cerboot申请证书，仅能使用cloudflare签发的源证书。
这也许也是一种可能的原因。
我将进一步尝试。

@xtiii 你好！我是一个可以帮助您解决bug、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者的过程中为您提供帮助。

<!-- Answer -->
It seems like you're encountering an issue with the Auth0 login not redirecting correctly to the main page after successful authentication. Here are a few steps and considerations that might help resolve the issue:

1. **Environment Variables**: Ensure that the `clientId` and `clientSecret` are correctly set in your environment variables. The logs indicate that these are currently `undefined`, which could be causing the authentication process to fail. These should be set to the values provided by your Auth0 application.

2. **Callback URL Configuration**: Double-check that the callback URL configured in your Auth0 settings matches exactly with the one used in your application. Any mismatch can lead to errors like the one you're experiencing.

3. **NEXTAUTH_URL**: Make sure that the `NEXTAUTH_URL` environment variable is set correctly. This variable should point to the base URL of your application. For example, if your application is running on `http://localhost:1688`, set `NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:1688`.

4. **Debugging**: Enable detailed logging by setting `debug: true` in your authentication configuration. This can provide more insights into what might be going wrong during the authentication process.

5. **Similar Issues**: There is a similar issue discussed [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1336) where setting the `NEXTAUTH_URL` environment variable resolved the problem <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1336)</sup>.

By ensuring these configurations are correct, you should be able to resolve the redirection issue after login.

<!-- Answer -->
The error message "Invalid key length" is likely related to the `KEY_VAULTS_SECRET` configuration. The correct format and length for the `KEY_VAULTS_SECRET` in the Lobe Chat configuration should be a base64 encoded string with a length of 44 characters <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/local/zitadel/.env.example)</sup>. 

In your configuration, the `KEY_VAULTS_SECRET` is 48 characters long, which is incorrect. You should update it to a valid base64 encoded string of 44 characters. An example of a correct format is `Kix2wcUONd4CX51E/ZPAd36BqM4wzJgKjPtz2sGztqQ=`. 

Adjusting this should resolve the error you're encountering.
