body:
我是按照官方文档进行部署的：

mkdir lobe-chat-db && cd lobe-chat-db

bash <(curl -fsSL https://lobe.li/setup.sh) -l zh_CN

选择的是端口模式
然后执行：docker compose up -d
登录就失败：
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e066a67c-6645-4ae6-bc54-2584b7ebd92b)


**### env:**
```
# Proxy，如果你需要的话（比如你使用 GitHub 作为鉴权服务提供商）
# HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:7890
# HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:7890


# 其他环境变量，视需求而定，可以参照客户端版本的环境变量配置，注意不要有 ACCESS_CODE
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxx
# OPENAI_PROXY_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
# OPENAI_MODEL_LIST=...


# ===================
# ===== 预设配置 =====
# ===================
# 如没有特殊需要不用更改
LOBE_PORT=3210
CASDOOR_PORT=8000
MINIO_PORT=9000
APP_URL=http://192.168.2.162:3210
AUTH_URL=http://192.168.2.162:3210/api/auth

# Postgres 相关，也即 DB 必须的环境变量
LOBE_DB_NAME=lobechat
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=uWNZugjBqixf8dxC

AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER=http://192.168.2.162:8000
# Casdoor secret
AUTH_CASDOOR_ID=a387a4892ee19b1a2249
AUTH_CASDOOR_SECRET=209bc86988785268ba31df7694d26af4

# MinIO S3 配置
MINIO_ROOT_USER=admin
MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=bdce4ad3

# 在下方配置 minio 中添加的桶
S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN=http://192.168.2.162:9000
S3_ENDPOINT=http://192.168.2.162:9000
MINIO_LOBE_BUCKET=lobe

# 为 casdoor 配置
origin=http://192.168.2.162:8000
```


### **docker-compose:**
```
name: lobe-chat-database
services:
  network-service:
    image: alpine
    container_name: lobe-network
    restart: always
    ports:
      - '${MINIO_PORT}:${MINIO_PORT}' # MinIO API
      - '9001:9001' # MinIO Console
      - '${CASDOOR_PORT}:${CASDOOR_PORT}' # Casdoor
      - '${LOBE_PORT}:3210' # LobeChat
    command: tail -f /dev/null
    networks:
      - lobe-network

  postgresql:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    container_name: lobe-postgres
    ports:
      - '5432:5432'
    volumes:
      - './data:/var/lib/postgresql/data'
    environment:
      - 'POSTGRES_DB=${LOBE_DB_NAME}'
      - 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}'
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U postgres']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    restart: always
    networks:
      - lobe-network

  minio:
    image: minio/minio
    container_name: lobe-minio
    network_mode: 'service:network-service'
    volumes:
      - './s3_data:/etc/minio/data'
    environment:
      - 'MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN=*'
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: always
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        minio server /etc/minio/data --address ':${MINIO_PORT}' --console-address ':9001' &
        MINIO_PID=\$!
        while ! curl -s http://localhost:${MINIO_PORT}/minio/health/live; do
          echo 'Waiting for MinIO to start...'
          sleep 1
        done
        sleep 5
        mc alias set myminio http://localhost:${MINIO_PORT} ${MINIO_ROOT_USER} ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
        echo 'Creating bucket ${MINIO_LOBE_BUCKET}'
        mc mb myminio/${MINIO_LOBE_BUCKET}
        wait \$MINIO_PID
      "

  casdoor:
    image: casbin/casdoor
    container_name: lobe-casdoor
    entrypoint: /bin/sh -c './server --createDatabase=true'
    network_mode: 'service:network-service'
    depends_on:
      postgresql:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      httpport: ${CASDOOR_PORT}
      RUNNING_IN_DOCKER: 'true'
      driverName: 'postgres'
      dataSourceName: 'user=postgres password=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} host=postgresql port=5432 sslmode=disable dbname=casdoor'
      runmode: 'dev'
    volumes:
      - ./init_data.json:/init_data.json
    env_file:
      - .env

  searxng:
    image: searxng/searxng
    container_name: lobe-searxng
    volumes:
      - './searxng-settings.yml:/etc/searxng/settings.yml'
    environment:
      - 'SEARXNG_SETTINGS_FILE=/etc/searxng/settings.yml'
    restart: always
    networks:
      - lobe-network
    env_file:
      - .env

  lobe:
    image: lobehub/lobe-chat-database
    container_name: lobe-chat
    network_mode: 'service:network-service'
    depends_on:
      postgresql:
        condition: service_healthy
      network-service:
        condition: service_started
      minio:
        condition: service_started
      casdoor:
        condition: service_started

    environment:
      - 'NEXT_AUTH_SSO_PROVIDERS=casdoor'
      - 'KEY_VAULTS_SECRET=Kix2wcUONd4CX51E/ZPAd36BqM4wzJgKjPtz2sGztqQ='
      - 'NEXT_AUTH_SECRET=NX2kaPE923dt6BL2U8e9oSre5RfoT7hg'
      - 'DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgresql:5432/${LOBE_DB_NAME}'
      - 'S3_BUCKET=${MINIO_LOBE_BUCKET}'
      - 'S3_ENABLE_PATH_STYLE=1'
      - 'S3_ACCESS_KEY=${MINIO_ROOT_USER}'
      - 'S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${MINIO_ROOT_USER}'
      - 'S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}'
      - 'LLM_VISION_IMAGE_USE_BASE64=1'
      - 'S3_SET_ACL=0'
      - 'SEARXNG_URL=http://searxng:8080'
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: always
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "
        /bin/node /app/startServer.js &
        LOBE_PID=\$!
        sleep 3
        if [ $(wget --timeout=5 --spider --server-response ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration 2>&1 | grep -c 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK') -eq 0 ]; then
          echo '⚠️Warining: Unable to fetch OIDC configuration from Casdoor'
          echo 'Request URL: ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
          echo 'Read more at: https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
          echo ''
          echo '⚠️注意：无法从 Casdoor 获取 OIDC 配置'
          echo '请求 URL: ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
          echo '了解更多：https://lobehub.com/zh/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
          echo ''
        else
          if ! wget -O - --timeout=5 ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration 2>&1 | grep 'issuer' | grep ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}; then
            printf '❌Error: The Auth issuer is conflict, Issuer in OIDC configuration is: %s' \$(wget -O - --timeout=5 ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration 2>&1 | grep -E 'issuer.*' | awk -F '\"' '{print \$4}')
            echo ' , but the issuer in .env file is: ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER} '
            echo 'Request URL: ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
            echo 'Read more at: https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
            echo ''
            printf '❌错误：Auth 的 issuer 冲突，OIDC 配置中的 issuer 是：%s' \$(wget -O - --timeout=5 ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration 2>&1 | grep -E 'issuer.*' | awk -F '\"' '{print \$4}')
            echo ' , 但 .env 文件中的 issuer 是：${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER} '
            echo '请求 URL: ${AUTH_CASDOOR_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
            echo '了解更多：https://lobehub.com/zh/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
            echo ''
          fi
        fi
        if [ $(wget --timeout=5 --spider --server-response ${S3_ENDPOINT}/minio/health/live 2>&1 | grep -c 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK') -eq 0 ]; then
          echo '⚠️Warining: Unable to fetch MinIO health status'
          echo 'Request URL: ${S3_ENDPOINT}/minio/health/live'
          echo 'Read more at: https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
          echo ''
          echo '⚠️注意：无法获取 MinIO 健康状态'
          echo '请求 URL: ${S3_ENDPOINT}/minio/health/live'
          echo '了解更多：https://lobehub.com/zh/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#necessary-configuration'
          echo ''
        fi
        wait \$LOBE_PID
      "

volumes:
  data:
    driver: local
  s3_data:
    driver: local

networks:
  lobe-network:
    driver: bridge
```
author: egWanp

<!-- Answer -->
The issues you're encountering with the "Copy" and "Download Screenshot" functionalities in the lobe-chat application seem to be related to JavaScript errors, specifically a `TypeError` and a warning about using `document.write()`. Here are some insights and potential steps to address these issues:

1. **Copy Functionality**: The "Copy" button uses the `copyToClipboard` function to copy text or images. If you're seeing a "Failed to copy image" error, it might be due to browser restrictions or issues with the clipboard API. Ensure that your browser has permissions to access the clipboard and that no extensions are interfering with this functionality <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/components/Thinking/index.tsx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/Extras/Translate.tsx)</sup>.

2. **Download Screenshot Functionality**: The "Download Screenshot" feature uses the `useScreenshot` hook and the `domToPng` function to capture and download images. If the download is slow, it could be due to the complexity of the DOM being captured or network issues. Ensure that your system resources are not being heavily utilized by other processes <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ShareModal/ShareImage/index.tsx)</sup><sup>[[4]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/(main)/chat/(workspace)/@portal/Artifacts/Body/Renderer/SVG.tsx)</sup>.

3. **Browser Compatibility**: There are known compatibility notes for Edge and Chrome, especially on macOS. Ensure that Chrome is open if you're using a PWA installed via Chrome, as it might affect functionality <sup>[[5]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/features/pwa.zh-CN.mdx)</sup><sup>[[6]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/usage/features/pwa.mdx)</sup>.

4. **JavaScript Errors**: The `TypeError` related to `document.write()` might be due to deprecated or restricted usage in modern browsers. Consider reviewing the code to replace `document.write()` with safer alternatives like DOM manipulation methods (e.g., `appendChild`, `innerHTML`).

5. **Extensions**: The "Immersive Translate" extension might be causing conflicts. Try disabling it temporarily to see if it resolves the issue.

If these steps do not resolve the problem, further investigation into the specific error messages and the context in which they occur would be necessary.

<!-- Answer -->
在使用 Docker 部署 LobeChat 的 Pglite 模式时，如果遇到“数据库准备”阶段卡住的问题，可以尝试以下步骤进行排查和解决：

1. **检查日志**：使用以下命令查看 Docker 容器的日志，以获取更多错误信息：
   ```bash
   docker logs -f lobe-chat
   ```
   这可以帮助识别是否有任何特定的错误或警告信息。

2. **数据库初始化问题**：Pglite 模式在初始化时可能会遇到依赖加载或数据库迁移的问题。确保所有依赖项正确加载，并且没有迁移错误。

3. **重试初始化**：如果日志中显示初始化错误，可以尝试重新启动容器以重试数据库初始化过程。

4. **检查环境变量**：确保 Docker 容器中设置的环境变量正确无误，特别是与数据库相关的配置。

5. **版本兼容性**：确认使用的 LobeChat 版本与 Docker 镜像的版本兼容，并且没有已知的版本特定问题。

如果问题仍然存在，建议检查是否有任何更新或补丁可以应用，或者查看相关的 GitHub 讨论以获取更多帮助。

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue with the model selection list jumping on mobile devices, specifically in the lobe-chat-database Docker deployment on iOS Safari, is due to an asynchronous configuration loading problem. This happens when configuration variables are not refreshed after the initial configuration pull, causing an abnormal display on first entry and after page refresh. The issue resolves itself after requesting the server configuration again or clicking on any model. A temporary workaround is to modify the default values in the `DEFAULT_LLM_CONFIG` configuration within the `genUserLLMConfig` function. This issue has been addressed in the latest version <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6934)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6464)</sup>.

This import order is necessary for the SDK to function correctly and should prevent the Docker container from failing to start and entering an infinite restart loop. The correct import order is:

import '@anthropic-ai/sdk/shims/web';
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue that addresses the problem of Vercel's 25-second limit on the initial response from Edge Functions. The suggested solution involves leveraging the streaming capabilities of the Lobe Chat framework to ensure that the response starts streaming back to the client before the 25-second limit is reached. Here are the key steps:

1. **Enable Streaming**: Set the `stream` parameter to `true` when making requests to the OpenAI API.

    ```ts
    const response = await openai.chat.completions.create(
      {
        messages: formatMessages,
        ...params,
        stream: true,
      },
      { headers: { Accept: '*/*' } },
    );
    ```

2. **Handle Streaming Responses**: Use the `OpenAIStream` utility to process the streaming response and return it as a `StreamingTextResponse`.

    ```ts
    const stream = OpenAIStream(response);
    return new StreamingTextResponse(stream);
    ```

3. **Frontend Handling**: Ensure that the frontend is set up to handle streaming responses using the `fetchSSE` method.

    ```ts
    export const fetchSSE = async (fetchFn: () => Promise<Response>, options: FetchSSEOptions = {}) => {
      const response = await fetchFn();

      if (!response.ok) {
        const chatMessageError = await getMessageError(response);
        options.onErrorHandle?.(chatMessageError);
        return;
      }

      const returnRes = response.clone();
      const data = response.body;

      if (!data) return;
      const reader = data.getReader();
      const decoder = new TextDecoder();

      let done = false;

      while (!done) {
        const { value, done: doneReading } = await reader.read();
        done = doneReading;
        const chunkValue = decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });

        options.onMessageHandle?.(chunkValue);
      }

      await options?.onFinish?.(output);

      return returnRes;
    };
    ```

By implementing these steps, you can avoid the 504 Gateway Timeout error by ensuring that the response starts streaming back to the client within the 25-second limit <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4046)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
在 lobe-chat 中，音频文件的请求和缓存逻辑主要在 `src/store/file/slices/tts/action.ts` 中实现。`useFetchTTSFile` 函数用于获取 TTS 文件，并可能涉及缓存机制，因为它使用了 SWR（stale-while-revalidate）策略<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/tts/action.ts)</sup>。

如果已经生成的音频文件在再次播放时仍然请求接口重新生成，可能是因为缓存机制没有正确地识别和使用已存在的音频文件。你可以检查以下几点：

1. 确保 `useFetchTTSFile` 函数正确实现了缓存逻辑。
2. 检查是否有配置设置控制音频文件的缓存行为。
3. 确认音频文件的标识符或键是否正确区分了缓存和新请求的音频文件。

如果问题仍然存在，可能需要进一步调试代码，查看是否有错误处理或日志记录来帮助识别问题的根本原因。

body:
<!-- Answer -->
在处理向量化失败的问题时，可以参考以下信息：

1. **常见问题**：向量化失败的一个常见原因是订阅计划限制，特别是 '[EmbeddingError]: SubscriptionPlanLimit'。如果您使用的是最低级别的订阅计划，可能需要提供自己的嵌入 API <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5723)</sup>。

2. **解决方案**：
   - 升级到包含内置向量化功能的更高级别订阅计划。
   - 如果希望保持最低计划，可以部署自己的 LobeChat 数据库版本，并配置自己的嵌入 API <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5723)</sup>。

3. **向量维度不匹配**：如果使用的模型（如 LM-studio 的 text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5）生成的向量维度与 Lobe Chat 期望的维度不匹配（例如 768 vs 1024），可以通过以下 SQL 命令更改 Lobe 数据库中的向量维度：
   ```sql
   alter table embeddings alter column embeddings type vector(768);
   ```
   <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5726)</sup>

4. **数据库迁移问题**：如果遇到 `pgvector` 扩展未找到的错误，确保 PostgreSQL 实例上安装了 `pgvector` 扩展。如果使用 Docker PostgreSQL 镜像，切换到 `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` 镜像。对于云 PostgreSQL 实例，请联系提供商获取帮助 <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/scripts/migrateServerDB/errorHint.js)</sup>。

如果这些方法仍然无法解决问题，建议检查配置文件和环境变量设置，确保所有代理和 API 配置正确无误。

Hey @SSDGADsss, I'm here to help you with bug fixes, answer questions, and guide you on becoming a contributor. Let's squash those bugs together! 🤖

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar unsolved discussion regarding a callback URL mismatch issue in the lobe-chat repository. You can check it out [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4296) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4296)</sup>.

Regarding your issue, it seems that the `direct_url` is indeed related to the `HOSTNAME` and `PORT` environment variables. By setting `HOSTNAME` to your public domain name and `PORT` to 80, you were able to resolve the issue. This suggests that the application might be using these environment variables to construct the `direct_url`, rather than relying solely on the `APP-URL` or HTTP request headers.

To address this, you can ensure that your `HOSTNAME` and `PORT` are correctly set to reflect your public domain and desired port. This should help maintain the correct `direct_url` for SSO logins. If you believe this behavior is a bug, you might consider reporting it to the maintainers for further investigation.

<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar discussion regarding proxy configuration issues with the Gemini model in a Docker environment. The issue was resolved by correcting the proxy settings for the Gemini model <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/1254)</sup>. 

In your case, it seems like the proxy settings in the `.env` file might not be correctly applied to the Gemini API requests. Here are a few steps you can try to troubleshoot and resolve the issue:

1. **Verify Proxy Settings:** Ensure that the proxy settings in your `.env` file are correctly configured and that the proxy server is accessible from within the Docker container. The settings should look like:
   ```
   HTTP_PROXY=http://host.docker.internal:7890
   HTTPS_PROXY=http://host.docker.internal:7890
   ```

2. **Check Docker Network Configuration:** Make sure that the Docker network allows communication through the specified proxy ports. You might need to adjust the Docker network settings or firewall rules.

3. **Test Proxy Connectivity:** From within the Docker container, try using a tool like `curl` to test connectivity through the proxy to the Gemini API. This can help verify if the proxy is functioning as expected.

4. **Review Application Logs:** Check the application logs for any additional error messages or stack traces that might provide more insight into the issue.

5. **Restart Services:** After making changes to the `.env` file, ensure that you restart the Docker services using `docker compose down && docker compose up -d` to apply the changes.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider reviewing the specific error messages in the logs for more detailed troubleshooting.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering is due to the `rejectRequestPattern` parameter, which is currently hardcoded to reject certain file types, including `.cgi` pages. This is causing the browserless service to abort requests to URLs like the one you're trying to access.

To resolve this, you can modify the code to allow the `rejectRequestPattern` to be set via an environment variable. This would provide flexibility to adjust the pattern as needed for different use cases.

Here's a general approach to implement this change:

1. **Modify the Code**: Update the part of the code where `rejectRequestPattern` is defined to check for an environment variable. If the environment variable is set, use its value; otherwise, fall back to the default pattern.

2. **Set Environment Variable**: In your deployment environment (e.g., Docker), set the environment variable with the desired pattern that includes `.cgi` files.

This change would involve editing the code where `rejectRequestPattern` is used, such as in the `browserless` function or related configuration files. Unfortunately, I don't have the exact location of the `crawlSinglePage` function in the codebase, but you can look for where `rejectRequestPattern` is defined and used, such as in the test file `packages/web-crawler/src/crawImpl/__tests__/browserless.test.ts` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/packages/web-crawler/src/crawImpl/__tests__/browserless.test.ts)</sup>.

By making this change, you should be able to customize the request pattern to allow `.cgi` pages and other necessary file types.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
I found a similar closed issue related to image handling: [Bug] 第一条消息附带图片失败, which was resolved by a pull request that fixed images not being included in the chat context. You can view the issue [here](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/3760).

In the current version (1.77.3) of lobe-chat, the function `convertMessageContent` is responsible for handling media files like images. It converts image URLs to base64 strings when necessary, controlled by the environment variable `LLM_VISION_IMAGE_USE_BASE64`. If this variable is set, the image URL is converted to a base64 data URI; otherwise, the URL remains unchanged <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/openaiHelpers.test.ts)</sup>.

Additionally, there are tests in the codebase that verify the correct copying of images in conversations, ensuring that image URLs are correctly parsed and converted <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/ollama/index.test.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/anthropicHelpers.test.ts)</sup>. 

If the issue persists, you might want to check if the environment variable `LLM_VISION_IMAGE_USE_BASE64` is set correctly and ensure that the image URLs are being processed as expected.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with Gemini 2.5 Pro is related to unsupported JSON schema properties like "default" in the request payload. This is a known limitation of the Gemini API, which does not support certain properties, leading to the "Invalid JSON payload received" error.

To resolve this issue, you should:

1. Ensure that the `GOOGLE_API_KEY` environment variable is correctly set in your Docker deployment configuration. This helps in properly configuring the Gemini API key without needing to manually enter the API parameters in settings every time <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5088)</sup>.

2. Disable plugins and function calls in your implementation, as Gemini has limited support for Tools Calling capabilities. The error occurs because the model doesn't support certain JSON schema properties (specifically 'default') in the request payload, which leads to the 400 Bad Request error <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/4994)</sup>.

These steps should help you resolve the error and successfully use Gemini 2.5 Pro in your setup.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The 403 error you're encountering during the deployment on Vercel typically indicates a permissions issue when trying to access the npm registry. Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Check npm Registry Configuration**: Ensure that your `package.json` is correctly configured to use the public npm registry. The `lobe-chat` project specifies the registry as `"https://registry.npmjs.org"` in its `publishConfig` section <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/package.json)</sup>.

2. **Authentication Issues**: If you are using a private npm package or a custom registry, make sure that the necessary authentication tokens are correctly set up in your environment variables or `.npmrc` file.

3. **Network Restrictions**: Verify if there are any network restrictions or firewall settings that might be blocking access to the npm registry. This can sometimes happen in corporate or restricted network environments.

4. **Vercel Environment Variables**: Double-check that all required environment variables are correctly set in your Vercel project settings. Missing or incorrect environment variables can sometimes lead to unexpected errors.

5. **npm Version Compatibility**: Although there are no known compatibility issues with specific npm versions in the `lobe-chat` project, ensure that you are using a compatible version of npm.

6. **Retry the Deployment**: Sometimes, transient network issues can cause 403 errors. Try redeploying your application to see if the issue persists.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider checking the Vercel logs for more detailed error messages or reaching out to Vercel support for further assistance.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
To optimize the regex in the `processWithArtifact` function and prevent excessive whitespace at the end of AI-generated messages, you can ensure that all trailing whitespace is removed from the final output. Here's an optimized version of the function:

```ts
export const processWithArtifact = (input: string = '') => {
  // First remove outer fenced code block if it exists
  let output = input.replace(
    /^([\S\s]*?)\s*```[^\n]*\n((?:<lobeThinking>[\S\s]*?<\/lobeThinking>\s*\n\s*)?<lobeArtifact[\S\s]*?<\/lobeArtifact>\s*)\n```\s*([\S\s]*?)$/,
    (_, before = '', content, after = '') => {
      return [before.trim(), content.trim(), after.trim()].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
    },
  );

  const thinkMatch = ARTIFACT_THINKING_TAG_REGEX.exec(output);

  // If the input contains the `lobeThinking` tag, replace all line breaks with an empty string
  if (thinkMatch) {
    output = output.replace(ARTIFACT_THINKING_TAG_REGEX, (match) =>
      match.replaceAll(/\r?\n|\r/g, ''),
    );
  }

  // Add empty line between lobeThinking and lobeArtifact if they are adjacent
  output = output.replace(/(<\/lobeThinking>)\r?\n(<lobeArtifact)/, '$1\n\n$2');

  // Remove fenced code block between lobeArtifact and HTML content
  output = output.replace(
    /(<lobeArtifact[^>]*>)\s*```[^\n]*\n([\S\s]*?)(```\n)?(<\/lobeArtifact>)/,
    (_, start, content, __, end) => {
      if (content.trim().startsWith('<!DOCTYPE html') || content.trim().startsWith('<html')) {
        return start + content.trim() + end;
      }
      return start + content + (__ || '') + end;
    },
  );

  // Keep existing code blocks that are not part of lobeArtifact
  output = output.replace(
    /^([\S\s]*?)(<lobeThinking>[\S\s]*?<\/lobeThinking>\s*\n\s*<lobeArtifact[\S\s]*?<\/lobeArtifact>)([\S\s]*?)$/,
    (_, before, content, after) => {
      return [before.trim(), content.trim(), after.trim()].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
    },
  );

  const match = ARTIFACT_TAG_REGEX.exec(output);
  // If the input contains the `lobeArtifact` tag, replace all line breaks with an empty string
  if (match) {
    output = output.replace(ARTIFACT_TAG_REGEX, (match) => match.replaceAll(/\r?\n|\r/g, ''));
  }

  // if not match, check if it's start with <lobeArtifact but not closed
  const regex = /<lobeArtifact\b(?:(?!\/?>)[\S\s])*$/;
  if (regex.test(output)) {
    output = output.replace(regex, '<lobeArtifact>');
  }

  // Remove any trailing whitespace from the final output
  output = output.trim();

  return output;
};
```

This version includes a final `trim()` call on the `output` to ensure that any trailing whitespace is removed, which should help prevent excessive whitespace at the end of AI-generated messages <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/components/ChatItem/utils.ts)</sup>.

@tax1drivcer 你好! 我是[Dosu](https://dosu.dev)，一个可以帮助您解决错误、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。我会在等待人类维护者时帮助您。

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're encountering seems to be related to an `EmbeddingError` with codes `22P02` and `22000` in the `vector.c` file. The error occurs during the vectorization process using the Zhipu AI embedding model. Here are some insights that might help:

1. **Dimension Mismatch**: The `CheckExpectedDim` routine in `vector.c` is responsible for ensuring that the dimensions of the vectors match the expected dimensions. An `EmbeddingError` with code `22000` can occur if there is a dimension mismatch, such as when the embedding model produces vectors of a different dimension than expected by the system. For example, if the model produces 768-dimensional vectors but the system expects 1024-dimensional vectors, this error can occur <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5635)</sup>.

2. **Parameter Error**: The error with code `22P02` related to "unnamed portal parameter $2" in the `vector_in` routine suggests there might be an issue with how input parameters are being handled. This could be due to incorrect or missing configuration settings for the embedding model.

To resolve these issues, you might want to:

- Verify the expected dimensions for the embedding model and ensure they match the system's requirements.
- Check the configuration settings for the Zhipu AI embedding model, especially the environment variables and model path, to ensure they are correctly set up.
- Review any recent changes to the configuration or code that might have introduced these errors.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, further investigation into the specific configuration and setup of your Docker environment may be necessary.

I found a similar unsolved discussion regarding document preview issues in Lobe Chat: [Doc文档无法预览](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/5248) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/5248)</sup>.

For your specific issue, it seems that DOCX files are not previewing correctly, while PDF files are working fine. Lobe Chat uses `DocxLoader` for DOCX files and `PdfLoader` for PDF files. Both loaders create a `Blob` from the file content, but the issue might be related to the specific configuration or dependencies for DOCX files <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/langchain/loaders/index.ts)</sup>.

Here are a few things you might want to check:
1. Ensure that all necessary dependencies for `DocxLoader` are included in your Docker setup.
2. Verify if there are any specific configurations or environment variables in your Dockerfile that might affect DOCX file previews.
3. Check if there are any error logs that could provide more insight into why DOCX files fail to preview.

If the issue persists, you might want to explore the repository or related discussions for any updates or patches that address this problem.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue with images disappearing in Lobe Chat is often linked to server-side configuration, particularly with AWS S3 operations. Here are some key configurations to check:

1. **S3 Bucket and Endpoint**: Ensure your S3 bucket and endpoint are correctly set up. The `S3_ENDPOINT` should not include a suffix path, as this can prevent file accessibility.

2. **Public Domain Access**: The `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` must be publicly readable to allow services like OpenAI to access and process images.

3. **S3 Access Keys**: Verify that your `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are correctly configured.

4. **CORS Configuration**: Ensure that your bucket's CORS settings allow cross-origin requests. A typical configuration might look like this:
   ```json
   [
     {
       "AllowedOrigins": ["https://your-project.vercel.app"],
       "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "PUT", "HEAD", "POST", "DELETE"],
       "AllowedHeaders": ["*"]
     }
   ]
   ```

5. **Path-Style Access**: If using a service like MinIO, set `S3_ENABLE_PATH_STYLE=1` to enable path-style access.

These configurations are crucial for the proper handling of image uploads and retrievals. If these settings are correct and the issue persists, consider using the pglite version or waiting for the v2 release, which is expected to address this issue <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/vercel.mdx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database.mdx)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/s3.mdx)</sup>.

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Verify the File Format**: Ensure that the Word document is correctly formatted and not corrupted. You can try opening it in a Word processor to confirm it's intact.

2. **Check File Upload Handling**: Make sure that the file upload process in your deployment is correctly configured to handle Word documents. The system should recognize the .docx format and process it accordingly.

3. **Review Configuration**: Double-check your deployment configuration, especially any settings related to file processing libraries like Unstructured.io, which is used for handling complex document formats in Lobe Chat <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/knowledge-base.mdx)</sup>.

4. **Inspect the Code**: If you have access to the codebase, look for any specific functions or methods that handle file uploads and ensure they are correctly identifying and processing Word documents.

5. **Consult Documentation**: Refer to the Lobe Chat documentation for any specific instructions or known issues related to Word document uploads.

If the issue persists, consider converting the Word document to another format, such as PDF, and see if the problem continues. This can help determine if the issue is specific to the Word format handling.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering indicates that the module 'styled-jsx/package.json' cannot be found, which is causing a JavaScript error in the main process of the Electron application. Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve this issue:

1. **Check Dependencies**: Ensure that 'styled-jsx' is listed as a dependency in the `package.json` file. If it's missing, you may need to add it and run `npm install` or `yarn install` to update your dependencies.

2. **Reinstall Node Modules**: Sometimes, reinstalling the node modules can resolve missing module issues. You can do this by deleting the `node_modules` directory and the `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` file, then running `npm install` or `yarn install` again.

3. **Verify Installation Path**: Make sure that the installation path for the application is correct and that there are no permission issues preventing access to the necessary files.

4. **Check for Compatibility Issues**: There are known compatibility issues with the LobeChat community edition on Windows when using the Edge browser, particularly related to network connectivity. Ensure that your network settings are correct and consider using a VPN if necessary <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5320)</sup>.

5. **Review Electron Setup**: If the issue persists, review the Electron setup and initialization scripts to ensure that all necessary modules are correctly imported and initialized.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to provide more detailed logs or seek further assistance from the development team.

Hello @GaffaSnobb! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), your friendly bot here to help you with bugs, answer questions, and support you in becoming a contributor. I'm here while you wait for a human maintainer. How can I assist you today?

The correct file for the Docker Compose setup is indeed `.env.en_US.example` when the language is set to `en_US`. The documentation specifies that you should download the file `.env.en_US.example` and then rename it to `.env`:

```sh
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/HEAD/docker-compose/local/.env.en_US.example
mv .env.en_US.example .env
```

If you're encountering a 404 error, it might be due to a recent change in the repository that moved or renamed the file. Unfortunately, I couldn't find any specific information about such a change. You might want to check the repository for any recent commits or updates that could have affected the file's location or name <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docker-compose/setup.sh)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose.mdx)</sup>.

你好，@Cheng2001！我是一个可以帮助你解决 bug、回答问题并成为贡献者的机器人。很高兴在这里见到你，我会在你等待人类维护者的同时提供帮助！

<!-- Answer -->
I found some similar discussions and issues that might help with the login problem you're experiencing:

1. In a closed issue, it was noted that the admin account password is no longer the default "123". When downloading the one-click startup script, the newly generated admin account password is output in the terminal. This password should be used instead of the default to log in as the admin <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/5309)</sup>.

2. Another discussion mentioned that after an update, the password might be regenerated, which could be causing the login issue <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/4890)</sup>.

3. An open issue suggested that if the database has not been initialized successfully, it could cause login problems. The recommendation was to rerun the script and choose 'N' when asked whether to initialize the database. After starting, confirm that you can log in, and then clear `init_data.json` <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6924)</sup>.

These insights might help you resolve the login issue by checking if the password has been regenerated or if there are any initialization problems with the database.

<!-- Answer -->
The error "Argument not supported: stream_options" is likely due to the o1 model in LobeChat Docker not supporting streaming with custom proxy endpoints. To resolve this issue, you should:

1. Use OpenAI's official API endpoint instead of a custom proxy endpoint, as the o1 model only supports streaming through the official API.
2. Update your Docker image to the latest version from Docker Hub, as this issue was resolved in version #5183 <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5407)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @Thinkscape! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), your friendly bug-squashing bot here to help you tackle issues, answer questions, and assist you in becoming a contributor. I'm on standby while a human maintainer joins the fun! 🐞

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the image upload button being greyed out, despite selecting a model that supports visual recognition, might be due to the model's capabilities not being correctly recognized by the system. In Lobe Chat, the image upload feature is enabled based on the model's capabilities. If the model does not support visual recognition, the upload button will be disabled <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5963)</sup>.

To resolve this, ensure that the model you have selected is indeed configured to support visual recognition. You can verify this by checking if the model has a `👁️` icon next to its name in the model list, which indicates visual recognition support <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/README.md)</sup>. If the model is correctly configured and the issue persists, there might be a problem with how the model's capabilities are being detected by the system. In such cases, you might need to check the configuration or update the model settings to ensure compatibility.

<!-- Answer -->
The error you're encountering during the Docker build process, specifically the "layer does not exist" error, can be caused by several factors. Here are some steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue:

1. **Docker Cache**: Try clearing the Docker cache by using the `--no-cache` option in your build command. This forces Docker to rebuild the image from scratch without using cached layers:
   ```bash
   docker build --no-cache -t lobe-chat-database-local -f Dockerfile.database --build-arg USE_CN_MIRROR=true .
   ```

2. **Docker System Prune**: Run `docker system prune` to remove unused data, including dangling images and layers, which might be causing the issue:
   ```bash
   docker system prune -a
   ```

3. **Check Dockerfile Syntax**: Ensure that the syntax in your `Dockerfile.database` is correct, especially around the `COPY` command. Verify that the paths specified in the `COPY` command are correct and that the files exist in the expected location in the `builder` stage.

4. **Builder Stage Dependencies**: Make sure that the `builder` stage in your Dockerfile correctly installs and prepares all necessary dependencies, including `drizzle-orm`. If there are any missing dependencies or files, it could lead to the "layer does not exist" error.

5. **Docker Version**: Ensure that your Docker version is up to date, as older versions might have bugs that could cause such errors.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to inspect the Dockerfile further or check for any specific configurations related to the `builder` stage that might be causing the problem.

```
#PROXY-START/
<IfModule mod_proxy.c>

  ProxyRequests Off
    ProxyPreserveHost On
    AllowEncodedSlashes NoDecode 

    ProxyPass / http://127.0.0.1:3210/ nocanon
    ProxyPassReverse / http://127.0.0.1:3210


    </IfModule>
#PROXY-END/
```
I needed `nocanon `because the folder names somehow got decoded since they include symbols.

<!-- Answer -->
To control different features for different user groups using feature flags in LobeChat, you can use the `FEATURE_FLAGS` environment variable. This allows you to enable or disable features by using `+` to add a feature and `-` to disable a feature. You can specify multiple feature flags by separating them with a comma `,` and enclosing the entire value in quotes `"` to avoid parsing errors <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/feature-flags.mdx)</sup>.

For example, to disable the "welcome_suggest" feature, you would set the `FEATURE_FLAGS` variable as follows:

```bash
FEATURE_FLAGS="-welcome_suggest"
```

This configuration lets you customize which features are available to different user groups by setting the appropriate feature flags in the environment variable. Each feature flag is a Boolean value, where `+` enables the feature and `-` disables it <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/feature-flags.mdx)</sup>.

Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific examples or templates for setting up feature flags for different user groups in LobeChat. You might want to explore the [Feature Flags documentation](https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/advanced/feature-flags) for more detailed information on available feature flags and their functionalities <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/feature-flags.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the grok-3 model getting stuck when trying to read a webpage might be related to network request handling or configuration settings in your Docker environment. Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue:

1. **Check Network Configuration**: Ensure that your Docker setup allows outgoing network requests. Sometimes, network restrictions or firewall settings can prevent the model from accessing external web content.

2. **Review Error Handling**: The lobe-chat framework has error handling mechanisms in place for network requests. Check if any errors are being logged when the model attempts to read the webpage. This might give you insights into what is going wrong <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/groq/index.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/utils/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.ts)</sup>.

3. **Update to Latest Version**: Make sure you are using the latest version of the lobe-chat framework and the grok-3 model. Updates often include bug fixes and improvements that might resolve your issue.

4. **Inspect Docker Logs**: Look at the logs generated by your Docker containers to see if there are any error messages or warnings that could indicate the source of the problem.

5. **Test with Different URLs**: Try using the grok-3 model with different URLs to see if the issue is specific to certain webpages.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, you might need to delve deeper into the specific configurations or consider reaching out to the community for more targeted support.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @deeeiznc! I'm here to help you with any bugs or questions you might have as you wait for a human maintainer. Feel free to ask me anything!

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issues you're experiencing with Lobe Chat, here are some suggestions:

1. **Streaming and Non-Streaming Toggle**: Implementing a global toggle for streaming and non-streaming requests can be beneficial. This would allow users to choose their preferred request type unless the model itself imposes restrictions. Additionally, adding a toggle for streaming output at the conversation level can provide more flexibility for temporary configurations. Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific steps for adding such toggles in the UI within the repository, but this feature could be considered for future updates.

2. **Handling Long Response Times**: If the Google series models in the uni-api are taking too long to respond, resulting in errors, consider deploying Lobe Chat using Docker instead of Vercel. Docker does not have the timeout limitations that Vercel does, which can help prevent interruptions during long inference processes <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6226)</sup>.

3. **Synchronizing Configurations**: Synchronizing configurations between third-party Custom AI Providers and official models is a feature that users have requested. However, I couldn't find specific information on how Lobe Chat currently handles this synchronization. It might be worth exploring this feature in future updates to ensure that third-party models can support functionalities similar to official models.

These suggestions aim to improve the flexibility and reliability of Lobe Chat when dealing with different AI models and configurations.

To resolve this issue, you might want to explore alternative data import methods provided by the codebase, such as the `importData` method, which is functional and used for importing various types of data <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/services/import/type.ts)</sup>.

To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the `showCitations` prop is not directly passed to a DOM element. Instead, it should be used within a React component where it can be handled appropriately. Here's what you can do:

1. **Check the `ChatItem` Component**: Ensure that the `showCitations` prop is not being directly applied to a native HTML element. It should be used within the logic of the component, possibly affecting rendering decisions or passed to other React components that understand this prop.

2. **Modify the Prop Usage**: If `showCitations` is being passed to a native element, consider using it to conditionally render parts of the component or pass it to a child component that can handle it correctly.

3. **Review the Component Logic**: Look at the logic around line 230 in `src/features/Conversation/components/ChatItem/index.tsx` to see how `showCitations` is being used. Ensure that it is not being spread onto a DOM element.

Additionally, the general hydration error indicating a mismatch between server-rendered and client-rendered HTML could be due to differences in the rendering logic between server and client. Check for:

- **Consistent Logic**: Ensure that any logic affecting rendering is consistent between server and client. Avoid using non-deterministic functions like `Date.now()` or `Math.random()` during rendering.

- **Data Consistency**: Make sure that any data used during rendering is the same on both server and client.

- **HTML Structure**: Verify that the HTML structure is valid and consistent between server and client.

By addressing these points, you should be able to resolve the hydration issues you're facing.

body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @creatorofuniverses! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), here to help you solve bugs, answer questions, and contribute to your experience while you wait for a human maintainer. How can I assist you today?

<!-- Answer -->
Lobe-chat processes files through several steps before sending them to the model, which might affect the quality of the model's response. Here's a brief overview of the process:

1. **File Hashing and Existence Check**: The file is hashed to check if it already exists in the system. If it does, the existing metadata is used <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/upload/action.ts)</sup>.

2. **File Upload and Type Detection**: If the file is new, it is uploaded, and its type is detected using a powerful file type detector <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/upload/action.ts)</sup>.

3. **Database Entry**: The file's metadata, including type, hash, name, size, and URL, is stored in the database <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/upload/action.ts)</sup>.

4. **File Processing**: After uploading, the file undergoes additional processing steps such as chunking and embedding, which are crucial for preparing the data for model usage <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/file/slices/upload/action.ts)</sup>.

The issue you're experiencing might be related to how the file is processed and represented before being sent to the model. Unfortunately, specific details on chunking, embedding, or vector representation optimizations in lobe-chat are not available in the current documentation. This could be a factor in the discrepancies you're observing between lobe-chat and the original model provider services.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @YYplus! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), a helpful bot here to assist you with bugs, questions, and contributing to the project. I'm ready to help while you wait for a human maintainer!

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issue of not being able to retrieve the "DeepSeek-V3-0324" model after the old "DeepSeek-V3" model was removed, you can update the model list in the lobe-chat framework. Here's how you can do it:

1. **Clear existing models for the DeepSeek provider:**

   Use the `clearModelsByProvider` method to remove all models associated with the DeepSeek provider.

   ```javascript
   await aiModelModel.clearModelsByProvider(deepSeekProviderId);
   ```

2. **Batch update with new models:**

   Use the `batchUpdateAiModels` method to add or update the models provided by the DeepSeek service.

   ```javascript
   await aiModelModel.batchUpdateAiModels(deepSeekProviderId, newModels);
   ```

   Ensure that `newModels` includes the updated model "DeepSeek-V3-0324".

This process will help you update the model list to reflect the changes made by the AI service provider <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/database/models/aiModel.ts)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/utils/parseModels.ts)</sup><sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/store/user/slices/modelList/action.ts)</sup>.

要在桌面应用中启用 SearchXNG 搜索引擎的联网搜索功能，需要设置环境变量 `SEARXNG_URL` 来指定 SearchXNG 实例的 URL。可以通过以下步骤在 macOS 上进行配置：

1. 打开终端。
2. 输入以下命令来设置环境变量（将 `https://searxng-instance.com` 替换为你的 SearchXNG 实例 URL）：
   ```bash
   export SEARXNG_URL=https://searxng-instance.com
   ```
3. 确保你的 SearchXNG 实例已配置为支持 `json` 输出。可以通过修改 `searxng/settings.yml` 文件来启用：
   ```yaml
   search:
     formats:
       - html
       - json
   ```
4. 重启 SearXNG 容器以应用更改。

完成这些步骤后，重新启动 LobeChat 服务，并尝试进行联网搜索。如果配置正确，AI 应该能够提供最新的信息<sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6482)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/advanced/online-search.mdx)</sup>.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
You can resolve the issue of the `SEARCH1API_API_KEY` automatically enabling the AI model provider by using a separate environment variable specifically for crawling. The lobe-chat codebase allows for the use of `SEARCH1API_CRAWL_API_KEY` for crawling purposes. If you set `SEARCH1API_CRAWL_API_KEY`, it will be used instead of `SEARCH1API_API_KEY`, thus preventing the automatic activation of the AI model provider for all users <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/packages/web-crawler/src/crawImpl/search1api.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the default model setting not taking effect and the model list not updating properly might be related to a known bug in Lobe Chat v1.15.16, where Docker environment variables were not taking effect correctly. This issue was resolved in version 1.52.1. Upgrading your Lobe Chat installation to version 1.52.1 or later should address these problems <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5881)</sup>.

Additionally, ensure that your environment variables are correctly formatted. For example, the `SYSTEM_AGENT` variable should be set using the format `default=provider/model`, which you have done correctly. If the issue persists after upgrading, double-check the configuration and consider restarting the application to ensure all changes are applied <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/basic.mdx)</sup>.

Given that you're using version 1.79.7, it's possible that this issue has resurfaced or is related to a different underlying problem. You might want to check if there are any recent updates or patches that address similar issues in the newer versions. docker pull lobehub/lobe-chat:latest

After pulling the latest image, restart your Docker container to apply the update. body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @nekomiya-hinata! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), your friendly bot here to help you with bugs, answer questions, and guide you in becoming a contributor. I'm here to assist while we wait for a human maintainer. How can I help you today?

<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing with the image upload button being disabled for the Claude 3.7 Sonnet model is likely due to the `vision` property not being set to `true` in the `src/config/modelProviders/anthropic.ts` file for this model. This property is crucial for enabling the image upload functionality, as it determines whether a model supports vision capabilities <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5963)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/useModelSupportVision.ts)</sup>.

To resolve this, you should ensure that the `vision: true` property is added for the Claude 3.7 Sonnet model in the `anthropic.ts` configuration file. This should enable the image upload button for this model, similar to how it works for Claude 3.5 Sonnet <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/hooks/useModelSupportVision.ts)</sup>.

Regarding the "extended thinking" toggle, it seems that this feature might not be configured for custom service providers in the same way as it is for built-in providers. You may need to check the configuration settings for custom providers to ensure they support this feature, or it might require additional implementation to match the built-in provider capabilities. Unfortunately, specific details on configuring this feature for custom providers are not available in the current context.

The issue you're experiencing with the mobile styling in version 1.79.7 of Lobe Chat, where the page can be scrolled infinitely, might be related to changes in the mobile layout components or CSS styles. Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific information about changes in version 1.79.7 that could affect mobile styling or layout. However, here are some areas you might want to investigate:

1. **Mobile Layout Components**: Check the `MobileContentLayout` and `Mobile.tsx` files for any recent changes that might affect the mobile view. These components manage the mobile layout and styling logic <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/[variants]/(main)/chat/(workspace)/_layout/Mobile/index.tsx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/app/[variants]/(main)/chat/(workspace)/@portal/_layout/Mobile.tsx)</sup>.

2. **CSS Styles**: Look for any CSS changes that might have been introduced in version 1.79.7. These could potentially affect how elements are displayed on mobile devices.

3. **Conditional Logic**: Review any conditional logic in the mobile layout components that might cause issues on specific devices or browsers. The `useIsMobile` hook, for example, determines the mobile state and could be affected by recent changes <sup>[[3]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/Conversation/Messages/Assistant/FileChunks/Item/index.tsx)</sup>.

4. **Docker Configuration**: Although there is no specific information about Docker affecting mobile styling, ensure that your Docker setup is consistent with previous versions to rule out any deployment-related issues.

Since the problem did not occur in previous versions, comparing the code and configuration between the versions might help identify the cause. If possible, you could also try reverting to an earlier version to see if the issue persists.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @Thelast0802! 👋 I'm here to assist you with any bugs, questions, or contributions you might have while you wait for a human maintainer. Let's tackle this together! 😊

<!-- Answer -->
要在 Mac 上使用 Docker 部署 LobeChat 并配置一个默认的 AI 模型服务商，使所有用户都能默认使用该模型，您可以在 `.env` 文件中使用 `SYSTEM_AGENT` 和 `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` 环境变量。这样可以确保默认配置适用于所有用户，无需每个账户单独设置模型 API。

例如，要将 DeepSeek AI 设置为默认模型服务商，您可以在 `.env` 文件中添加以下内容：

```plaintext
SYSTEM_AGENT=DeepSeek
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your_deepseek_api_key
DEEPSEEK_PROXY_URL=your_custom_proxy_url (optional)
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG=provider=deepseek/model=deepseek-model
```

这些设置将自动应用于所有用户。有关更多详细信息，您可以参考文档：[self-hosting/environment-variables/basic](https://lobehub.com/zh/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/basic#default-agent-config) <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/5805)</sup>.

### Adding Non-Stream Output Capability to Gemini Provider ✅

Successfully implemented non-stream output capability for the Gemini provider to help resolve stream parsing errors.

#### Completed Tasks:
- [x] Read repository structure and guidelines
- [x] Explore current Gemini provider implementation
- [x] Understand model-runtime architecture for non-stream support

#### Summary of Changes:

**New Features:**
- ✨ Added support for both streaming and non-streaming modes in Gemini provider
- 🔄 Check `payload.stream` flag to determine which mode to use
- 📡 Use `generateContent` for non-streaming vs `generateContentStream` for streaming
- 🔧 Transform non-streaming response to stream format for compatibility
- 🐛 Enhanced error logging for stream debugging as requested in the original issue

**Key Implementation Details:**
- Modified the `chat` method in `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/google/index.ts`
- Added `transformGoogleResponseToStream` method to convert non-streaming responses
- Enhanced error logging with detailed stack traces and error messages
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing streaming functionality

**Benefits:**
- Reduces stream parsing errors by providing non-streaming alternative
- Better debugging capabilities with enhanced error logging  
- Fallback option when streaming mode encounters issues
- Addresses the core issue raised about Gemini stream interruption problems

**Usage:**
Users can now set `stream: false` in their payload to use non-streaming mode for Gemini models, which should help avoid the stream parsing errors mentioned in the issue.

I'll help add non-stream output capability to the Gemini provider to address the stream parsing errors mentioned in this issue.

### Todo List
- [x] Analyze codebase structure for Gemini provider
- [x] Locate current Gemini implementation
- [x] Add non-stream chat completion method
- [x] Update types and configurations if needed
- [x] Test the implementation
- [x] Commit and push changes
- [x] Create pull request

### ✅ Implementation Complete

I've successfully implemented non-streaming support for the Gemini provider to address the stream parsing errors mentioned in this issue.

**Key Changes Made:**

1. **Modified `chat()` method** in `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/google/index.ts`:
   - Added logic to check the `stream` property in the payload
   - When `stream` is `false`, uses Google's `generateContent()` instead of `generateContentStream()`
   - Maintains backward compatibility - streaming remains the default behavior

2. **Added `transformGoogleResponseToStream()` method**:
   - Converts non-streaming Google responses to streaming format for API compatibility
   - Handles thinking content, function calls, usage metadata, and all Gemini features
   - Ensures consistent response format across streaming and non-streaming modes

3. **Enhanced test coverage**:
   - Added test case for non-streaming functionality
   - Verifies that `generateContent()` is called when `stream: false`
   - Maintains existing test coverage for streaming mode

**How Users Can Use This:**

When experiencing stream parsing errors with Gemini, users can now set `stream: false` in their request payload to use the reliable non-streaming mode:

```javascript
const response = await geminiProvider.chat({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }],
  model: 'gemini-2.0-flash',
  stream: false, // Use non-streaming mode
  temperature: 0.7
});
```

**Benefits:**
- ✅ Provides reliable fallback when streaming fails
- ✅ Maintains full feature compatibility (thinking, function calls, multimodal)
- ✅ Zero breaking changes - streaming remains default
- ✅ Addresses the core issue raised in this GitHub issue

4. **Update Dependencies**: Ensure that all dependencies, especially those related to date handling (like `dayjs`), are up to date. This can sometimes resolve unexpected behavior due to bugs in older versions.

By addressing these areas, you should be able to resolve the `TypeError` and ensure that all data, including branches in the `threads` table, is imported correctly.

I found a similar closed issue that might help you resolve the problem with the Casdoor webhook not triggering any response in LobeChat after changing the avatar <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/6130)</sup>. Here are some steps you can follow:

1. **Webhook URL Configuration**: Ensure the webhook URL is set to `http://lobe.example.com/api/webhooks/casdoor` (not `/api/auth/webhooks/casdoor`).

2. **Environment Variables**: Verify that the `CASDOOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable is correctly set in your `.env` file. The secret must match the `casdoor-secret` header in the incoming request.

3. **Version**: Use LobeChat version 1.61.6 or later <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions/6232)</sup>.

4. **MinIO Configuration**: Ensure MinIO is properly configured for avatar storage. Check your MinIO settings according to the official documentation at [LobeHub Docs](https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/server-database/docker-compose#using-min-io). Make sure the `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` and `S3_ENDPOINT` environment variables are correctly set.

5. **User Session**: After changing the avatar, users may need to log out and log back in or refresh their browser cache to see the updates.

6. **Reverse Proxy Configuration**: Check your reverse proxy settings to ensure it does not intercept Casdoor's OAuth2 configuration requests. Verify by accessing `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration` to ensure it returns the correct JSON data.

These steps should help you troubleshoot and resolve the issue with the webhook not responding.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The 404 errors for JavaScript files in your Cloud Run deployment of the lobe-chat application could be due to incorrect base path configuration. To resolve this issue, ensure that the `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` environment variable is correctly set. This variable is used to define the base path for the application, which is crucial for correctly loading JavaScript files and other assets.

Here are some steps you can take to address the issue:

1. **Check Environment Variables**: Ensure that the `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` is set correctly in your environment variables. This should match the path where your application is hosted. For example, if your application is hosted at `https://chat.example.com`, the base path should be set accordingly.

2. **Verify Terraform Configuration**: In your Terraform script, ensure that the `APP_URL` environment variable is set correctly. This should reflect the actual URL where your application is accessible.

3. **Review Cloud Run Settings**: Double-check the Cloud Run service settings to ensure that the deployment is configured to serve files from the correct paths. This includes verifying the `basePath` configuration if applicable.

4. **Check Deployment Logs**: Review the Cloud Run logs for any additional errors or warnings that might provide more context on why the JavaScript files are not being found.

By ensuring that the base path and related configurations are correctly set, you should be able to resolve the 404 errors and successfully load the JavaScript files.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
Lobe does not currently have a documented method for automatically selecting an available embedding model from the API URL. If you leave the `DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG` blank, the `parseFilesConfig` function will return the default configuration specified by `DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG` <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/server/globalConfig/parseFilesConfig.ts)</sup>. 

The default settings include:

- `embeddingModel`: Uses the default embedding model and provider specified by `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`.
- `queryMode`: Uses the default rerank query mode specified by `DEFAULT_RERANK_QUERY_MODE`.
- `rerankerModel`: Uses the default rerank model and provider specified by `DEFAULT_RERANK_MODEL` and `DEFAULT_RERANK_PROVIDER` <sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/const/settings/knowledge.ts)</sup>.

The build failure you're experiencing seems to be related to several issues:

1. **Service Worker Registration**: Warnings about service worker registration might indicate issues with how the service worker is being implemented or registered. This could affect caching and offline capabilities.

2. **Serialization Performance**: Warnings about serialization performance might suggest inefficiencies in how data is being serialized, which could impact performance.

3. **Large Files Not Being Precached**: This issue could be due to configuration settings in the service worker or build process that limit the size of files that can be cached.

4. **"self is not defined" Error**: This error typically occurs when the `self` variable is used in a context where it is not defined, such as server-side code where `self` is not available. This might require checking the code for any client-side constructs being used on the server.

5. **ELIFECYCLE Command Failure**: This is a common error in Node.js projects that indicates a script failed to execute properly. It could be due to the issues mentioned above or other underlying problems in the build script.

To address these issues, you might need to:

- Review the service worker registration and ensure it is correctly implemented.
- Optimize serialization processes to improve performance.
- Adjust caching strategies to handle large files appropriately.
- Check the server-side code for any incorrect usage of client-side variables like `self`.
- Investigate the build scripts and logs for more specific errors related to the ELIFECYCLE failure.

Unfortunately, I couldn't find specific solutions for these issues in the lobe-chat repository, but these general steps might help you troubleshoot the problem.

The Lobe Chat documentation does not currently provide specific examples for configuring LM Studio environment variables. However, you can try using a similar approach to other model providers. Here are some steps and considerations:

1. **Enable LM Studio**: Set `ENABLED_LM_STUDIO=1` to enable LM Studio as a provider.

2. **Set Proxy URL**: Use `LM_STUDIO_PROXY_URL` to specify the API service address. Ensure the URL is correctly formatted and accessible.

3. **Define Model List**: Use `LM_STUDIO_MODEL_LIST` to list the models you want to use, separated by commas if there are multiple models.

4. **Check Configuration**: Ensure that the syntax aligns with examples provided for other models in the documentation. Double-check for any typos or incorrect values.

5. **Troubleshooting**: If the configuration does not take effect, verify that the environment variables are correctly set and that there are no connectivity issues, such as mismatched protocols or CORS policies.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, it might be helpful to check for any updates or additional guidance in the Lobe Chat community or documentation.

The issue you're experiencing might be related to the configuration settings for enabling web search in the o3 component of the lobe-chat framework. Ensure that the configuration settings are correctly defined in the `handlePayload` function within the `chatCompletion` object. The settings should look like this:

```javascript
web_search: {
  enable: true,
  enable_citation: true,
  enable_trace: true,
}
```

These settings are applied when the `enabledSearch` property is true in the payload. You can find these settings in the `src/libs/agent-runtime/wenxin/index.ts` file of the lobe-chat framework <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/wenxin/index.ts)</sup>.

If the configuration is correct and the issue persists, it might be related to permissions or roles required for your organization to access the web search feature. Unfortunately, specific permissions or roles required are not documented in the available information. You might want to double-check your API configuration and ensure that all necessary permissions are granted.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
The issue you're experiencing might be related to the configuration settings for enabling web search in the o3 component of the lobe-chat framework. Ensure that the configuration settings are correctly defined in the `handlePayload` function within the `chatCompletion` object. The settings should look like this:

```javascript
web_search: {
  enable: true,
  enable_citation: true,
  enable_trace: true,
}
```

These settings are applied when the `enabledSearch` property is true in the payload. You can find these settings in the `src/libs/agent-runtime/wenxin/index.ts` file of the lobe-chat framework <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/agent-runtime/wenxin/index.ts)</sup>.

If the configuration is correct and the issue persists, it might be related to permissions or roles required for your organization to access the web search feature. Unfortunately, specific permissions or roles required are not documented in the available information. You might want to double-check your API configuration and ensure that all necessary permissions are granted.

body:
<!-- Answer -->
This issue with the Lobe Chat application (version v1.80.4) is a known problem related to Zitadel authentication. The error message "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')" occurs intermittently and is linked to the authentication flow. This issue has been reported and discussed in the repository <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/7312)</sup>.

The problem seems to arise without any server-side changes, indicating a potential bug in the client-side code handling the authentication process. It has been noted since version v1.77, and the error occurs particularly after logging in, making it difficult to consistently reproduce <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/7312)</sup>.

If you are looking for a solution, you might want to check if there have been any updates or patches released after version v1.80.4 that address this issue. Additionally, reviewing the client-side code related to authentication might help identify and fix the bug.

用AI问了下，回答是`在 LobeChat 中，当聊天请求超过 60 秒（1分钟）没有收到上游消息时，会报错 504 超时错误。
这个超时限制是由 Next.js 的 API 路由默认超时设置决定的，而不是 LobeChat 代码中明确设置的。在 LobeChat 的聊天服务实现中，当使用 fetchSSE 函数发送请求到上游 AI 服务提供商时，如果上游服务超过 60 秒没有响应，Next.js 服务器会自动中断连接并返回 504 Gateway Timeout 错误。
在 LobeChat 代码中没有明确设置超时时间的地方，它依赖于 Next.js 的默认设置。如果你需要修改这个超时限制，需要在 Next.js 配置中进行调整，而不是在 LobeChat 的代码中直接修改。`

This timeout limit is determined by the default timeout setting of Next.js' API routing, rather than explicitly set in the LobeChat code. In LobeChat's chat service implementation, when using the fetchSSE function to send a request to the upstream AI service provider, if the upstream service does not respond for more than 60 seconds, the Next.js server will automatically interrupt the connection and return a 504 Gateway Timeout error.
There is no explicit place to set the timeout in the LobeChat code, it depends on the default settings of Next.js. If you need to modify this timeout limit, you need to adjust it in the Next.js configuration instead of directly modifying it in the LobeChat code. `

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @bsq1989! I'm here to help you solve bugs, answer questions, and assist you in becoming a contributor. While you wait for a human maintainer, feel free to let me know how I can assist you!

<!-- Answer -->
To address the issue of handling large Excel tables in the RAG process without exceeding the embedding model's input limit, you can implement a chunking strategy that ensures the data is divided into manageable parts. Here's a refined approach based on your modification:

1. **Chunking Strategy**: Implement a condition to check the length of the text in the table elements. If the text length is below a certain threshold (e.g., 5000 characters), you can process it as a single element. Otherwise, apply a chunking strategy to split the data into smaller parts.

2. **Handling Large Tables**: For large tables, ensure that the data is split into chunks that do not exceed the model's token limit. This prevents vectorization failures due to input size constraints.

3. **Storing and Querying Origin Elements**: Ensure that `originElements` are correctly stored and can be queried during the RAG process. This involves appending decompressed elements to `originElements` and ensuring they are accessible for subsequent processing.

Here's a code snippet reflecting these changes:

```typescript
// Step 1: Decode the Base64 encoded string to binary
const binaryBuffer = Buffer.from(base64EncodedString, 'base64');

// Step 2: Decompress the binary data
const elements = await this.decompressGzip(binaryBuffer);

// Check if the table element should be merged or split
const merge_Flag = element.type === 'Table' && elements[0].text.length < 5000;

if (merge_Flag) {
  if (element.metadata.is_continuation) {
    return;
  }

  compositeElements = [...compositeElements, elements[0]];
  originElements = [...originElements, elements[0]];
  return;
}

// For larger elements, handle them appropriately
compositeElements = [...compositeElements, element];
originElements = originElements.concat(
  elements.map(
    (e) => ({ ...e, compositeId: element.element_id }) as UnstructuredPartitionElement,
  ),
);
```

This approach ensures that large tables are split into smaller chunks, preventing issues with the embedding model's input limits, and maintains the integrity of the `originElements` for querying during the RAG process <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/libs/unstructured/index.ts)</sup>.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hello @zhou-zeyun! I'm [Dosu](https://dosu.dev), your friendly bot here to help with bugs, answer questions, and assist you in becoming a contributor. I'm here to help you while you wait for a human maintainer. How can I assist you today?

<!-- Answer -->
To enable the "Limit historical message count" feature in the official cloud version v1.81.2 using the lobe-chat-database image, you need to ensure that the toggle switch is turned on. This can be done by setting the `enableHistoryCount` state to `true` in the `History` component. You can achieve this by setting the `checked` property of the `Switch` component to `true` and updating the agent configuration with `updateAgentConfig({ enableHistoryCount: true })`. Here is the relevant code snippet:

```jsx
<Switch
  checked={enableHistoryCount}
  onChange={(enableHistoryCount) => {
    updateAgentConfig({ enableHistoryCount });
  }}
  size={'small'}
/>
```

Additionally, make sure that the environment variable `chatConfig.enableHistoryCount=true` is set. You can also specify the number of messages to retain by setting the `historyCount` parameter. For example, setting `historyCount=2` will retain the last two messages <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/History.tsx)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/basic.mdx)</sup>.

<!-- Answer -->
要解决在构建 Docker 镜像时出现的 TypeScript 错误 "Cannot find module '@mozilla/readability' or its corresponding type declarations"，可以按照以下步骤进行处理：

1. **检查现有的类型定义**：首先，尝试安装 `@mozilla/readability` 的类型定义包：
   ```bash
   npm install @types/mozilla__readability
   ```
   如果该包不存在，请继续下一步。

2. **创建自定义类型声明文件**：如果没有可用的类型定义，可以创建一个自定义类型声明文件。在项目中创建一个名为 `readability.d.ts` 的文件，通常放在 `types` 目录中，并添加以下内容：
   ```typescript
   declare module '@mozilla/readability' {
     export class Readability {
       constructor(document: Document);
       parse(): { [key: string]: any };
     }
   }
   ```

3. **包含类型声明文件**：确保 TypeScript 能识别你的自定义类型声明文件，在 `tsconfig.json` 中添加以下配置：
   ```json
   {
     "compilerOptions": {
       "typeRoots": ["./types", "./node_modules/@types"]
     }
   }
   ```

通过这些步骤，你应该能够解决在构建 Docker 镜像时遇到的 TypeScript 错误 <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/blob/main/packages/web-crawler/package.json)</sup>。

<!-- Answer -->
To resolve the "Unsupported parameter: 'top_p' is not supported with this model" error when using Azure OpenAI's o-series models, you need to remove the unsupported parameters from your API request. Specifically, for models like o1-mini, o1, o3-mini, o4-mini, and others in the o-series, the parameters `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `temperature`, and `top_p` are not supported. Make sure these parameters are not included in your request to avoid the error <sup>[[1]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/7479)</sup><sup>[[2]](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues/7127)</sup>.
